name: Long-only short-horizon mean reversion (RSI(2)/IBS)
mechanism: Buy after a short-term oversold reading (RSI(2)<10 or IBS<0.2) with price above its 200-day MA; exit on a bounce above the 5-day MA, IBS>0.8, or a 10-day time stop.
ruled_out_reason: Excluded at pre-screen: the expected edge of this short-horizon mean-reversion spec was too thin relative to the trading cost it must clear.
source: Pre-screen of strategy alternatives (not a mining target)

name: Dual momentum / tactical asset allocation / trend
mechanism: Rotate into the strongest-momentum asset class or exit to cash/bonds on a trend-following signal across a multi-asset universe.
ruled_out_reason: Excluded at pre-screen: its trend exposure duplicates a leveraged-ETF trend rotation already studied in this project.
source: Pre-screen of strategy alternatives (not a mining target)

name: Gayed 200-day MA LETF rotation
mechanism: Rotate leveraged-ETF exposure on/off based on price vs. its 200-day moving average.
ruled_out_reason: Excluded at pre-screen: same trend-duplication reason as dual_momentum_taa_trend.
source: Pre-screen of strategy alternatives (not a mining target)

name: Turn-of-month effect
mechanism: Hold equities only around calendar month-end/month-start sessions, flat otherwise.
ruled_out_reason: Real effect but too small in absolute terms to be worth trading -- excluded on materiality, not on mechanism, so re-testing would not change it.
source: Pre-screen of strategy alternatives (not a mining target)

name: Pre-FOMC announcement drift
mechanism: Hold equities only in the ~24h window before scheduled FOMC announcements.
ruled_out_reason: Peer-reviewed literature (Kurov et al.) documents the effect's disappearance, outweighing one 2024-inclusive blog backtest; also only about eight events per year, too few to verify at this scale.
source: Pre-screen of strategy alternatives (not a mining target)

name: Opening Range Breakout, 5-min QQQ/TQQQ
mechanism: Enter on first-5-minute-bar directional breakout at 9:35 ET, stop at the bar's extreme, exit at the close.
ruled_out_reason: Feed-fragile by the authors' own multi-provider study, and dependent on intraday data of a specific provenance.
source: Pre-screen of strategy alternatives (not a mining target)

name: 9-Sig TQQQ value averaging
mechanism: Quarterly value-averaging rebalance targeting a 9%/quarter growth path in TQQQ, funded/drained by a bond sleeve.
ruled_out_reason: Fails survival: drawdowns of a 3x value-averaging book are too deep to survive.
source: Pre-screen of strategy alternatives (not a mining target)

name: Overnight drift (buy close, sell open)
mechanism: Buy at the close, sell at the next open, capturing the overnight-vs-intraday return anomaly.
ruled_out_reason: Dominated by buy-and-hold in recent windows, the underlying anomaly's edge decayed 2020-2022, and 3x overnight exposure carries uncapped gap-down risk.
source: Pre-screen of strategy alternatives (not a mining target)

name: Tiny Titans micro-cap momentum
mechanism: Hold a rotating basket of the smallest-cap, highest-momentum micro-cap stocks.
ruled_out_reason: Micro-cap bid-ask spreads at 100%+ annual turnover impose trading costs large enough to consume a thin edge.
source: Pre-screen of strategy alternatives (not a mining target)

name: Options wheel (CSP/covered call), single names
mechanism: Sell cash-secured puts and covered calls on individual equities to harvest premium.
ruled_out_reason: Index-level put-write evidence needs large collateral per contract; a single-name substitute is a concentrated stock bet, not a diversified premium harvest.
source: Pre-screen of strategy alternatives (not a mining target)

name: Long-option shapes (0DTE momentum calls / tail puts)
mechanism: Buy short-dated options for directional or tail-risk exposure.
ruled_out_reason: Documented negative expectancy for option buyers as a class.
source: Pre-screen of strategy alternatives (not a mining target)

name: Stocks-in-Play Opening Range Breakout
mechanism: ORB entries on high-relative-volume 'stocks in play' rather than a fixed index ETF.
ruled_out_reason: The published backtest assumes zero slippage on wide-spread names, where realistic spreads consume a thin intraday edge.
source: Pre-screen of strategy alternatives (not a mining target)

name: Post-earnings-announcement drift (PEAD)
mechanism: Single-stock reformulation of the cross-sectional PEAD signal (the literature's SUE-decile ranking across a broad screened universe does not reduce to one ticker's OHLC, which is all this engine's run_backtest/fetch_ohlc can consume -- see REFORMULATION NOTE). On each of JNJ's real historical quarterly earnings-announcement dates (fetched via yfinance's Ticker.get_earnings_dates(), which returns actual Earnings Date/EPS Estimate/Reported EPS/Surprise% history -- not synthetic or invented dates), compute JNJ's realized same-day return (announcement-day close vs. prior close); if that return exceeds +1 standard deviation of JNJ's own trailing 60-trading-day daily return (a volatility-relative definition of an 'unusually large' positive reaction, chosen to avoid an arbitrary flat percentage or an invented 'typical surprise' figure), enter long at the next trading session's open and hold for hold_days trading days, exiting via time stop.

parameters.earnings_date_source: yfinance Ticker.get_earnings_dates() -- earnings dates with EPS estimate, reported EPS and surprise history; it needs the lxml package, so an implementation must fetch earnings dates in an environment that has lxml, separately from the OHLC fetch, which stays in data_pipeline.fetch_ohlc.

source: Bernard, V.L. & Thomas, J.K. (1989), "Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Delayed Price Response or Risk Premium?", Journal of Accounting Research 27, 1-36. https://ideas.repec.org/a/bla/joares/v27y1989ip1-36.html (verified via web search 2026-08-29). REFORMULATION NOTE: reformulated around blue-chip single stocks so that real tickers can be used to test the strategy. No PEAD-specific ETF exists (verified via web search 2026-08-29) -- the academic version cross-sectionally ranks a broad universe by standardized earnings surprise and buys the top decile, which cannot reduce to one ticker's OHLC. Reformulated as a genuine single-stock test on Johnson & Johnson (JNJ): NYSE blue chip, Dow Jones Industrial Average component, Dividend King (60+ consecutive years of dividend increases), 16,273 daily bars back to 1962-01-02 in yfinance (verified live 2026-08-29), ~7.9M shares/day average volume over the trailing 60 sessions (verified live 2026-08-29) -- long-tenured, highly liquid, consistently profitable, real quarterly earnings cadence. This is a REAL earnings-date-anchored single-stock signal, not a price-only proxy: it uses JNJ's actual announcement calendar (see parameters.earnings_date_source) to identify which trading days are earnings days, then a volatility-relative same-day-return threshold (not an invented flat percentage or a guessed 'typical surprise' number) to flag which of those real earnings days counts as a sufficiently large positive reaction. A future real gate on any survivor would need to (a) wire earnings-date fetching into the pipeline's execution environment (see parameters.earnings_date_source) and (b) decide whether this single-name test is sufficient evidence or whether the original cross-sectional SUE-decile sort needs separate validation on a broader universe.

name: 52-week-high proximity momentum
mechanism: Rank equities/ETFs by nearness of current price to trailing 52-week high; buy the closest-to-high decile and hold with periodic rebalance. Nearness-to-high is documented to subsume and outperform standard past-return momentum as a forecasting signal.
source: George, T.J. & Hwang, C.-Y. (2004), "The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing", Journal of Finance 59(5), 2145-2176. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1540-6261.2004.00695.x (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Distinct mechanism (proximity-to-high, cross-sectional single-name ranking) from any trend/momentum entry above. PROXY NOTE: tested via MTUM (iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF, real/verified via web search 2026-08-29) as a real, tradeable stand-in -- MTUM's methodology is broad price momentum, not literally '52-week-high proximity', so this measures a real momentum product's behavior, not a direct replication of George & Hwang's specific ranking variable. A future real gate on any survivor would need to decide whether the ETF-proxy result is sufficient or whether the literal 52-week-high-proximity ranking needs separate validation.

name: Betting-against-beta / low-volatility anomaly
mechanism: Long low-beta equities/ETFs (optionally leveraged toward unit beta), short or underweight high-beta ones -- leverage-constrained investors bid up high-beta assets, compressing their risk-adjusted return, so a low-beta-tilted portfolio earns a persistent premium. Long-only variant: overweight low-volatility ETFs (e.g. SPLV, USMV) relative to a cap-weighted benchmark.
source: Frazzini, A. & Pedersen, L.H. (2014), "Betting Against Beta", Journal of Financial Economics 111(1), 1-25. https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:eee:jfinec:v:111:y:2014:i:1:p:1-25 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). New mechanism (leverage-constraint-driven low-beta premium) -- not previously catalogued.

name: ETF/equity pairs trading (distance-method statistical arbitrage)
mechanism: Match two highly-correlated instruments (e.g. sector-pair ETFs, or an index ETF vs. its equal-weight twin) by minimum historical price-distance; go long the underperformer / short the outperformer when their spread diverges beyond a historical-sd threshold, closing on convergence or a time stop. Market-neutral relative-value mechanism, distinct from the single-instrument mean reversion already in this catalog.
source: Gatev, E., Goetzmann, W.N. & Rouwenhorst, K.G. (2006), "Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative-Value Arbitrage Rule", Review of Financial Studies 19(3), 797-827. https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/19/3/797/1646694 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Two-instrument relative-value mechanism, not previously catalogued. ENGINE-CAPABILITY GAP NOTE: the blocker is NOT the ticker (XLE/XOP above are both real, fetchable ETFs) -- it is that the backtest engine is single-instrument: src/mining/backtest_engine.py's run_backtest(df, signal_fn, ...) takes exactly one OHLC DataFrame and one SignalFn evaluated against that single frame. A pairs/spread strategy inherently needs two simultaneous price series to compute a spread and its divergence -- there is no way to express that as this engine's single-frame SignalFn. This is an engine-capability gap, not a data-availability problem, and it is not worked around with a synthetic pre-computed ratio file; until a two-instrument, spread-aware backtest mode exists, this candidate cannot be screened by the pipeline.

name: Cross-asset time-series momentum (bonds/gold/commodities)
mechanism: Apply a trailing-return trend-following rule (long if trailing 12-month return positive, flat/short otherwise) to non-equity-index ETFs -- Treasuries (TLT), gold (GLD), broad commodities (DBC). Diversifies into asset classes outside the leveraged-ETF rotation sleeve, rather than re-timing the same QQQ/SOX/SPY/DIA exposure that sleeve already covers -- the specific overlap that led to dual_momentum_taa_trend and gayed_200dma_letf_rotation above being excluded.
source: Moskowitz, T.J., Ooi, Y.H. & Pedersen, L.H. (2012), "Time Series Momentum", Journal of Financial Economics 104(2), 228-250. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304405X11002613 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Same general trend-following technique as the excluded LETF-rotation entries, but applied to non-overlapping asset classes -- see mechanism note for why this is not a re-proposal.

name: Halloween indicator / Sell-in-May seasonality
mechanism: Hold equity index ETF exposure only November-April (the 'winter' half of the calendar year), flat or in cash May-October. A distinct six-month seasonal effect from turn_of_month above (which was excluded on materiality grounds) -- larger reported effect size and a different calendar mechanism, warranting its own fresh materiality check rather than assuming it shares turn-of-month's fate.
source: Bouman, S. & Jacobsen, B. (2002), "The Halloween Indicator, 'Sell in May and Go Away': Another Puzzle", American Economic Review 92(5), 1618-1635. https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257%2F000282802762024683 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). New calendar mechanism, distinct effect size/window from turn_of_month above.

name: Value factor (book-to-market)
mechanism: Rank equities by book-to-market ratio (or a composite of book-to-market/earnings-to-price/cash-flow-to-price); buy the highest-book-to-market ('cheap') decile and hold with periodic reformation, expecting price to mean-revert toward fundamental value over a multi-year horizon. Foundational cross-sectional value premium, distinct from the price-nearness-to-high momentum signal (fifty_two_week_high_momentum) and the leverage-constraint-driven low-beta premium (betting_against_beta_low_vol) already in this catalog.
source: Fama, E.F. & French, K.R. (1992), "The Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns", Journal of Finance 47(2), 427-465. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1540-6261.1992.tb04398.x (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Foundational cross-sectional value premium -- distinct mechanism (book-to-market fundamental mispricing) from any momentum/low-vol/quality entry above; not previously catalogued. PROXY NOTE: the backtest engine only fetches a single ticker's OHLC (tickers[0]), so this cross-sectional decile strategy is tested via VLUE (iShares MSCI USA Value Factor ETF, real/verified via web search 2026-08-29) as a real, tradeable stand-in basket -- VLUE tracks a broad value-factor INDEX (MSCI's own methodology), not a literal book-to-market decile sort, so a pass/fail here says something about 'a real value-factor product's daily-bar behavior', not a direct replication of Fama-French's original portfolio construction. A future real gate on any survivor would need to decide whether the ETF-proxy result is itself sufficient or whether the literal decile-sort needs separate validation.

name: Quality-minus-junk (QMJ) factor
mechanism: Rank equities by a composite quality score (profitability, earnings growth, balance-sheet safety/low leverage, low earnings volatility, high payout); long the highest-quality decile (short or underweight the lowest, 'junk', decile in a long/short construction). Quality's premium is attributed to persistent mispricing/behavioral underpricing of safe, profitable firms, not the leverage-constraint mechanism behind betting_against_beta_low_vol already in this catalog -- the two factors are empirically correlated but mechanistically distinct in the source literature.
source: Asness, C.S., Frazzini, A. & Pedersen, L.H. (2019, orig. working paper 2013), "Quality Minus Junk", Review of Accounting Studies 24(1), 34-112. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2312432 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Distinct mechanism (composite quality characteristics, not leverage-constrained beta) from betting_against_beta_low_vol above; not previously catalogued.

name: Open-market buyback / net repurchase-yield anomaly
mechanism: Buy equities following open-market share-repurchase announcements, weighted toward value-tilted (high book-to-market) repurchasers where the undervaluation signal is strongest per the original study; hold multiple years as the market slowly incorporates the repurchase's informational content, since the market is documented to underreact to the announcement rather than overreact. Event-driven single-name signal, distinct from the cross-sectional book-to-market ranking of value_factor_book_to_market and from the earnings-surprise event in pead_earnings_surprise_drift.
source: Ikenberry, D., Lakonishok, J. & Vermaelen, T. (1995), "Market Underreaction to Open Market Share Repurchases", Journal of Financial Economics 39(2-3), 181-208. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0304405X9500826Z (verified via web search 2026-08-29). New mechanism (repurchase-announcement underreaction drift) -- distinct event and signal from PEAD's earnings-surprise trigger; not previously catalogued.

name: S&P 500 index-addition / reconstitution effect
mechanism: Buy an equity upon announcement of its addition to the S&P 500 (or a comparable major index), holding from announcement through the effective inclusion date and a short post-inclusion window; the price effect is attributed to inelastic index-fund/tracker demand shock ('demand curves for stocks slope down'), not a fundamental change in the company. Purely event/flow-driven, distinct from every fundamental- or price-pattern-based entry already in this catalog.
source: Shleifer, A. (1986), "Do Demand Curves for Stocks Slope Down?", Journal of Finance 41(3), 579-590. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1540-6261.1986.tb04518.x (verified via web search 2026-08-29). New mechanism (passive-fund demand shock from index reconstitution) -- not previously catalogued. NOT-TESTABLE-AS-SINGLE-TICKER NOTE: confirmed by web search 2026-08-29 (Morningstar 'The Index Inclusion Effect Isn't Cause for Concern'; NBER w27593; Greenwood/HBS 'The Disappearing Index Effect') -- this is inherently an EVENT STUDY across many discrete, historically-scattered index-inclusion announcements on many DIFFERENT stocks, not a standing exposure. There is no 'always-on' ticker, ETF, or ETN that represents 'being newly added to the S&P 500' the way e.g. a factor ETF represents a standing factor tilt -- each event is a different company on a different date, and once included, the stock is simply an ordinary S&P 500 constituent with no ongoing inclusion-effect exposure. A faithful test of this mechanism needs a real historical dataset of index-addition announcement dates paired with the affected tickers (an event-study harness), which this single-instrument, single-signal-function mining engine does not have a slot for -- distinct from etf_pairs_trading_stat_arb's gap (that one is a two-simultaneous-series problem; this one is a many-discrete-events-across-many-tickers problem). That event-study harness is scripts/run_index_addition_mining.py, which pools per-event trades over the publicly sourced events in data/mining/index_addition_cache/events.json instead of forcing the mechanism onto one placeholder ticker. Recent research (Greenwood/HBS, cited above) additionally finds the effect itself has weakened/disappeared over the past decade as passive AUM growth was already priced in, which weighs against the mechanism even with that harness.

name: Accrual anomaly
mechanism: Rank equities by total accruals scaled by total assets (the non-cash component of earnings); long the lowest-accrual ('high cash-flow quality') decile, short or avoid the highest-accrual decile, on an annual reformation following fiscal-year-end disclosures. Investors are documented to overweight the less-persistent accrual component of earnings and are systematically surprised when it reverses -- a distinct fundamental-mispricing mechanism from the earnings-surprise-momentum signal in pead_earnings_surprise_drift (which uses SUE, not the accrual/cash-flow decomposition of earnings).

parameters.universe_source: PENDING_CONFIRMATION -- the same CIK-resolved 25-ticker watchlist as capex_cycle_blue_chip_dip_pooled (built by scripts/build_capex_watchlist.py), which also avoids overlap with retail_inventory_sales_breadth_short's own inventory-driven mechanism

source: Sloan, R.G. (1996), "Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows about Future Earnings?", The Accounting Review 71(3), 289-315. https://publications.aaahq.org/accounting-review/article/71/3/289/18989 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Distinct fundamental-accounting mechanism (accrual/cash-flow earnings decomposition) from PEAD's earnings-surprise signal above; not previously catalogued. IMPLEMENTATION: no ETF/ETN isolates Sloan's accrual signal alone (see the NO-FAITHFUL-PROXY NOTE below), so the family is built on SEC EDGAR point-in-time XBRL fundamentals (mining.edgar_data, mining.edgar_point_in_time), the same plumbing that ranks/screens company universes directly from EDGAR for capex_cycle_blue_chip_dip_pooled and retail_inventory_sales_breadth_short. Total accruals is computed from three well-tagged, common XBRL concepts (NetIncomeLoss/ProfitLoss, NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities, Assets -- see mining.edgar_data's NET_INCOME_TAGS/CFO_TAGS/TOTAL_ASSETS_TAGS), scaled by average total assets (Sloan's own convention, verified via web search 2026-09-17). Built as src/mining/batch5/accrual_anomaly_sloan.py (pooled_single_asset shape) + src/mining/accrual_coverage.py (coverage check, mirrors retail_inventory_coverage.py) + scripts/run_accrual_anomaly_mining.py (bespoke ABI-1 driver, mirrors run_capex_cycle_mining.py). Universe: reuses capex_cycle_blue_chip_dip_pooled's CIK-resolved 25-name S&P 500 watchlist rather than a literal full-market cross-sectional decile rank -- chosen over retail_inventory_sales_breadth_short's XRT/retail universe specifically to avoid conflating accrual with that family's own inventory-driven mechanism (a retailer's working capital is dominated by inventory swings). "Decile" is approximated as a quintile (bottom_fraction=0.20) given the bounded 25-name pool -- a literal decile of 25 is 2-3 names, too thin to call a cross-section. NO-FAITHFUL-PROXY NOTE: confirmed by web search 2026-08-29 -- no dedicated accrual-anomaly ETF or ETN exists. The closest real products (iShares Edge MSCI USA Quality Factor ETF, QUAL; Invesco S&P 500 Quality Portfolio, SPHQ) use low accruals as ONE input inside a broader multi-factor quality composite (profitability, earnings growth, leverage, earnings volatility), not as the sole or primary sort variable Sloan's original single-variable accrual-to-total-assets ranking uses -- and QUAL is already this catalog's proxy for the separate quality_minus_junk_factor entry above, so reusing it here would silently test the SAME mechanism twice under two different family_ids rather than the accrual-specific one.

name: Merger arbitrage (risk arbitrage)
mechanism: On announcement of a definitive M&A deal, buy the target (in a cash deal) or buy the target and short the acquirer at the stock-swap ratio (in a stock deal), capturing the spread between the deal price and the target's market price as compensation for deal-completion risk; exit at deal close or on deal-break. Long-only or long/short depending on deal structure, no options -- distinct event-driven mechanism from every other entry in this catalog, with a documented return profile resembling a short index put (crash risk concentrated in market downturns).
source: Mitchell, M. & Pulvino, T. (2001), "Characteristics of Risk and Return in Risk Arbitrage", Journal of Finance 56(6), 2135-2175. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/0022-1082.00401 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). New event-driven mechanism (announced-merger spread capture) -- not previously catalogued. PROXY NOTE: tested via MNA (IQ Merger Arbitrage ETF, real/verified via web search 2026-08-29 -- launched 2009, tracks a systematic long-target/short-acquirer merger-arb index) as a real, tradeable stand-in for the single-deal-by-deal strategy described above -- MNA holds a diversified basket across many concurrent deals rather than one target/acquirer pair at a time, so this measures a real merger-arb product's daily-bar behavior, not a direct replication of Mitchell & Pulvino's single-deal event-study construction. A future real gate on any survivor would need to decide whether the ETF-proxy result is sufficient or whether the literal per-deal construction needs separate validation.

name: Small-Cap Size Premium
mechanism: Maintain a long-only, continuously-held position in a broad small-capitalization index fund (the S&P SmallCap 600), capturing the historically documented "size effect" where smaller-capitalization firms earn higher average risk-adjusted returns than large-cap firms. No cross-sectional stock-picking is performed by this pipeline -- the ETF itself already holds roughly 600 small-cap constituents that S&P reconstitutes quarterly -- so the test is whether persistent exposure to this cap-weighted small-cap basket earns a premium over a large-cap benchmark like SPY, independent of any trend or momentum timing overlay. Entry is at backtest start and the position stays fully invested throughout (subject only to the pipeline's own generic risk-management overlay, if applied).
source: Banz, R. W. (1981), "The Relationship Between Return and Market Value of Common Stocks," Journal of Financial Economics 9(1), 3-18. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0304405X81900180 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Ticker verified: IJR is a real, currently-trading BlackRock/iShares ETF launched May 22, 2000, tracking the S&P SmallCap 600 index (verified via stockanalysis.com and etfdb.com, 2026-08-29). DISTINCTNESS NOTE: tests the Fama-French/Banz SIZE factor (small- vs. large-cap exposure) as a standalone buy-and-hold position -- not a momentum rank, trend/MA rotation, volatility factor, fundamental sort, or calendar/intraday effect already in the catalog.

name: Equal-Weight Rebalancing Premium
mechanism: Hold the S&P 500 Equal-Weight Index -- each of the roughly 500 constituents held near 1/500th of the portfolio and mechanically rebalanced back to equal weights every quarter -- instead of the market-cap-weighted S&P 500. This forced quarterly rebalance systematically trims recent winners and adds to recent losers back to par, harvesting a documented "rebalancing premium" plus an implicit tilt away from mega-cap concentration relative to cap-weighting. The rule is simply to stay fully long the equal-weight index continuously; any premium over SPY comes from the ETF's own built-in rebalancing mechanism, not from a timing signal generated by this pipeline.
source: Plyakha, Y., Uppal, R., and Vilkov, G. (2012), "Why Does an Equal-Weighted Portfolio Outperform Value- and Price-Weighted Portfolios?" SSRN Working Paper 2724535. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2724535 (verified via web search 2026-08-29; the paper attributes roughly 42% of equal-weight outperformance directly to the rebalancing mechanism itself). Ticker verified: RSP is a real, currently-trading Invesco ETF launched April 24, 2003, tracking the S&P 500 Equal Weight Index (verified via stockanalysis.com and etfdb.com, 2026-08-29). DISTINCTNESS NOTE: isolates the equal-weight REBALANCING mechanism as the return driver -- structurally different from the cap-weighted trend rotations, momentum ranks, or single-name fundamental sorts already in the catalog.

name: Dividend Growth (Aristocrats) Quality
mechanism: Hold an equal-weighted basket of S&P 500 companies that have raised their dividend every year for at least 25 consecutive years (the "Dividend Aristocrats" methodology), with the basket reconstituted and rebalanced annually. The screen selects purely for a multi-decade streak of consecutive dividend increases -- evidence of durable earnings/cash-flow growth and management's shareholder-return commitment -- not for current yield level or a single-period profitability or leverage ratio; a high-yield stock with a spotty or cut dividend history is excluded, while a low-current-yield compounder with 25+ straight annual raises qualifies.
source: S&P Dow Jones Indices research, "Dividend Investing and a Look Inside the S&P Dow Jones Dividend Indices" and the S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats research note (backtest Dec-1999 to Jun-2019 showing +4.3%/yr annualized outperformance and a higher Sharpe ratio vs. the S&P Composite 1500). https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/documents/research/research-sp500-dividend-aristocrats.pdf (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Ticker verified: NOBL is a real, currently-trading ProShares ETF launched October 9, 2013, tracking the S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats Index (verified via stockanalysis.com and ProShares' own fact sheet dated 6/30/2026, 2026-08-29). DISTINCTNESS NOTE: screens on consecutive annual dividend-increase streak length, a different fundamental from the quality/buyback/value factors already in the catalog.

name: High Dividend Yield Factor
mechanism: Hold a market-cap-weighted basket of U.S. common stocks drawn from the top half of the market by trailing dividend yield (REITs excluded), rebalanced semi-annually, on the thesis from the dividend-yield literature that stocks with above-average current yield earn above-average future total returns. This is a cross-sectional RANK-AND-HOLD on the CURRENT yield level, not a growth-history screen: a stock qualifies purely by paying a high dividend relative to its price today, regardless of how many consecutive years it has raised that dividend.
source: Fama, E. F., and French, K. R. (1988), "Dividend Yields and Expected Stock Returns," Journal of Financial Economics 22(1), 3-25. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0304405X88900207 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Ticker verified: VYM is a real, currently-trading Vanguard ETF launched November 10, 2006, tracking the FTSE High Dividend Yield Index, with roughly 84 billion USD in AUM as of the most recent cited coverage (verified via stockanalysis.com and etfdb.com, 2026-08-29). DISTINCTNESS NOTE: ranks purely on current dividend YIELD LEVEL, distinct from the growth-streak screen above and from every other fundamental sort already in the catalog -- yield-level and payout-growth-history are separately-studied, only loosely correlated dividend factors.

name: January Small-Cap Effect
mechanism: Hold small-cap equity exposure only during the calendar month of January (positions opened at the January 1st trading session's open or the prior December close, closed at January's final trading session's close); stay in cash or a risk-free proxy the rest of the year. The mechanism is distinct from a general seasonal risk-premium shift (like Halloween): it is specifically attributed to a rebound after December tax-loss-selling pressure unwinds, concentrated in small, previously-depressed names, and is measured on a small-cap-specific instrument rather than a broad index.
source: Rozeff, M.S. & Kinney, W.R. (1976), "Capital Market Seasonality: The Case of Stock Returns", Journal of Financial Economics 3(4). Keim, D.B. (1983), "Size-Related Anomalies and Stock Return Seasonality: Further Empirical Evidence", Journal of Financial Economics 12(1). Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker verified: IWM (iShares Russell 2000 ETF), issuer BlackRock, inception May 22, 2000, actively exchange-traded today. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: driven by a size-premium/tax-loss-selling-rebound mechanism concentrated in a single named month (January) on small-cap stocks specifically, unlike turn_of_month, pre_fomc_drift, or the Halloween indicator's 6-month split.

name: Santa Claus Rally Window
mechanism: Go long a broad equity index ETF at the close of the 6th-to-last trading day of the calendar year (i.e., entering before the last 5 trading days of December) and hold through the close of the 2nd trading day of the new January, then exit to cash -- a fixed 7-trading-day seasonal window each year end. This is a specific, narrowly-dated year-end window (not a month-boundary or half-year split) historically associated with low-volume holiday-period buying pressure and portfolio positioning.
source: Hirsch, Yale (1972), Stock Trader's Almanac (Hirsch Organization / Wiley), which first defined and has tracked this 7-trading-day window since 1950-era data; window and ~1.3% average S&P 500 return with ~80% historical win rate confirmed via web search 2026-08-29 (Britannica Money, LPL Research). Ticker verified: SPY (SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust), issuer State Street Global Advisors, inception January 22, 1993, actively exchange-traded today. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: a fixed, narrowly-dated 7-trading-day year-end window distinct from turn_of_month's monthly window and the Halloween indicator's 6-month split.

name: Weekend/Monday Effect
mechanism: Exploit the historically weak or negative average return on Mondays relative to other weekdays: hold a broad equity index ETF long from Monday's close through Friday's close each week (i.e., skip holding the position over the Friday-close-to-Monday-close weekend/Monday session), rebalancing weekly. This tests a day-of-week return-generating-process anomaly, not a monthly or macro-seasonal one.
source: French, K.R. (1980), "Stock Returns and the Weekend Effect", Journal of Financial Economics 8(1), pp. 55-69. Verified via web search 2026-08-29 (paper found average Monday returns significantly negative vs. positive on other four weekdays for the S&P composite, 1953-1977). Ticker verified: SPY (SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust), issuer State Street Global Advisors, inception January 22, 1993, actively exchange-traded today. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: a weekly, day-of-week-keyed rule (skip Monday, hold Tue-Fri) is a fundamentally different calendar axis than any monthly, event-relative, or half-year effect already in the catalog. CAVEAT: later literature (e.g. Kamara 1997) documents this effect weakening or disappearing at the S&P 500 level after ~1987, likely arbitraged away by index-futures trading -- included anyway because the DSR+holdout bar is designed to catch a decayed effect empirically rather than exclude it by literature-reading alone.

name: Triple Witching Week Effect
mechanism: Take a position in a broad equity index ETF during the trading week that contains the third Friday of March, June, September, or December -- the quarterly date when stock index futures, stock index options, and single-stock options all expire simultaneously -- entering at that week's open and exiting at that week's close, four times per year. The mechanism is derivatives-expiration-driven order flow and unwind pressure (options/futures rebalancing, pinning, and program trading around expiration), not a macro seasonal risk-premium or a day-of-week/tax-timing effect.
source: Stoll, H.R. & Whaley, R.E. (1990), "Program Trading and Individual Stock Returns: Ingredients of the Triple-Witching Brew", Journal of Business 63(1), pp. S165-S192. Verified via web search 2026-08-29 (documented downward price pressure and elevated volatility around simultaneous quarterly expiration of index futures/options/options-on-futures). Ticker verified: QQQ (Invesco QQQ Trust), issuer Invesco, inception March 10, 1999, actively exchange-traded today. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: keyed on a quarterly derivatives-expiration calendar driven by options/futures unwind mechanics, entirely different from every other calendar mechanism already in the catalog, and operates on daily bars (week open to week close), not intraday.

name: High-Yield/Investment-Grade Credit Spread Regime Filter
mechanism: Compute the daily price ratio HYG/LQD as a real-time proxy for the high-yield-vs-investment-grade credit spread (bond prices move inversely to yields, so a falling ratio means high-yield bonds are underperforming investment-grade bonds -- i.e., credit spreads are widening, a risk-off signal). Take a 20-day and a 100-day simple moving average of this ratio. Hold SPY long while the 20-day average is above the 100-day average (spreads stable or compressing); exit to a cash/short-Treasury (SHY) position when the 20-day average crosses below the 100-day average (spreads widening). Re-evaluate the crossover daily and re-enter SPY once the 20-day average crosses back above the 100-day average. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch HYG and LQD OHLC itself (via data_pipeline.fetch_ohlc) and align by date to the traded ticker's (SPY) index.
source: Chen, N., Roll, R. & Ross, S.A. (1986), "Economic Forces and the Stock Market", Journal of Business 59(3), 383-403. Corroborated by Fama, E.F. & French, K.R. (1989), "Business Conditions and Expected Returns on Stocks and Bonds", Journal of Financial Economics 25(1), 23-49. Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Tickers verified: HYG (iShares iBoxx $ High Yield Corporate Bond ETF, BlackRock, inception 2007-04-04), LQD (iShares iBoxx $ Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF, BlackRock, inception 2002-07-22), SPY (State Street, inception 1993) -- all actively trading. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: uses a corporate credit-spread proxy (HYG/LQD ratio) as a moving-average regime filter -- no other candidate in the catalog uses a credit-spread or bond-ratio signal.

name: Treasury Curve Slope (Long-vs-Short Duration) Equity Filter
mechanism: Compute the daily price ratio TLT/SHY as a proxy for the Treasury yield-curve slope (TLT's long duration makes it far more sensitive to long-end yield moves than SHY's short duration, so a rising ratio reflects the curve flattening -- long yields falling faster than short yields -- while a falling ratio reflects steepening). Take the ratio's 126-trading-day (6-month) rate of change. When that change exceeds +8% (curve flattening sharply, historically a leading recession/risk signal per Estrella-Mishkin), scale SPY exposure down into a defensive cash/short-Treasury (SHY) allocation; when the 6-month change is below +8% (curve normal or steepening), hold SPY at full weight. Re-evaluate once a month. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch TLT and SHY OHLC itself and align by date.
source: Estrella, A. & Mishkin, F.S. (1998), "Predicting U.S. Recessions: Financial Variables as Leading Indicators", Review of Economics and Statistics 80(1), 45-61. https://direct.mit.edu/rest/article/80/1/45/57058 . Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Tickers verified: TLT (iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF, BlackRock, inception 2002-07-22), SHY (iShares 1-3 Year Treasury Bond ETF, BlackRock, inception 2002-07-22) -- both actively trading. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: uses the Treasury long-vs-short duration price ratio as a yield-curve-slope proxy -- a rates/macro regime signal with no counterpart among the trend-following candidates already in the catalog, which have no term-structure concept.

name: Broad Dollar Strength Risk-Off Filter
mechanism: Track UUP's closing price against its own 200-day simple moving average as a proxy for broad US dollar strength. When UUP closes above its 200-day average (the dollar in a sustained uptrend -- historically coinciding with tighter global USD funding conditions and risk-asset stress), move out of SPY into a defensive cash/short-Treasury (SHY) allocation. When UUP closes below its 200-day average (dollar weakening or range-bound -- easier global liquidity), hold SPY at full weight. Recompute the signal daily. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch UUP OHLC itself and align by date to SPY.
source: Bruno, V. & Shin, H.S. (2015), "Cross-Border Banking and Global Liquidity", Review of Economic Studies 82(2), 535-564. https://academic.oup.com/restud/article-abstract/82/2/535/1585168 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Ticker verified: UUP = Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund, issuer Invesco, inception 2007-02-20, actively trading. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: no other candidate in the catalog uses a currency/USD signal -- a genuinely new macro input applied as an equity-exposure filter.

name: Real-Rate-Driven Gold/Equity Rotation
mechanism: Use TIP's own price trend as a real-time proxy for the direction of real interest rates: by construction of an inflation-protected bond, TIP's price rises when real yields fall and falls when real yields rise. Compute TIP's 63-trading-day (3-month) return. When that return exceeds +2% (real yields falling meaningfully), rotate the full position out of SPY and into GLD, since gold's real return is documented as strongly negatively correlated with real rates. When TIP's 3-month return is below +2% (real yields flat or rising), hold SPY instead. Re-evaluate once a month. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch TIP OHLC itself and align by date; the traded ticker (tickers[0]=SPY) frame supplied by the harness is one leg of the SPY/GLD switch -- GLD's own OHLC must also be fetched inside signal_fn for the switch to actually work.
source: Erb, C.B. & Harvey, C.R. (2013), "The Golden Dilemma", Financial Analysts Journal 69(4), 10-42 (documents an approximately -82% correlation between real interest rates and gold's real price, 1997-2012). https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2078535 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Tickers verified: GLD (SPDR Gold Shares, State Street, inception 2004-11-18), TIP (iShares TIPS Bond ETF, BlackRock, inception 2003-12-04) -- both actively trading. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: rotates between SPY and GLD keyed to a real-interest-rate proxy (TIP's price trend), mechanically and economically distinct from the catalog's existing absolute-momentum time-series candidate, which trend-follows each asset's own return with no real-rate concept.

name: VIX Term Structure Carry
mechanism: Each day, compute the ratio of the spot CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) to the CBOE 3-Month Volatility Index (VIX3M). When the ratio is below 1.0 (contango -- the futures curve is upward-sloped and short-dated VIX futures decay toward the higher long-dated price), hold SVXY, ProShares' short-VIX-futures ETF, long to harvest the roll yield. When the ratio rises to 1.0 or above (backwardation -- the curve inverts, roll yield turns negative and a volatility event is typically already underway), close the SVXY position and hold cash. Re-enter SVXY once the ratio drops back below 1.0. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch ^VIX and ^VIX3M via data_pipeline.fetch_ohlc and align by date to the SVXY frame.
source: Simon, D.P. and Campasano, J. (2014), "The VIX Futures Basis: Evidence and Trading Strategies," Journal of Derivatives, 21(3), 54-69 (SSRN abstract_id=2094510). Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker verified: SVXY = ProShares Short VIX Short-Term Futures ETF, issuer ProShares, inception 2011-10-03, confirmed actively trading in 2026. ^VIX3M confirmed as a live, currently-quoted CBOE index on Yahoo Finance. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: a volatility-ETP carry trade keyed on the futures-curve slope (VIX vs VIX3M ratio) -- a different signal and product family from any options-trading or oscillator-based candidate already in the catalog.

name: VIX Spike Reversal Buy
mechanism: Track the VIX index's own 10-day moving average. When VIX closes at least 50% above that moving average (a volatility spike, historically most common when VIX also crosses above roughly 30), buy SPY the next session and hold for a fixed 10-trading-day window before exiting, regardless of what VIX does in between. No new entry is taken on additional spikes while a position is already open. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch ^VIX via data_pipeline.fetch_ohlc and align by date to the SPY frame.
source: Whaley, R.E. (2000), "The Investor Fear Gauge," Journal of Portfolio Management, 26(3), 12-17; Giot, P. (2005), "Relationships Between Implied Volatility Indexes and Stock Index Returns," Journal of Portfolio Management, 31(3), 92-100. Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker verified: SPY, State Street, inception 1993, most liquid U.S. equity ETF. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: the trigger is the standalone VIX implied-volatility index spiking, a cross-asset signal, not a price-derived oscillator computed purely from SPY's own OHLC bars like the catalog's existing RSI2/IBS candidate -- and it is a reactive post-spike entry, the opposite timing of the VVIX/VIX de-risking candidate below.

name: Variance Risk Premium Harvest
mechanism: Each day, compute SPY's trailing 20-day realized (historical) volatility, annualized, and subtract it from the current VIX level (implied volatility). When that spread -- the variance risk premium -- is positive, meaning implied volatility trades above what has recently realized, hold SVXY long to harvest the premium option sellers are paid for insuring against volatility. When the spread compresses toward zero or turns negative, exit to cash. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch ^VIX and SPY OHLC (in addition to the harness-supplied SVXY frame) and align by date.
source: Carr, P. and Wu, L. (2009), "Variance Risk Premiums," Review of Financial Studies, 22(3), 1311-1341. Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker verified: SVXY = ProShares Short VIX Short-Term Futures ETF, inception 2011-10-03, actively trading. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: triggers off an implied-vs-realized valuation spread (Carr-Wu variance risk premium) rather than the futures curve's contango/backwardation slope used by the term-structure-carry candidate above -- a separately-published, distinct academic mechanism despite trading the same instrument (SVXY).

name: VVIX/VIX De-Risking Regime
mechanism: Compute the ratio of the CBOE VVIX Index (the implied volatility of VIX options, "the vol of the VIX") to the VIX index itself. This ratio normally sits near a long-run median around 4.5; when it rises above roughly 6, options traders are aggressively bidding up protection against further VIX moves even though VIX itself has not yet spiked, historically a leading stress signal. Reduce the SPY position to cash while the ratio stays elevated above that threshold, and hold SPY normally once it falls back into its typical band. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch ^VVIX and ^VIX via data_pipeline.fetch_ohlc and align by date to the SPY frame.
source: Huang, D., Schlag, C., Shaliastovich, I., and Thimme, J. (2019), "Volatility-of-Volatility Risk," Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis, 54(6), 2423-2452 (SSRN abstract_id=2497759). Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker verified: ^VVIX = CBOE VVIX Index, introduced 2012, confirmed still published/quoted today. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: a leading vol-of-vol regime filter that reduces equity exposure BEFORE a VIX spike is confirmed -- the opposite direction and timing of the reactive post-spike buy candidate above, and uses an entirely different index pair (VVIX/VIX) not referenced by any other candidate.

name: Defensive Sector Rotation on Recession-Risk Signal
mechanism: Rotate into Utilities (XLU) as a defensive holding when the yield curve signals rising recession risk, and hold the broad market (SPY) otherwise. The recession-risk signal is the 10-year minus 3-month Treasury yield spread (10y ~ ^TNX, 3-month ~ ^IRX); when the spread inverts (short rates exceed long rates), switch into XLU, following the documented pattern that defensive sectors like utilities outperform around economic slowdowns. Rebalance monthly on signal changes; a positively-sloped curve holds SPY instead. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch ^TNX and ^IRX via data_pipeline.fetch_ohlc and align by date to the XLU frame.
source: Estrella, A. & Mishkin, F.S. (1996), "The Yield Curve as a Predictor of U.S. Recessions," Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Current Issues in Economics and Finance, Vol. 2, No. 7. https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/current_issues/ci2-7.pdf . Defensive-sector response documented in Sam Stovall's S&P's Guide to Sector Rotation. Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker verified: XLU = Utilities Select Sector SPDR ETF, State Street, inception 1998-12-16, actively trading. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: uses a macro yield-curve-inversion regime signal, not a price trend/MA rule or multi-asset relative-momentum ranking, to switch a single defensive sector ETF in and out of the market.

name: Financials Rotation on Yield Curve Steepening
mechanism: Long the Financial Select Sector SPDR (XLF) when the yield curve is steepening -- the 10-year minus 2-year Treasury spread is rising over its trailing trend -- because a steeper curve expands bank net interest margins, the spread banks earn borrowing short-term and lending long-term. Exit to cash/SPY when the spread is flattening or inverting, which compresses margins and has historically pressured bank profitability. The signal is the rolling trend (rate of change) of the 10y-2y spread, rebalanced monthly. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch ^TNX and a 2-year proxy (e.g. via yfinance ^UST2Y or a documented substitute if unavailable) via data_pipeline.fetch_ohlc and align by date.
source: English, W.B. (2002), "Interest Rate Risk and Bank Net Interest Margins," BIS Quarterly Review, December 2002, pp. 67-82. https://www.bis.org/publ/qtrpdf/r_qt0212g.pdf . Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker verified: XLF = Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF, State Street, inception 1998-12-16, actively trading. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: trades a single-sector ETF on a yield-curve STEEPENING signal tied to bank net interest margin mechanics -- opposite signal direction and different economic mechanism than the recession-signal candidate above, and unrelated to any momentum, mean-reversion, calendar, or factor mechanism already in the catalog.

name: REIT Rotation on Dividend Yield Spread vs Treasuries
mechanism: Long the Vanguard Real Estate ETF (VNQ) when REITs are cheap relative to bonds -- the spread between the REIT sector's trailing dividend yield and the 10-year Treasury yield is wide relative to its own trailing history -- since historically a wide spread (roughly 1.5-2.0 points or more) has preceded strong forward REIT total returns. Exit to cash/SPY when the spread compresses well below its trailing average. Rebalance monthly using a rolling z-score of the yield spread computed over a multi-year lookback. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch ^TNX via data_pipeline.fetch_ohlc and compute VNQ's own trailing dividend yield from its distribution history or a documented proxy, aligned by date.
source: Nareit, "Using REIT Yield Spreads to Make Tactical Investment Decisions," Nareit Market Commentary, November 2020. https://www.reit.com/news/blog/market-commentary/using-reit-yield-spreads-to-make-tactical-investment-decisions . Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker verified: VNQ = Vanguard Real Estate ETF, Vanguard, inception 2004-09-23, actively trading. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: a valuation/spread-based regime signal (REIT dividend yield relative to the risk-free rate), not a price-momentum or trend rule -- targets the REIT sector specifically rather than a broad-market or leveraged-ETF trend signal already in the catalog.

name: Gold Miners Rotation on Real Interest Rates
mechanism: Long the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) when real interest rates are falling or negative -- proxied by the trend in the 10-year Treasury yield minus breakeven inflation expectations -- since gold, and by extension gold-mining equities economically leveraged to the gold price, has historically moved inversely with real rates. Move to cash when real rates are rising. The signal is the trailing change in the real-rate proxy over a multi-month window, rebalanced monthly. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch ^TNX and a breakeven-inflation proxy (e.g. via a documented FRED-equivalent series or TIP-vs-nominal-Treasury spread) and align by date.
source: Erb, C.B. & Harvey, C.R. Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker verified: GDX = VanEck Gold Miners ETF, VanEck, inception 2006-05-22, actively trading.
