name: Spin-Off Outperformance
mechanism: When a company spins off a division into an independently-traded stock, both the spinoff and its former parent tend to outperform the market for roughly the following one to three years -- index funds and institutional holders that only mandate the parent's profile are forced to sell the newly-listed, often smaller/off-index spinoff regardless of its fundamentals, creating temporary underpricing that corrects over time. The strategy holds a continuously-refreshed basket of these post-spinoff names, proxied by an ETF that adds each new U.S. spinoff shortly after it begins trading and holds it for up to four years before rotating it out, rather than trying to time individual spinoff events by hand.
source: Cusatis, P., Miles, J., Woolridge, J.R. (1993), "Restructuring Through Spinoffs: The Stock Market Evidence," Journal of Financial Economics, 33(3), 293-311 (found spinoffs outperformed industry-matched benchmarks by ~30% over 3 years for 161 spinoffs, 1965-1988). Verified via web search 2026-08-29: Invesco S&P Spin-Off ETF (CSD), issuer Invesco, inception December 15, 2006, confirmed currently trading on NYSE Arca. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: no other candidate in the catalog involves a corporate divestiture/spinoff event -- unrelated to momentum, mean reversion, calendar effects, or the merger-arb/buyback/index-addition mechanisms already covered.

name: Hedge Fund High-Conviction 13F Copycat
mechanism: Each quarter, hedge funds must publicly disclose their U.S. equity holdings via SEC Form 13F; the small subset of stocks that represent the largest, most concentrated positions relative to each fund's own portfolio ("best ideas") continue to outperform after the filing becomes public, even accounting for the mandatory 45-day disclosure lag. The strategy holds a rules-based basket of these high-conviction picks aggregated across a curated panel of hedge funds, reconstituted each quarter as new 13F filings are processed, proxied by an ETF built directly on this methodology.
source: Cohen, R.B., Polk, C., Silli, B., "Best Ideas" (SSRN 1364827), finds high-conviction manager holdings outperform the market and the rest of the same manager's portfolio by roughly 2.8-4.5%/year. Verified via web search 2026-08-29: Global X Guru Index ETF (GURU), issuer Global X, launched June 4, 2012, tracks the Solactive Guru Index built from hedge fund Form 13F filings, confirmed actively trading. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: tracks institutional 13F-disclosure-driven conviction picks pooled across many hedge funds -- a fundamentally different signal source from price-based momentum, factor indexes, or any calendar/technical rule already in the catalog, and is not merger arbitrage or buyback-driven.

name: IPO Long-Run Underperformance Fade
mechanism: Newly public companies tend to underperform the broad market and matched non-issuing peers over the one-to-three years following their IPO, once the initial first-day pop and post-IPO "honeymoon" period fade -- largely because issuers and underwriters time offerings to windows of investor over-optimism. The strategy takes a SHORT position in a continuously-refreshed basket of recent U.S. IPOs, proxied by an ETF that adds new offerings on a fast-entry basis shortly after listing and removes each holding after roughly two years, harvesting the documented long-run underperformance spread versus the broad market.
source: Ritter, J.R. (1991), "The Long-Run Performance of Initial Public Offerings," Journal of Finance, 46(1), 3-27 -- documents IPOs returning 34.5% vs. 61.9% for a matched non-issuing control sample over the 3 years from first-day close, 1975-84. Verified via web search 2026-08-29: Renaissance IPO ETF (IPO), issuer Renaissance Capital, inception October 14, 2013, confirmed actively trading. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: targets long-run price drift following a company's own IPO -- a distinct corporate-lifecycle anomaly from post-earnings drift or index-addition already in the catalog; also directionally SHORT rather than long, unlike every other candidate.

name: Fallen Angel Bond Re-Rating Drift
mechanism: When a corporate bond issuer is downgraded from investment-grade to high-yield ("fallen angel" status), forced selling by investment-grade-only mandates and insurers pushes the bond's price below fair value; documented research shows an initial post-downgrade dip followed by a multi-year reversal/recovery that outperforms both the broad high-yield index and newly-issued junk bonds of similar credit quality. The strategy holds a continuously-rebalanced basket of these recently-downgraded issuers, proxied by an ETF reconstituted monthly to add newly-downgraded names and remove issuers once upgraded back to investment grade or that default.
source: Ben Dor, A., Xu, Z. (2011), "Fallen Angels: Characteristics, Performance, and Implications for Investors," Journal of Fixed Income, 20(4), 33-58. Verified via web search 2026-08-29: VanEck Fallen Angel High Yield Bond ETF (ANGL), issuer VanEck, launched April 10, 2012, confirmed actively trading. NOTE: this is a credit-rating-downgrade event on corporate BONDS, not an equity anomaly -- consistent with the catalog's existing precedent of bond/commodity ETFs as instruments (TLT/GLD/DBC in cross_asset_time_series_momentum). DISTINCTNESS NOTE: a genuine corporate/credit-action anomaly (forced-selling overreaction on a rating downgrade) with no overlap with any other candidate.

name: Weekly Short-Term Return Reversal
mechanism: Lehmann (1990) and Jegadeesh (1990) documented that securities with an unusually large negative (positive) return over a short window earn abnormally positive (negative) returns the following period -- a pure return-magnitude overreaction effect, not an oscillator reading. Adapted to a single liquid ETF: compute the trailing 5-trading-day (1-week) cumulative close-to-close return; when it falls below a large-negative threshold (a z-score below -1.5 versus its own trailing 1-year distribution of 5-day returns, roughly a -3% weekly move), go long at the next close. Hold for a fixed 5-trading-day period and then exit, re-evaluating the trigger fresh each week rather than holding indefinitely.
source: Lehmann, B.N. (1990), "Fads, Martingales, and Market Efficiency", Quarterly Journal of Economics 105(1), 1-28. Jegadeesh, N. (1990), "Evidence of Predictable Behavior of Security Returns", Journal of Finance 45(3), 881-898. Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker verified: SPY, State Street, inception 1993. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: triggers on a rolling 5-day realized return magnitude (a z-scored return, not an RSI/IBS oscillator formula) -- the classic short-horizon (1-week) reversal literature, unrelated to the RSI(2)/IBS oscillator already in the catalog.

name: Large Cumulative Decline Rebound
mechanism: Bremer & Sweeney (1991) found that extremely large negative 10-day cumulative stock returns are followed on average by statistically significant positive rebounds over the next several trading days, a return-magnitude event trigger, not an oscillator reading. Applied to a single ETF: compute the trailing 10-trading-day cumulative close-to-close return; when it drops below a large-negative threshold (-10%), enter long at the next close to capture the rebound. Hold for a short fixed window (5 trading days) and exit, since the documented rebound is concentrated in the first one to two days after the trigger and decays quickly thereafter.
source: Bremer, M. & Sweeney, R.J. (1991), "The Reversal of Large Stock-Price Decreases", Journal of Finance 46(2), 747-754. Atkins, A.B. & Dyl, E.A. (1990), "Price Reversals, Bid-Ask Spreads, and Market Efficiency", Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 25(4), 535-547. Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker verified: QQQ, Invesco, inception 1999. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: triggers on an extreme, event-like 10-day cumulative decline (a crash/rebound event definition), a different window and threshold philosophy than the weekly reversal candidate above and unrelated to any RSI/IBS oscillator or momentum-ranking candidate already in the catalog.

name: Turtle Soup Failed-Breakout Reversal
mechanism: Raschke & Connors' 'Turtle Soup' pattern (Street Smarts, 1996) fades failed breakouts of the rolling 20-trading-day price extreme -- the mirror image of the original Turtle trend-following breakout system. Track the rolling 20-day low (and high), requiring the prior extreme to have been set at least 4 sessions earlier; when the ETF closes below that low (a fresh 20-day low) and then closes back above the prior low within the next 1-2 sessions, enter long, since the breakdown has failed and reversed -- mirror the rule for shorts on a failed new 20-day high. Exit on a fixed holding period or when price closes back above a short (5-day) moving average.
source: Raschke, L.B. & Connors, L.A. (1996), Street Smarts: High Probability Short-Term Trading Strategies, M. Gordon Publishing Group. Verified via web search 2026-08-29 (also documented at turtletrader.com and oxfordstrat.com). Ticker verified: SPY, State Street, inception 1993. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: fades a confirmed failed breakout of a rolling 20-day price level (a level/pattern-based trigger requiring the breakout to reverse) -- structurally different from a raw return-magnitude threshold, an oscillator formula, and nearness-to-52-week-high momentum ranking, since it specifically fades new extremes rather than ranking proximity to them.

name: Multi-Year Index Mean Reversion
mechanism: Fama & French (1988) and Poterba & Summers (1988) found that aggregate stock index returns contain a slowly mean-reverting component, with returns negatively autocorrelated at roughly 3-to-5-year horizons -- unusually weak (strong) trailing multi-year performance tends to be followed by above-(below-)average subsequent returns. Applied to a single index ETF: compute the trailing 36-month (3-year) cumulative total return and z-score it against its own trailing 15-year rolling history of 36-month returns; when the z-score falls below -1.0 (an unusually poor 3-year run), go long or overweight for the following year, and when it rises above +1.0, reduce or flatten the position. Rebalance monthly.
source: Fama, E.F. & French, K.R. (1988), "Permanent and Temporary Components of Stock Prices", Journal of Political Economy 96(2), 246-273. Poterba, J.M. & Summers, L.H. (1988), "Mean Reversion in Stock Prices: Evidence and Implications", Journal of Financial Economics 22(1), 27-59 (NBER Working Paper 2343). Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker verified: SPY, State Street, inception January 22 1993 (30+ years of history for the 3-year-return/15-year-lookback windows this mechanism needs). DISTINCTNESS NOTE: operates on a multi-year (3-to-5-year) horizon using the index's own long-run serial correlation -- a categorically different time-scale and statistical mechanism from every short-term reversal, calendar, or trend/momentum candidate already in the catalog.

name: Emerging vs Developed Markets Relative Strength Rotation
mechanism: At the end of each month, compute the trailing 6-month total return of EEM (emerging markets equities) and EFA (developed ex-US equities). Hold whichever of the two had the higher trailing return for the following month, fully invested at all times (no cash/bond fallback, no absolute trend filter). Rebalance monthly by re-ranking the pair and switching holdings only when the ranking flips. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch EFA OHLC itself (in addition to the harness-supplied EEM frame, tickers[0]) and align by date to compute the relative-strength comparison.
source: Faber, Mebane T. (2010), "Relative Strength Strategies for Investing," Cambria Investment Management working paper, SSRN abstract_id=1585517. Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker facts verified same search: EEM (iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ETF, BlackRock, inception April 7, 2003) and EFA (iShares MSCI EAFE ETF, BlackRock, inception August 14, 2001), both real, currently exchange-traded, 20+ year price histories. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: uses always-invested relative-strength ranking between two specific equity regimes (no absolute trend/MA filter, no cash fallback) -- mechanically distinct from the catalog's multi-asset TAA (absolute-trend-gated with a cash/bond safe-haven) and time-series-momentum candidates.

name: Commodity Backwardation & Momentum Selection Index (USCI)
mechanism: Hold USCI, an ETF that itself implements a monthly commodity-SELECTION rule (not a price-trend rule applied by us): each month its underlying SummerHaven Dynamic Commodity Index screens 27 eligible commodity futures and picks the 7 showing the greatest backwardation (or least contango) plus the 7 showing the strongest 12-month momentum, subject to a minimum-sector-diversification constraint, then equal-weights the resulting 14. The strategy simply buys and holds this reformulated basket, testing whether the backwardation/roll-yield-and-momentum contract-selection premium (distinct from a fixed-weight commodity index) earns excess return.
source: Gorton, Gary B., Fumio Hayashi, and K. Geert Rouwenhorst (2013), "The Fundamentals of Commodity Futures Returns," Review of Finance, 17(1), 35-105. SummerHaven Dynamic Commodity Index methodology: https://summerhavenindex.com/sdci_methodology/ . Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker fact verified: USCI (United States Commodity Index Fund, issuer USCF Investments/Marygold, launched Aug 10, 2010), real, currently exchange-traded. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: the alpha source is the fund's own monthly backwardation-plus-momentum contract SELECTION across 27 commodities (a curve-shape/roll-yield signal), mechanically unrelated to the catalog's fixed-weight commodity time-series-momentum candidate (DBC) or the 200-day-MA trend rule.

name: Managed Futures / CTA Trend Replication (DBMF)
mechanism: Hold DBMF, an ETF that does not follow a single-asset price rule but instead runs a rolling regression each month to replicate the aggregate long/short futures positioning of a basket of the largest managed-futures (CTA/trend-following) hedge funds across equity indices, fixed income, currencies, and commodities simultaneously. The strategy is simply to buy and hold this replicated basket, testing whether the diversified, dynamically-net-long-or-short trend premium documented in the managed-futures literature is captured by an investable single ticker.
source: Hasanhodzic, Jasmina, and Andrew W. Lo (2007), "Can Hedge-Fund Returns Be Replicated?: The Linear Case," Journal of Investment Management, 5(2), 5-45 (SSRN abstract_id=924565). Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker fact verified: DBMF (iMGP DBi Managed Futures Strategy ETF, issuer iM Global Partner / Dynamic Beta Investments, launched May 2019), real, currently exchange-traded, described in industry coverage as the largest managed-futures ETF. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: a multi-asset, dynamically long-or-short regression-replicated exposure to professional trend-followers' aggregate positioning (an entirely different construction than a self-computed trend/momentum signal) -- no other candidate buys a third-party-replicated CTA return stream.

name: Commodity-Currency Cross-Asset Lead-Lag (DBC signal to FXA)
mechanism: At each month-end, compute the trailing 6-month return of a broad commodity index (DBC), and use that as a leading signal to trade a DIFFERENT, economically-linked instrument: the Australian dollar via FXA. If DBC's trailing 6-month return is positive, hold FXA (long AUD) for the next month; if negative, hold cash. This exploits the documented linkage between world commodity export prices and the currencies of commodity-exporting economies -- a cross-asset PREDICTIVE signal (one ticker's trend forecasts a different ticker's direction), not a same-asset trend or a same-asset-class rotation. Implementation note: signal_fn must fetch DBC OHLC itself and align by date to the FXA frame.
source: Chen, Yu-chin, and Kenneth Rogoff (2003), "Commodity Currencies," Journal of International Economics, 60(1), 133-160. Verified via web search 2026-08-29. Ticker facts verified: FXA (Invesco CurrencyShares Australian Dollar Trust, tracks spot AUD), confirmed actively trading; DBC (Invesco DB Commodity Index Tracking Fund), an existing liquid broad commodity ETF. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: a cross-asset lead-lag mechanism -- a signal computed on one ticker (DBC) trades an entirely different, economically-linked ticker (FXA, a currency) -- no other candidate uses one asset's signal to time a different asset class.

name: Analyst Rating Upgrade Momentum
mechanism: Each quarter, rank all Bloomberg US Large & Mid Cap Index members (min. 10 million USD/day traded) by an analyst-recommendation-improvement score that measures how much the stock's average sell-side buy/hold/sell rating has improved over the trailing 6- and 12-month windows. Hold an equal-weighted basket of the 50 stocks with the biggest rating upgrades, reconstituting/rebalancing every March, June, September, and December.
source: Womack, K. L. (1996), "Do Brokerage Analysts' Recommendations Have Investment Value?", Journal of Finance 51(1), 137-167. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1540-6261.1996.tb05205.x (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Ticker verified: Invesco Bloomberg Analyst Rating Improvers ETF (UPGD), issuer Invesco, inception 2006-05-19, actively trading (~110 million USD AUM).

name: Insider Cluster Buying with Value Overlay
mechanism: Screen for companies with recent discretionary open-market SEC Form 4 insider purchases (not automatic comp-plan buys), then within that subset further rank on a multi-factor deep-value composite (price/book, price/earnings, price/cash-flow); hold names passing both filters.
source: Jeng, Metrick & Zeckhauser (2003), "Estimating the Returns to Insider Trading", Review of Economics and Statistics 85(2), 453-471. https://direct.mit.edu/rest/article/85/2/453/57400 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Ticker verified: Tweedy, Browne Insider + Value ETF (COPY), issuer Tweedy Browne, inception 2024-12-27, actively trading. SHORT-HISTORY CAVEAT (disclosed, not forced): only ~20 months of live trading as of 2026-08-29, materially shorter than most catalog tickers -- may not clear MIN_TRADES_FOR_SCORING or provide a meaningful holdout split; let the pipeline's own eligibility gating decide, not a pre-judgment here.

name: High-Yield Credit Bond Absolute Momentum
mechanism: Compute HYG's own trailing 6-month total return. If positive, hold HYG; if negative, rotate fully into BIL (T-bill cash proxy). Re-evaluate monthly. A single-instrument absolute (time-series) momentum filter on the credit-risk premium itself, distinct from a cross-asset equity-timing regime signal.
source: Jostova, Nikolova, Philipov & Stahel (2013), "Momentum in Corporate Bond Returns", Review of Financial Studies 26(7), 1649-1693. https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/26/7/1649/1608115 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Ticker verified: HYG (iShares iBoxx $ High Yield Corporate Bond ETF), issuer BlackRock, launched 2007-04-04, actively trading.

name: Treasury Duration Volatility-Regime Timing
mechanism: Compute TLT's trailing 20-day realized annualized volatility against its own trailing 252-day median. Below median (calm) -> hold long-duration TLT; above median (elevated bond-market stress) -> rotate to short-duration SHY. Re-evaluate monthly. A pure volatility-regime filter on the bond market's own risk, not a curve-slope/momentum signal.
source: Viceira, L.M. (2012), "Bond Risk, Bond Return Volatility, and the Term Structure of Interest Rates", International Journal of Forecasting 28, 97-117. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0169207011000446 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Tickers verified: TLT/SHY (iShares Treasury ETFs), both launched 2002-07-22, actively trading.

name: TIPS-vs-Nominal Breakeven Relative-Momentum Rotation
mechanism: Compute TIP's trailing 3-month total return relative to IEF (a market-implied-inflation-expectations proxy). TIP outperforming IEF (rising breakeven) -> hold TIP; underperforming (falling breakeven) -> hold IEF. Rebalance monthly. Isolates inflation-expectations direction from outright nominal-rate direction, and trades bonds directly (never equities).
source: David Varadi/CSS Analytics, "The Inflation Compass Model" (2026), https://cssanalytics.wordpress.com/2026/07/27/the-inflation-compass-model/; independent replication at Allocate Smartly (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Tickers verified: TIP (iShares TIPS, launched 2003-12-04), IEF (iShares 7-10yr Treasury, launched 2002-07-22), both actively trading.

name: International Government Bond Absolute Momentum
mechanism: Compute BWX's (ex-US developed-market sovereign bonds) trailing 12-month total return. Positive -> hold BWX; negative -> rotate to BIL. Rebalance monthly. Single-asset absolute momentum applied to a foreign-sovereign-debt universe, distinct from any domestic-Treasury/gold/commodity multi-asset momentum already covered.
source: Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen (2013), "Value and Momentum Everywhere", Journal of Finance 68(3), 929-985. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jofi.12021 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Ticker verified: BWX (SPDR Bloomberg International Treasury Bond ETF), issuer State Street, launched 2007-10-02, actively trading.

name: Stock Split Signaling Drift
mechanism: Hold a monthly-rebalanced, equally-weighted basket of U.S. exchange-listed companies that recently announced/completed a 2-for-1-or-greater forward stock split, testing the documented market underreaction to the split as a costly voluntary signal of management confidence.
ruled_out_reason: TOFR (USCF Stock Split ETF, issuer USCF Investments) was liquidated by its issuer in October 2017 -- Board-approved liquidation 2017-09-22, last creation orders 2017-10-10, NYSE Arca trading ceased 2017-10-13, proceeds distributed ~2017-10-20 (per SEC EDGAR). No live successor ETF implementing the same forward-split-signaling mechanism was found.
source: Ikenberry & Ramnath (2002), "Underreaction to Self-Selected News Events: The Case of Stock Splits", Review of Financial Studies 15(2), 489-526. https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/15.2.489

name: De-SPAC Post-Merger Fade
mechanism: SHORT a basket of SPAC and post-merger de-SPAC companies, harvesting documented structural underperformance driven by sponsor promote dilution, warrant overhang, and heavy pre-close redemptions.
ruled_out_reason: SPAK (Defiance Next Gen SPAC Derived ETF, issuer Defiance ETFs) was liquidated -- closed and liquidated after close of business 2022-08-30 (SEC EDGAR Form 497, ETF Series Solutions, 'defiancespakandpsyliquidat.htm'). No live successor ETF implementing the same de-SPAC short-basket mechanism was found.
source: Gahng, Ritter & Zhang (2023), "SPACs", Review of Financial Studies (forthcoming) -- equal-weighted post-merger SPACs returned -11.3% in year 1 vs +19.4% for the CRSP value-weighted market, 2010-2020.

name: Activist 13D Campaign Drift
mechanism: Hold an actively-managed basket that adds a company as soon as a new SEC Schedule 13D activist-intent filing is identified against it (5%+ ownership, stated intent to seek board/operational/financial changes), holding through the campaign to capture the market's slow repricing of expected activist-driven value creation.
ruled_out_reason: ACTV (LeaderShares Activist Leaders ETF, issuer Redwood Investment Management/LeaderShares) was liquidated -- last NYSE Arca trading day 2025-10-24, fund dissolved on/about 2025-10-30 (Redwood's own PR Newswire liquidation announcement). No live successor ETF implementing the same 13D-activist-basket mechanism was found.
source: Brav, Jiang, Partnoy & Thomas (2008), "Hedge Fund Activism, Corporate Governance, and Firm Performance", Journal of Finance 63(4), 1729-1775. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1540-6261.2008.01373.x

name: Free Cash Flow Yield ("Cash Cows") Screen
mechanism: Rank large/mid-cap US stocks by trailing free cash flow yield (FCF / enterprise value) and hold the 100 highest-yielding names, reconstituted quarterly -- the exact Pacer US Cash Cows 100 Index rule.
source: Hackel, Livnat & Rai (2000), "A Free Cash Flow Investment Anomaly", Journal of Accounting, Auditing & Finance 15(1). https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=240540 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Ticker verified: COWZ (Pacer US Cash Cows 100 ETF), issuer Pacer Advisors, inception 2016-12-16, actively trading.

name: Wide-Moat Competitive-Advantage Investing
mechanism: Hold US companies Morningstar's equity-research team rates as having a durable "Wide" Economic Moat, filtered to the cheapest wide-moat names by price-to-fair-value, split into two staggered-reconstituting 40-stock sub-portfolios.
source: Morningstar Wide Moat Focus Index methodology; economic-moat framework in Dorsey, P. (2004), "The Little Book That Builds Wealth", Wiley (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Ticker verified: MOAT (VanEck Morningstar Wide Moat ETF), issuer VanEck, inception 2012-04-24, actively trading (~13 billion USD AUM).

name: Faith-Based Values Screen (Sin-Stock Neglect Discount)
mechanism: Hold the S&P 500 with companies excluded per US Conference of Catholic Bishops guidelines (abortion, contraceptives, embryonic stem-cell research, for-profit weapons), reweighting remaining constituents to track the broad index. Tests whether norm-constrained institutional neglect of excluded 'sin' names creates a return premium the screened index forgoes (a performance-drag test vs. its unscreened parent).
source: Hong & Kacperczyk (2009), "The Price of Sin: The Effects of Social Norms on Markets", Journal of Financial Economics 93(1), 15-36. https://w4.stern.nyu.edu/sternfin/mkacperc/public_html/sin.pdf (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Ticker verified: CATH (Global X S&P 500 Catholic Values ETF), issuer Global X, inception 2016-04-18, actively trading.

name: Employee Satisfaction / Human Capital Factor
mechanism: Rank US large-cap stocks on a human-capital-quality score (employee reviews, satisfaction surveys, workforce-management data via the CIBC/Solactive Human Capital Factor index) and hold the highest-scoring names, reconstituted quarterly.
source: Edmans, A. (2011), "Does the Stock Market Fully Value Intangibles? Employee Satisfaction and Equity Prices", Journal of Financial Economics 101(3), 621-640. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X11000869 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Ticker verified: HAPI (Harbor Human Capital Factor US Large Cap ETF), issuer Harbor Capital Advisors, inception 2022-10-12, actively trading.

name: CBOE SKEW Index Tail-Risk Regime Filter
mechanism: Track a 20-day moving average of the CBOE SKEW Index (^SKEW, pricing far-OTM S&P put crash protection relative to lognormal) against its own 252-day moving average. Fast MA crosses above slow MA (crash-hedging demand rising) -> exit SPY into SHY; re-enter SPY once the fast MA falls back below the slow MA.
source: Mora-Valencia, Rodriguez-Raga & Vanegas (2021), "Skew index: Descriptive analysis, predictive power, and short-term forecast", North American Journal of Economics and Finance 56. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1062940820302370 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Tickers verified via direct Yahoo Finance query 2026-08-29: ^SKEW (CBOE SKEW Index, live), SPY (SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust).

name: Monthly Options-Expiration-Week Drift
mechanism: Buy SPY 4 trading sessions before the ordinary monthly (3rd-Friday) options-expiration Friday, hold through that Friday's close, then exit to cash for the rest of the month. Recurs all 12 months/year (not just the 4 quarterly triple-witching months), attributed to concentrated dealer delta-hedge rebalancing/pinning flows around the largest recurring monthly options rolloff.
source: Johnson & So (2013), "Returns and option activity over the option-expiration week for S&P 100 stocks", Journal of Banking and Finance 37(11), 4226-4240. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0378426613003051 (verified via web search 2026-08-29; also on Quantpedia). Ticker verified: SPY.

name: Nasdaq/S&P Implied-Vol Spread De-Risking Regime
mechanism: Compute the ratio ^VXN/^VIX (Nasdaq-100 vs S&P 500 implied volatility). 20-day MA of the ratio crosses meaningfully above its 252-day MA (tech-specific options fear spiking faster than its trailing norm) -> rotate QQQ into SHY; re-enter QQQ once the ratio's fast MA falls back below its slow MA.
source: Marks & Simon (2017), "Sector Option Implied Volatility Dynamics and Predictability", Journal of Derivatives 25(2), 22-42. https://jod.pm-research.com/content/25/2/22 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Tickers verified via direct Yahoo Finance query 2026-08-29: ^VXN (CBOE NASDAQ-100 Volatility Index, live), QQQ.

name: FINRA Margin Debt Growth Regime
mechanism: Compute trailing 12-month % change in FINRA-published aggregate NYSE member-firm customer margin-debt balances, lagged ~20 trading days for real publication delay. Positive growth (leverage/risk appetite expanding) -> hold SPY; growth crosses below zero -> exit to cash.
source: Beluska & Vojtko (2025), "Can Margin Debt Help Predict SPY's Growth & Bear Markets?", QuantPedia/SSRN. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5198812 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Data source verified real: FINRA Margin Statistics, finra.org/rules-guidance/key-topics/margin-accounts/margin-statistics, monthly, from Jan 1997. IMPLEMENTATION: src/mining/batch5/margin_debt_growth_regime.py (a thin adapter over mining.signals.finra_margin_debt_risk_on_series) + scripts/run_margin_debt_mining.py, scored under the ABI-1 construction; scripts/run_batch3_mining.py wires the same mining.signals functions into a separate per-trade construction.

name: AAII Cash Allocation Contrarian Signal
mechanism: Compute AAII's monthly Asset Allocation Survey cash-allocation percentage as a z-score against its own trailing 5-year mean/stdev. Elevated cash allocation (crowd retreat to cash) -> go long SPY (contrarian-bullish); historic-low cash allocation (fully invested) -> reduce/exit to cash.
source: AAII Asset Allocation Survey, published monthly since Nov 1987, aaii.com/assetallocationsurvey; contrarian interpretation in AAII's own published research (verified via web search 2026-08-29). EXTERNAL-DATA CAVEAT: the full historical survey series is not freely, reliably scriptable (AAII's public site does not expose a simple bulk CSV/API the way FRED does), and it is BLOCKED: AAII's own robots.txt disallows automated access to /files/* (verified 2026-09-15), a site-policy block this pipeline does not bypass, not merely a build-effort gap. Status stays eligible: the block is on data access, not on the mechanism.

name: Money Market Fund Flow Risk-Off Signal
mechanism: Compute a 3-month rate-of-change z-score of the Fed's Retail Money Market Fund assets series (H.6 release, FRED ticker RMFSL -- fixed USD 1 NAV, so % change is a direct net-flow proxy). Inflows accelerate sharply (flight to safety) -> reduce/exit SPY; growth decelerates/reverses -> re-enter SPY.
source: Warther, V.A. (1995), "Aggregate mutual fund flows and security returns", Journal of Financial Economics 39(2-3), 209-235. https://sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0304405X95008272 (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Data source verified real and freely downloadable: FRED series RMFSL (fred.stlouisfed.org/series/RMFSL), monthly, from 1980. DATA NOTE: FRED series are NOT yfinance symbols, so data_pipeline.fetch_ohlc cannot fetch them. IMPLEMENTATION: src/mining/batch5/money_market_fund_flow_riskoff.py (a thin adapter over mining.signals.money_market_risk_on_series) + scripts/run_money_market_mining.py, using the point-in-time FRED API (mining.external_data.fetch_fred_series_point_in_time; a free API key is required). METHODOLOGY NOTE: the z-score uses an expanding window over the full RMFSL history (from 1973), so by SPY's 1993 inception it already carries about 20 years of pre-inception burn-in, and that long early history dominates the normalization of every later reading. See money_market_fund_flow_riskoff_bounded_burnin for the bounded-burn-in variant.

name: Fed Net Liquidity Regime
mechanism: Compute Net Liquidity = Fed total assets (weekly H.4.1, FRED WALCL) minus Treasury General Account (FRED WTREGEN) minus Overnight Reverse Repo (FRED RRPONTSYD). Above its own 13-week MA (liquidity expanding, e.g. QE or RRP drawdown) -> hold SPY; below (liquidity contracting, e.g. QT or TGA rebuild) -> reduce/exit to cash. Rebalance weekly.
source: Howell, M.J. (2020), "Capital Wars: The Rise of Global Liquidity", Macmillan; ongoing tracking at capitalwars.substack.com (verified via web search 2026-08-29). Data sources verified real and free: FRED WALCL/WTREGEN/RRPONTSYD (fred.stlouisfed.org). Same DATA NOTE as money_market_fund_flow_riskoff above: FRED series are not fetched through data_pipeline.fetch_ohlc. IMPLEMENTATION: src/mining/batch5/fed_net_liquidity_regime.py (a thin adapter over mining.signals.fed_net_liquidity_risk_on_series) + scripts/run_fed_net_liquidity_mining.py, using the point-in-time FRED API (a free API key is required). Built on SPY only (the catalog also lists QQQ, but the mechanism text never exercises it; see fed_net_liquidity_regime_qqq for the QQQ variant).

name: Money Market Fund Flow Risk-Off Signal (bounded pre-inception burn-in)
mechanism: SAME mechanism as money_market_fund_flow_riskoff (3-month rate-of-change z-score of FRED RMFSL, expanding-window normalization) EXCEPT the raw RMFSL input is capped to mining.constants.MAX_PRE_INCEPTION_BURN_IN_YEARS years before SPY's own first tradeable date before the expanding z-score is computed. Motivation: the uncapped expanding window in money_market_fund_flow_riskoff, fed RMFSL's full 1973 history, carries decades of pre-SPY-inception burn-in by 1993, so that long early history dominates the normalization of every later reading; the cap bounds it. This is a different signal DEFINITION (what the strategy computes), not a re-evaluation of the same one, so it is a new family_id paying its own trial rather than an edit to the original.
source: Same underlying source as money_market_fund_flow_riskoff (Warther 1995; FRED RMFSL, fred.stlouisfed.org/series/RMFSL). The burn-in cap itself is a methodology choice, not a literature citation -- see mining.constants.MAX_PRE_INCEPTION_BURN_IN_YEARS. Implementation: src/mining/batch5/money_market_fund_flow_riskoff_bounded_burnin.py + scripts/run_money_market_bounded_burnin_mining.py.

name: Fed Net Liquidity Regime (QQQ variant)
mechanism: IDENTICAL mechanism to fed_net_liquidity_regime (Net Liquidity = FRED WALCL minus WTREGEN minus RRPONTSYD, above/below its own 13-week MA), traded on QQQ instead of SPY. This builds the QQQ variant that the original catalog entry's tickers field named but its mechanism text never actually exercised. A distinct family_id, not a pooled/rotation family with the SPY sibling -- the mechanism gives no rule for choosing or rotating between the two underlyings, and this pipeline pools multi-ticker tests into one trial only when a stated pooling/rotation rule exists.
source: Same underlying source as fed_net_liquidity_regime (Howell 2020; FRED WALCL/WTREGEN/RRPONTSYD). Implementation: src/mining/batch5/fed_net_liquidity_regime_qqq.py + scripts/run_fed_net_liquidity_qqq_mining.py. Benchmarked against SPY (not QQQ) per abi1_driver.evaluate_family's own documented contract -- ABI-1's benchmark is the market reference (SPY) system-wide, not whatever is traded, so this family's DSR stays comparable to every other family's under the shared DAILY_SR_VARIANCE/ABI1_N_TRIALS calibration. QQQ execution cost comes from a bid/ask sample taken after the regular session closed rather than during it, a disclosed limitation of the cost model.

name: Post-Opex Gamma-Release Leverage Window, Pooled (11 Select Sector SPDRs)
mechanism: Dealer delta-hedge rebalancing around the largest recurring monthly options rolloff (ordinary 3rd-Friday expiration) measurably pins/alters underlying closing prices into expiration (Ni, Pearson & Poteshman 2005, JFE). That pressure is mechanically tied to the expiring contracts' gamma; once they expire, the block of gamma dealers were hedging rolls off (the 'gamma release'/'gamma unpin' practitioners describe) and Klemkosky (1978) and Chiang (2014) independently document a short-term reversal in the days/week immediately following expiration that partially offsets the pre-expiration move. This family holds a SYNTHETIC 2x Reg-T-margin-financed position in each of the 11 Select Sector SPDRs ONLY during the trading week immediately after expiration -- flat the rest of the month -- amplifying with leverage a literature-documented single-week effect enough to clear trading costs, pooled across the same 11-member panel as vol_managed_sector_spdr_pooled for statistical power.
source: Ni, S.X., Pearson, N.D. & Poteshman, A.M. (2005), "Stock price clustering on option expiration dates", Journal of Financial Economics 78(1), 49-87, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfineco.2004.08.005 (verified via web search 2026-09-17: dealer hedge-rebalancing measurably alters expiration-date closing prices, ~16.5bp average). Klemkosky, R.C. (1978), "The Impact of Option Expirations on Stock Prices", Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 13(3), 507-518, https://doi.org/10.2307/2330155 (verified via web search 2026-09-17: 14 expiration dates 1975-76, -1% the week before expiration, +0.4% the week after -- the direct precedent for this family's post-opex window). Chiang, C.-H. (2014), "Stock returns on option expiration dates: Price impact of liquidity trading", Journal of Empirical Finance 28, 273-290, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jempfin.2014.07.001 (verified via web search 2026-09-17: expiration-date return drop followed by short-term reversal). 'Gamma release/unpin' terminology is practitioner usage (SpotGamma and similar dealer-positioning literature), disclosed as such -- not itself a peer-reviewed source, only the causal-mechanism label; the three citations above carry the actual statistical evidence. Tickers: the 11 Select Sector SPDRs, same real, liquid, decades-old funds (nine since 1998-12-16/22, XLRE since 2015-10-07/08, XLC since 2018-06-18/19) already verified for vol_managed_sector_spdr_pooled (data/mining/panel/sector_spdr_11_membership.json). Implementation: src/mining/signals.py::post_opex_window_dates + src/mining/batch5/post_opex_gamma_release_leverage_window.py, each with its own tests. A rough in-sample backtest can be run through the generic engine (mining.backtest_engine.run_backtest); that is not the official ABI-1 scoring path. The cost basis is the underlying SPDR's own quoted spread rather than a leveraged product's.
distinctness_note: vs. vol_managed_sector_spdr_pooled (SAME 11-member panel): that family's signal is each fund's own trailing realized variance against an expanding median, a continuous price-derived regime signal. This family's signal is a fixed CALENDAR EVENT (the public 3rd-Friday options-expiration date) with no price input into the entry/exit decision at all -- reusing the same liquid panel with a genuinely different signal is an established pattern already in this catalog (see sector_same_month_seasonality's own note against this identical sibling). Not a leveraged wrapper around the same realized-variance switch: this candidate's SIGNAL itself differs in kind (event/calendar vs. price/variance), not merely its wrapper, and the leverage here is a SYNTHETIC margin-financed position (avoiding the thin liquidity of real leveraged sector products) rather than a real 3x fund. vs. monthly_opex_week_drift (SPY): that family enters 4 sessions BEFORE expiry and exits AT expiry's close (Johnson & So 2013's pre-expiration pinning window); this family enters AT expiry and exits a week AFTER -- the opposite side of the same recurring event, pooled across 11 sector funds with 2x synthetic leverage instead of one unlevered SPY position. The two families' entry/exit dates are pinned never to overlap as holding days (test_post_opex_window_dates_never_shares_a_date_with_monthly_opex_dates_pre_window). vs. long_treasury_3x_fomc_window_drift (TMF, status eligible): closest sibling in SHAPE (a leveraged product held only in a short window around a recurring calendar event, flat otherwise) but a different asset class, event, and literature.
directional_rationale: Klemkosky (1978) and Chiang (2014) both report a modest positive reversal in the days/week following expiration (Klemkosky: +0.4% the week after, vs. -1% the week before) -- too small to clear round-trip costs unlevered, which is the entire reason this family tests a 2x synthetic wrapper rather than the unlevered SPY window that monthly_opex_week_drift covers. Evaluate on time-matched excess over SPY across the pooled post-opex windows, not raw Sharpe.
rule_pseudocode: For each T in POOL independently, using T's own real auto-adjusted daily calendar: EXPIRY = the month's 3rd-Friday option-expiration session (weekday==Friday, day in [15,21], exactly one per month). SIGNAL: signal(EXPIRY)=True (entry); the engine's next-open convention fills the SYNTHETIC 2x position at the first post-opex session. EXIT: signal fires exit=True at the close of the session hold_trading_days_after_opex=5 actual trading sessions after EXPIRY. A month whose expiry falls too close to the end of available history for that exit session to exist is skipped entirely, never truncated (mining.signals.post_opex_window_dates). TRADED instrument: a SYNTHETIC 2x Reg-T-margin position built off T's own real Close via data_pipeline.build_synthetic_leveraged(leverage=2.0, annual_expense_ratio=0.0, financing_spread=0.0100), OHLC-shaped via synthetic_ohlc_from_close (Open_t=Close_{t-1}, High=Low=Close -- a daily-reset instrument has no real intraday range). One trade per (ticker, month) pair with a resolvable exit; trades of all 11 pool members concatenated into one sample, scored as ONE trial.

name: Earnings-Reaction Opening-Range Breakout with PEAD Hold
mechanism: On the trading day immediately following a pre-market or post-market earnings release that produces an opening gap of at least 3% in the surprise direction, measure the high/low of the first 15 minutes of RTH (09:30-09:45 ET) as the earnings-reaction range. Enter long (short for a negative-surprise gap-down) on a break above (below) that 15-minute range's high (low), confirming the market actually digested the news constructively intraday rather than gapping and fading. Hold as a multi-day post-earnings-announcement-drift swing position, exiting after a max hold of 20 trading days or a trailing stop, rather than closing same-day.
source: Ball, R. & Brown, P. (1968), "An Empirical Evaluation of Accounting Income Numbers," Journal of Accounting Research (foundational PEAD documentation; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post%E2%80%93earnings-announcement_drift, verified via web search 2026-08-31); practitioner entry mechanics from Wagner, Deron / Morpheus Trading Group, "Gap Trading Strategy: 5 Top Ways to Buy Stocks Gapping Up from Earnings," https://morpheustrading.com/blog/gap-trading-strategy/ (describes multi-day, 5-15-session PEAD gap holds entered on an intraday breakout above the post-gap range high with volume confirmation; verified via web search 2026-08-31). Ticker verified: NVDA (NVIDIA Corp., NASDAQ, IPO Jan 1999) confirmed trading today at ~USD 217.55 (Investing.com, verified via web search 2026-08-31).
distinctness_note: Not a re-parameterization of pead_earnings_surprise_drift (daily-bar, eligible): the daily version enters at the earnings-day close with no intraday confirmation of whether the market held the gap; this version's trigger is a specific 15-minute post-open range on the reaction day itself -- a construct that only exists at minute-bar resolution and screens out gaps that reverse within 15 minutes. Also distinct from qqq_tqqq_orb (ruled_out): anchored to a real earnings catalyst rather than a fixed daily open, mechanism-general across any liquid earnings-reporting stock rather than QQQ/TQQQ, and holds up to 20 trading days for the drift rather than exiting same-day.
pooling_note: mechanism-general (applies to any liquid stock with a qualifying earnings gap), intended for pooling across a wide universe of real earnings events in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism, similar to the existing pead_earnings_surprise_drift pooling); NVDA/AAPL/MSFT here are placeholder liquid representatives for the first single-ticker test.

name: Anchored VWAP Reclaim Continuation
mechanism: Anchor a volume-weighted average price calculation at the most recent significant multi-week swing low (identified on daily bars). When intraday price crosses back above that running anchored-VWAP line on a 5-minute bar whose volume exceeds 1.3x the average 5-minute volume for that time of day (confirming a real reclaim, not a wick-through), enter long at the close of that confirmation bar. Hold as a multi-day swing (up to 20 trading days) as long as each day's close stays above the (continuously updating) anchored VWAP, exiting on the first daily close back below it or at the max hold.
source: Shannon, B. (2008), "Technical Analysis Using Multiple Timeframes", and Shannon, B. (2023), "Maximum Trading Gains With Anchored VWAP" -- Shannon pioneered anchored-VWAP swing-trading technique via Alphatrends.net since 2003 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Shannon, https://alphatrends.net/trading-books/). Verified via web search 2026-08-31. Ticker verified: SPY, SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust, launched by State Street Jan 22 1993 (the first US ETF), trades on NYSE Arca, still the world's most heavily traded ETF in 2026 (~54.94 billion USD avg daily volume).
distinctness_note: Not a re-parameterization of qqq_tqqq_orb -- there is no fixed opening-range window at all; the entry trigger is a volume-confirmed cross back above a VWAP line anchored to a prior swing low (an anchor point plus a running intraday average, not a session-open range), and the multi-day hold is trend-following continuation logic rather than a same-day breakout play. Also distinct from every daily-bar trend/rotation family in the catalog because the entry timing depends on which specific intraday 5-minute bar actually reclaims the anchored VWAP with volume confirmation -- a signal daily bars cannot resolve, since the anchored VWAP itself is a continuously-updating intraday-derived series, not a daily indicator. NOTE: near-duplicate variants of this anchored-VWAP reclaim (a 5-min-bar variant with no time-of-day-adjusted volume baseline; a long-only daily-close-confirmation variant) are not catalogued as separate family_ids, under the pipeline's rule against multiplying near-identical trials.
pooling_note: mechanism-general (the anchored-VWAP-reclaim rule applies to any liquid, trending index ETF or stock), intended for pooling across a wide universe of liquid equities/ETFs in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism); SPY is the first single-ticker, most-liquid proxy.

name: Volatility-Contraction-Pattern Breakout with Intraday Volume Confirmation
mechanism: After a stock forms a multi-week volatility contraction pattern (at least 2 successively shallower pullbacks converging toward a pivot high, e.g. 15% then 8%), watch the first 30 minutes of RTH (09:30-10:00 ET) on the breakout day: enter long if price breaks above the VCP pivot high AND the opening-30-minute bar's volume already exceeds 50% of the stock's 20-day average full-day volume (a real-time volume-surge confirmation that requires intraday minute-bar volume, not an end-of-day total). Hold as a multi-week trend-continuation swing (target a multiple of the contraction's measured risk, or trail a moving-average stop), max hold 20 trading days.
source: Minervini, Mark (2013), "Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard" (VCP pattern origin); rule detail verified via TraderLion, "Mastering the Volatility Contraction Pattern," https://traderlion.com/technical-analysis/volatility-contraction-pattern/ (describes the successive-contraction structure and the 40-50%-above-average intraday volume-surge breakout confirmation; verified via web search 2026-08-31). Ticker verified: TSLA (Tesla Inc., NASDAQ, IPO June 2010) confirmed trading today at ~USD 348.75, market cap ~1.37 trillion USD (CNBC/Yahoo Finance, verified via web search 2026-08-31).
distinctness_note: Not a re-parameterization of anything in the excluded list, including qqq_tqqq_orb: the entry trigger requires a prior multi-week structural consolidation pattern (not present in any daily or intraday catalog entry) plus a real-time intraday volume-surge confirmation that only a minute-bar feed can measure (comparing opening-30-minute volume against a full-day average, not just a price range); the hold is a multi-week trend-continuation swing (up to 20 days) rather than qqq_tqqq_orb's same-day momentum scalp on a fixed leveraged-ETF pair, and this mechanism applies broadly to growth-stock breakouts rather than a fixed index/leverage relationship.
pooling_note: mechanism-general (VCP breakout detection and volume confirmation apply to any liquid stock exhibiting the contraction structure), intended for pooling across a wide universe in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism); TSLA/NVDA/AAPL here are placeholder liquid representatives, not the intended final universe.

name: Gap-and-Go Momentum Continuation
mechanism: At the 9:30 ET opening print, compute the raw overnight gap = (open - prior regular-session close) / prior regular-session close. If the gap is >=2% (long) or <=-2% (short) and first-15-minute (9:30-9:45 ET) cumulative volume is at least 2x the trailing 20-day average 15-minute opening volume, and price never trades back through the exact opening print during that 9:30-9:45 confirmation window, enter in the gap direction at 9:45 ET. This is a multi-day trend position, not a same-day exit: hold using a 3x-ATR(14-day) trailing stop, maximum hold 20 trading days.
source: Plastun, A., Sibande, X., Gupta, R., & Wohar, M.E. (2020), "Price Gap Anomaly in the US Stock Market: The Whole Story", North American Journal of Economics and Finance (SSRN 3461283, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3461283) -- finds prices tend to continue in the gap's direction following a gap day (1928-2018 DJI/S&P500/NASDAQ data), and a gap-based trading simulation beat a random benchmark. Baniya, S. (2024), "Rough Gaps Exist? Opening Gaps Helps To Surge Returns in Swing and Intraday Trading", SSRN 4834097 -- studies opening-gap signals specifically framed for swing holding periods, not just intraday. Both verified via web search 2026-08-31. Ticker verified via web search 2026-08-31: NVDA (Nasdaq) is the world's largest company by market cap (~5.2 trillion USD as of Aug 2026), one of the most heavily traded stocks globally, actively trading today; AMZN and MSFT independently confirmed Nasdaq-listed, actively trading, multi-trillion-dollar market caps as of Aug 2026.
distinctness_note: Not a re-parameterization of qqq_tqqq_orb: that family defines a computed opening-RANGE (high/low over the first N minutes) and enters on a breakout of that range with a same-day exit; this candidate's trigger is the raw GAP MAGNITUDE vs. the prior close plus a 'does-not-fade-through-the-open' confirmation, and its exit is a multi-day ATR trail (max 20 trading days), never same-day. It also differs from overnight_drift (daily-bar), which trades every single overnight session unconditionally on a daily-bar buy-close/sell-open mechanic with no gap-size filter, no intraday confirmation, and no multi-day hold. This mechanism genuinely requires minute-bar precision: the entry gate depends on price never crossing back through the exact opening print during a specific 15-minute window, which cannot be derived from daily OHLC.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general (any liquid, news-driven stock can gap), intended for pooling across a wide universe in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism) rather than one family per ticker.

name: Earnings Gap Continuation with Intraday Confirmation
mechanism: On the first regular session following a company's earnings release, measure the exact opening gap at 9:30 ET vs. the prior regular-session close. If the gap direction matches the sign of the earnings surprise (actual EPS vs. consensus) and gap magnitude is >=3%, require price to hold within 1% of the opening print through the first 30 minutes (9:30-10:00 ET) as a confirmation bar -- i.e., no immediate intraday fade back through the pre-earnings prior close. Enter in the gap direction at 10:00 ET. Hold for up to 20 trading days (the standard PEAD drift window), exiting early only on a full retracement below the opening print's level.
source: Bernard, V.L. & Thomas, J.K. (1989), "Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Delayed Price Response or Risk Premium?", Journal of Accounting Research, 27, 1-36 (verified via web search 2026-08-31, IDEAS/RePEc and Semantic Scholar listings) -- the landmark study establishing that earnings-surprise-driven price drift is a real, persistent, non-risk-based anomaly (positive SUE-decile spread in 41 of 48 quarters, 1974-1985). Ticker verified via web search 2026-08-31: AAPL, AMZN, MSFT all confirmed Nasdaq-listed, actively trading in 2026 with multi-trillion-dollar market caps, and all report quarterly earnings with reliably large, liquid opening-print reactions.
distinctness_note: Distinct from pead_earnings_surprise_drift, which is a daily-bar candidate keyed on the surprise magnitude and a next-day-close-or-later entry with no intraday confirmation. This candidate's entry gate is load-bearing on minute-bar data: it requires that price does NOT fade back through the prior close within a specific 30-minute post-open window, a fact that only exists at intraday resolution -- a daily-bar version cannot distinguish 'gapped and held' from 'gapped and round-tripped back to unchanged by the close.' Holding period is explicitly multi-day (up to 20 trading days, matching the published PEAD drift window), not a same-day trade.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general (applies to any liquid stock with a qualifying earnings gap), intended for pooling across the same real S&P 500 + NASDAQ 100 ticker universe this pipeline already built for pead_earnings_surprise_drift, in a later wider test (one pooled trial per mechanism).

name: Anchored VWAP Swing-Pivot Reclaim/Loss Breakout
mechanism: Identify the most recent significant swing pivot on the daily chart (a rolling 20-trading-day high or low) and anchor a volume-weighted average price line to that exact pivot session, recomputing it cumulatively from real minute-bar trade prints starting at that session's open. Enter long the first time the daily close reclaims (moves back above) that anchored VWAP line on a session whose actual intraday volume (summed from minute bars) is at least 1.5x the 20-day average daily volume -- mirror short entries on an AVWAP-loss breakdown from a swing-high anchor. Hold the resulting trend-continuation position for up to 20 trading days, exiting early on a second daily close back through the AVWAP line.
source: Brian Shannon (2008), "Technical Analysis Using Multiple Timeframes", Fibonacci Trading LLC; Brian Shannon (2023), "Maximum Trading Gains With Anchored VWAP". Shannon is documented as the originator/pioneer of the Anchored VWAP methodology, first using it in 2003 (TrendSpider, "Anchored VWAP: What It Is, How It Works, and How to Use It", https://trendspider.com/learning-center/anchored-vwap-trading-strategies/). Verified via web search 2026-08-31. Ticker verified: SPY (SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust) launched 1993 by State Street Global Advisors as the first U.S.-listed ETF, ~650 billion USD AUM, actively exchange-traded today (Yahoo Finance/Motley Fool, Aug 2026).
distinctness_note: This is a SHORT-SIDE-CAPABLE variant of anchored_vwap_reclaim_continuation, kept as a separate family because it explicitly adds a mirrored short-entry rule (AVWAP-loss breakdown from a swing-high anchor) and uses DAILY-close confirmation (not a 5-minute bar) plus a heavier daily-volume confirmation -- a genuinely different confirmation timeframe and directionality, not a cosmetic rename. Not a re-parameterization of qqq_tqqq_orb (fixed opening-range breakout, no VWAP element, same-day exit) nor of long_mean_reversion_ibs_rsi2 (a fixed-lookback oscillator, not an intraday-reconstructed volume-weighted line).
pooling_note: Mechanism-general, intended for pooling across a wide universe of liquid large-cap stocks/ETFs in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism); SPY/QQQ/AAPL are three initial liquid representatives, with SPY as the first single-ticker test.

name: Earnings-Reaction Anchored VWAP Reclaim
mechanism: On the first full trading session after a company's earnings report (the reaction day), anchor a volume-weighted average price line to that session's exact opening print, computed from real minute-bar trade prints starting at the open. Over the following up to 10 trading days, enter long the first time the daily close reclaims that earnings-anchored VWAP after having closed below it at least once, provided the reclaim session's volume is at least 1.3x the 20-day average -- signaling that institutional buyers who built a position on the earnings gap are defending their average cost basis rather than sitting underwater. Exit on a daily close back below the AVWAP line or after a maximum hold of 15 trading days, whichever comes first.
source: Brian Shannon, alphatrends.net, "How To Use The Anchored VWAP (AVWAP)" (https://alphatrends.net/archives/2017/12/use-anchored-vwap-avwap/) and "Maximum Trading Gains With Anchored VWAP" (2023) -- explicitly documents anchoring AVWAP to earnings-report/gap sessions to track institutional cost basis. Underlying drift rationale grounded in Bernard, V.L. & Thomas, J.K. (1989), "Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Delayed Price Response or Risk Premium?", Journal of Accounting Research, 27, 1-36 (https://ideas.repec.org/a/bla/joares/v27y1989ip1-36.html). Verified via web search 2026-08-31. Ticker verified: AAPL trades on NASDAQ, a top-3 holding in both SPY and QQQ, actively traded today with reliable earnings-date and minute-bar coverage (multiple 2026 sources); MSFT and NVDA independently confirmed as highly liquid NASDAQ mega-caps actively trading in 2026.
distinctness_note: Distinct from the existing daily-bar pead_earnings_surprise_drift, which enters on a fixed calendar day after earnings and simply holds through the drift window: this candidate's entry trigger is a minute-bar-reconstructed AVWAP reclaim that can fire on any of several days after the reaction (or never fire at all), and the anchor line itself must be built from real intraday trade prints starting at the exact reaction-session open -- a daily-bar backtest cannot produce this anchor or trigger. Also distinct from qqq_tqqq_orb (range breakout, no VWAP) and long_mean_reversion_ibs_rsi2 (oscillator, not an event-anchored volume-weighted line).
pooling_note: Mechanism-general and catalyst-triggered, following the same pooling precedent already used for pead_earnings_surprise_drift -- intended to be pooled across a wide universe of tickers with real earnings events in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism); AAPL/MSFT/NVDA are three liquid mega-cap representatives with reliable minute-bar and earnings-date coverage, AAPL as the first single-ticker test.

name: Anchored VWAP Band-Extension Mean Reversion
mechanism: Anchor a volume-weighted average price line and its +-2 standard-deviation bands (all computed from real minute-bar trade prints, not daily closes) to the most recent 20-trading-day swing pivot -- the same anchor convention as the reclaim/breakout mechanism above, but used for the opposite trading logic. When the daily close extends to or beyond the 2-standard-deviation band, enter a counter-trend mean-reversion position only if the extension session's final 30 minutes (measured from minute bars) shows price decelerating back toward the AVWAP line rather than accelerating further away from it. Exit on a touch of the AVWAP centerline or after a maximum hold of 10 trading days, whichever comes first.
source: TrendSpider, "VWAP with St. Dev Bands" (https://help.trendspider.com/kb/indicators/vwap-with-st-dot-dev-bands) and GoCharting, "VWAP Bands: Standard Deviation Trading Strategy" (https://gocharting.com/docs/orderflow/vwapbands), documenting +-1/2/3 standard-deviation bands around an anchored VWAP as a mean-reversion/extension-fade technique, extending Brian Shannon's Anchored VWAP framework (Maximum Trading Gains With Anchored VWAP, 2023). Verified via web search 2026-08-31. Tickers verified: SPY (1993, State Street SPDR, S&P 500, ~650 billion USD AUM) and QQQ (launched March 10, 1999, Invesco, NASDAQ-100, ~375 billion USD AUM), both actively exchange-traded today; IWM (launched May 22, 2000, BlackRock/iShares, tracks Russell 2000, currently trading ~USD 298 a share, Aug 2026).
distinctness_note: Opposite economic logic from the reclaim/continuation AVWAP families above (fades an extension away from the AVWAP rather than trading a reclaim WITH it), so it is not a cosmetic parameter variant of those candidates. Also distinct from long_mean_reversion_ibs_rsi2 (a fixed daily oscillator, not a volume-weighted event-anchored band) and from qqq_tqqq_orb (range breakout, no VWAP). The band values require real minute-bar volume-weighted reconstruction from the anchor session plus a minute-bar deceleration check in the final 30 minutes of the extension session -- neither can be derived from daily bars.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general, intended for pooling across a wide universe of liquid index ETFs/large-cap names in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism); SPY/QQQ/IWM are three liquid index-ETF representatives, with SPY as the first single-ticker test.

name: Earnings Reaction: Delayed-Entry PEAD
mechanism: On the regular session in which a stock's earnings surprise is first digested by the market (the same day for a before-open report, the next morning for an after-close report), skip the first five 15-minute bars after the 09:30 ET open -- Ogneva, Xia & Ye (2021) show this ~75-minute window is dominated by overreaction/reversal, not the real signal. At 10:45 ET, measure the cumulative reaction return from the open through that point; if it sits in the extreme top or bottom quintile of same-stock historical reaction returns, enter long or short at the 10:45 bar's close. Hold up to 10 trading days to capture the classic Bernard & Thomas (1989) post-earnings drift, which the delayed entry is specifically timed to avoid buying into before it has separated from the noisy opening reaction.
source: Ogneva, M., Xia, J., & Ye, T. (2021), "Market-wide Spillovers from Individual Firms' Earnings Announcements", SSRN working paper (abstract_id=3837800), https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3837800 -- documents a reversal-dominated pattern over the first five 15-minute intervals after an announcement-reaction open, with genuine continuation only emerging in later intervals; underlying drift target is Bernard, V. & Thomas, J. (1989), "Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Delayed Price Response or Risk Premium?", Journal of Accounting Research, 27(Supplement), 1-36 (foundational, real, widely-cited PEAD paper). Ticker verified: AAPL is Apple Inc., NASDAQ-listed since its Dec 12, 1980 IPO, actively trading today (all verified via web search 2026-08-31).
distinctness_note: Distinct from pead_earnings_surprise_drift (which holds the daily post-earnings drift starting at the next raw daily close/open with no intraday precision): this candidate's entry trigger is a specific minute-bar-measured cumulative return through 10:45 ET, deliberately built to skip a documented 75-minute overreaction window that a daily bar cannot see at all -- the intraday timing IS the mechanism, not a re-labeling of the daily signal. Genuinely multi-day (up to 10 days), not a same-day/day-trade candidate.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general, intended for pooling across a wide universe in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism) -- like pead_earnings_surprise_drift, this fires on any stock reporting earnings, not one ticker; AAPL/MSFT/JPM are liquid first-test representatives only.

name: Time-of-Day Return Continuation
mechanism: Heston, Korajczyk & Sadka (2010, Journal of Finance) document that a stock's return in a specific 30-minute clock-time bucket exhibits significant positive autocorrelation with its OWN return in that same clock-time bucket on future trading days, a pattern that persists for at least 20 and up to roughly 40 trading days and is not explained by liquidity or bid-ask bounce. Each day, measure the 09:30-10:00 ET bar's return; if it falls in the extreme (top or bottom) tercile of that same bucket's trailing 20-day history, enter long or short at the 10:00 ET bar close. Hold for up to 15 trading days, exiting at the SAME 09:30-10:00 ET bucket's close on the exit day to stay consistent with the clock-time-matched signal the effect is built on.
source: Heston, S.L., Korajczyk, R.A., & Sadka, R. (2010), "Intraday Patterns in the Cross-Section of Stock Returns", The Journal of Finance, 65(4), 1369-1407 (top-3 finance journal; also on SSRN abstract_id=1107590 and arXiv:1005.3535) -- finds return continuation at half-hour intervals that are exact multiples of a trading day, lasting at least 40 trading days. Ticker verified: SPY is the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust, issued by State Street, listed on NYSE Arca since Jan 22, 1993, still one of the world's most actively traded ETFs today (verified via web search 2026-08-31).
distinctness_note: Not a re-parameterization of anything excluded: no daily-bar candidate in this catalog uses a specific intraday clock-time bucket's own return as its signal -- this requires genuine minute-bar (30-minute-bar) measurement that a daily OHLC bar structurally cannot provide, and the holding period (up to 15-20 days) is directly sized to the paper's own documented decay horizon, making it inherently swing-shaped rather than same-day.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general, intended for pooling across a wide universe in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism) -- the paper's finding is a broad cross-sectional effect, not specific to SPY; SPY is the single best liquid first-test representative given its long, clean minute-bar history.

name: NR7-Conditioned Opening Range Breakout, Multi-Day Trend Continuation
mechanism: Require yesterday's daily range (high minus low) to be the narrowest of the trailing 7 sessions (Crabel's NR7 volatility-contraction precondition) before considering a trade today. Measure the opening range as the high/low of the first 30 minutes after the 09:30 ET open; if the next 5-minute bar closes beyond that range, enter long (on an upside break) or short (on a downside break) at that confirmation bar's close. Unlike a same-day ORB scalp, hold the position as a trend-initiation swing trade for up to 10 trading days (or a trailing-stop exit), on Crabel's own finding that NR7-conditioned opening-range breakouts show materially stronger multi-day follow-through than unconditioned breakouts.
source: Crabel, T. (1990), "Day Trading with Short-Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout", Traders Press -- the original source for both the Narrow Range (NR4/NR7) volatility-contraction pattern and the opening-range-breakout entry, and Crabel's own documented finding that an NR7-conditioned breakout can signal direction for the next few hours, the trading day, and potentially a multi-day move; corroborated by multiple independent practitioner writeups with backtested statistics (e.g. quantifiedstrategies.com "NR7 Trading Strategy", tradingstrategiesdaily.com "The NR7ID"). Ticker verified: IWM is the iShares Russell 2000 ETF, issued by BlackRock, launched May 22, 2000, actively trading today at a real, current market price (verified via web search 2026-08-31).
distinctness_note: This is an ORB-shaped candidate, so it is checked explicitly against qqq_tqqq_orb's ruled_out_reason: qqq_tqqq_orb enters on a raw, unconditioned 5-minute opening-range breakout on QQQ/TQQQ and exits at the SAME day's close (a day-trade scalp, excluded because the Zarattini/Aziz authors' own multi-provider study shows the result is feed-fragile). This candidate is a DIFFERENT confirmation rule (adds Crabel's NR7 volatility-contraction precondition, absent from the Zarattini/Aziz mechanism, and uses a 30-minute opening range plus a separate 5-minute confirmation bar rather than a single 5-minute range) AND a completely different exit/holding-period logic (multi-day trend continuation, up to 10 days, vs. same-day close-out) on a different first-test instrument (IWM, not QQQ/TQQQ) -- a genuinely different mechanism family, not a cosmetic re-parameterization, and not a re-test of the same published day-trade strategy.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general, intended for pooling across a wide universe in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism) -- an NR7-conditioned opening range breakout is not specific to one instrument; IWM is the single best liquid first-test representative given its higher baseline volatility and clean multi-decade minute-bar-compatible history.

name: Closing-Auction Deviation Reversal
mechanism: In the final 5 minutes before the 16:00 ET close, compute the deviation between the eventual closing-auction print and the last pre-close continuous-market quote/VWAP from minute bars in that window. Bogousslavsky & Muravyev (2023) show this deviation is often economically large and mean-reverts by about 85% by the next session; when the deviation exceeds a threshold (in bps), enter a position the OPPOSITE direction of the deviation (fade it) at the next session's open. Manage the exit adaptively over up to 5 subsequent trading days -- closing early once price has retraced the estimated gap, or at the day-5 cap -- rather than mechanically selling at the very next daily open the way a flat overnight-drift rule would.
source: Bogousslavsky, V., & Muravyev, D. (2023), "Who Trades at the Close? Implications for Price Discovery and Liquidity", Journal of Financial Markets, 66, 100852. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3485840 -- documents that closing-auction price deviations from the pre-close quote are economically large and reverse at a coefficient of -0.85 (85% reversed) by the next morning, and that this closing-auction volume is increasingly driven by indexing/ETF flow. Ticker verified: SPY is the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust, the ETF class the paper itself identifies as most exposed to this closing-auction-driven pressure, confirmed actively trading today (verified via web search 2026-08-31).
distinctness_note: Distinct from the daily-bar overnight_drift family, which unconditionally holds close-to-open every session with no selectivity: this candidate only enters when a minute-bar-measured mispricing signal (the gap between the last pre-close quote and the actual auction print, computable only from intraday data -- a daily OHLC bar's close field IS the auction print, it has no 'quote 5 minutes earlier' field) exceeds a threshold, and it manages the exit adaptively over up to 5 days rather than a fixed single close-to-open leg -- a selective, signal-gated reversal trade, not the same daily anomaly re-labeled.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general, intended for pooling across a wide universe in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism) -- closing-auction mispricing is not specific to one ETF, though the paper's own finding that indexed/ETF names carry the largest and fastest-growing share of closing-auction volume makes SPY a natural, well-evidenced first-test representative.

name: Buyable Gap-Up Continuation
mechanism: On a session where a stock opens with a gap up of at least 0.75x its 40-day ATR above the prior close, on pace for volume at least 1.5x its 50-day average daily volume, and the stock trades bullishly (closes above the open, low of day stays above the prior day's high, i.e. the gap does not fill), enter long the instant a 5-minute bar closes above the high established in the first 20 minutes of the regular session (09:30-09:50 ET). Hold as a multi-week swing position (up to 15 trading days), trailing the stop to a close below the 10-day moving average rather than exiting same day.
source: Morales, G. & Kacher, C. (2010), "Trade Like an O'Neil Disciple: How We Made Over 18,000% in the Stock Market", Wiley -- formalizes William O'Neil's/Investor's Business Daily's "Buyable Gap-Up" rule (gap >=0.75x 40-day ATR, volume >=1.5x 50-day average, first-20-30-minute intraday high confirmation), corroborated by independent practitioner explainers (https://www.tradingsim.com/blog/episodic-pivot-power-earnings-gap-buyable-gap-up-explained, https://alpharvestpro.com/owl-strategy-types/). Verified via web search 2026-08-31. Ticker verified: NVDA, Nasdaq-listed since its Jan 22 1999 IPO, actively trading in 2026 (~USD 217 a share, ~5.25 trillion USD market cap as of Aug 31 2026 per Yahoo Finance/investing.com).
distinctness_note: Not a re-parameterization of qqq_tqqq_orb (a fixed 5-minute opening-range breakout on QQQ/TQQQ exited intraday) -- this triggers only on an ATR-and-volume-qualified gap in an individual growth stock, confirms via the first-20-minute high rather than a fixed early-session range rule, and is held as a multi-week swing, not exited same day; also distinct from the existing daily-bar pead_earnings_surprise_drift because entry is gated by technical price/volume gap characteristics (ATR-sized gap, volume surge, unfilled gap, first-20-min high break) rather than the magnitude of the accounting earnings surprise. Genuinely needs minute-bar data to measure the first-20-minute high and confirm the gap holds intraday before entry -- this cannot be determined from a daily bar.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general (any liquid stock that gaps up on an ATR/volume-qualifying catalyst), intended for pooling across a wide universe of liquid large/mid-cap growth stocks in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism); NVDA is the first single-ticker proxy this pipeline would actually backtest.

name: Darvas Box Breakout (Volume-Confirmed)
mechanism: Identify a multi-week Darvas box: a price range where the stock has failed to close above a defined ceiling for at least 15 (and at most 40) trading days, with a stable floor below. Once price first prints above the box ceiling intraday, require the specific 5-minute bar that closes above the ceiling to carry volume at least 2.0x the 20-day average 5-minute volume for that time of day before treating the breakout as confirmed; enter long only on that confirmed bar. Hold as a multi-week swing (up to 20 trading days), trailing the stop to the most recent Darvas box floor rather than exiting intraday.
source: Darvas, N. (1960), "How I Made Two Million Dollars in the Stock Market" -- the original box theory required a volume-confirmed breakout above the box ceiling before buying. Corroborated by independent modern explainers: https://trendspider.com/learning-center/darvas-box-theory-trading-strategy/, https://www.quantifiedstrategies.com/nicolas-darvas/, https://tradethatswing.com/the-technical-foundations-of-nicolas-darvass-trading-strategy/. Verified via web search 2026-08-31. Ticker verified: AMD, Nasdaq-listed since its Sept 1972 IPO, actively trading in 2026 (all-time high USD 584.73 reached June 30 2026 per historical price data).
distinctness_note: Not a re-parameterization of qqq_tqqq_orb -- the 'range' here is a multi-week consolidation box (15-40 trading days), not a single session's opening range, and the confirmation gate is a volume-multiple threshold on the specific breakout minute-bar rather than a fixed time-of-day breakout rule; applies to individual momentum/growth stocks rather than QQQ/TQQQ, with a box-floor trailing stop as a genuinely different multi-day exit than an intraday ORB stop. Genuinely needs minute-bar data because the box ceiling can be probed and rejected intraday multiple times before a real, volume-confirmed break-through occurs -- a daily bar cannot distinguish a false intraday poke above the ceiling from a confirmed breakout.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general (the box-and-volume-confirmed-breakout rule applies to any stock that forms a multi-week consolidation), intended for pooling across a wide universe of liquid momentum/growth stocks in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism); AMD is the first single-ticker proxy.

name: First-Hour Range Breakout (Swing Hold)
mechanism: Measure the high and low of the first 60 minutes of the regular session (09:30-10:30 ET) using 5-minute bars. When a later 5-minute bar in the same session closes above that first-hour high (long) or below the first-hour low (short), enter in the breakout direction. Unlike a same-day opening-range breakout, the position is NOT exited same day: hold as a multi-day swing (up to 10 trading days) with a stop at the first-hour range's midpoint, using the range break purely as a trend-continuation entry trigger rather than an intraday trade.
source: Connors, L.A. & Raschke, L.B. (1996), "Street Smarts: High Probability Short-Term Trading Strategies" -- describes the First Hour Breakout as one of Raschke's most consistent patterns, entering on a break of the first hour's established range. Supporting evidence for the first hour's informational significance: FINRA volume-concentration data cited in academic ORB literature showing ~50% of daily volume occurs in the first hour (via https://bullishbears.com/opening-range-breakout/ and related ORB research summaries). Verified via web search 2026-08-31. Ticker verified: IWM, iShares Russell 2000 ETF, launched by BlackRock/iShares May 22 2000, actively trading in 2026 per iShares' own fact sheet dated June 30 2026.
distinctness_note: Distinct from qqq_tqqq_orb both in mechanism and explicitly in application: qqq_tqqq_orb uses a fixed 5-minute opening range on QQQ/TQQQ exited same day, while this uses a 60-minute ('broader first hour') range on IWM/SPY/DIA and is deliberately NOT exited same day -- the range break is repurposed purely as a trend-continuation entry trigger for a multi-day swing hold. This is an explicit, acknowledged adaptation of Raschke's originally same-day/short-term pattern to the swing track's multi-day-hold requirement (not a silent reuse of a same-day mechanism), and is the 'broader first-hour trading range' variant, distinct from the opening-range-specific one. Genuinely needs minute-bar data to establish the 60-minute range and detect the confirming 5-minute breakout bar.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general (the first-hour-range-break rule applies to any liquid index ETF or stock), intended for pooling across a wide universe of liquid ETFs/equities in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism); IWM is the first single-ticker proxy, chosen to diversify from SPY/QQQ already used elsewhere in the catalog.

name: Intraday Liquidity-Sweep Failed-Breakdown Reversal
mechanism: On a 5-minute chart during the New York AM session (09:30-11:00 ET), flag when price trades below the prior 20-session swing low (a level at least 4 sessions old) -- a liquidity sweep of the level that would have triggered a breakdown-follower's stop.
