If a subsequent 5-minute bar closes back above that swing-low level, with volume at least 1.5x the trailing 20-bar average, before 12:00 ET the same day, enter long at the close of that confirming reclaim bar (not at the day's close). Hold for up to 20 trading days with a trailing stop, targeting continuation of the failed-breakdown reversal.
source: Connors, L.A. & Raschke, L.B. (1996), 'Street Smarts: High Probability Short-Term Trading Strategies', M. Gordon Publishing Group -- originator of the 'Turtle Soup' failed-breakout fade mechanism. The specific intraday, session-time-windowed, minute-bar liquidity-sweep-and-reclaim variant is documented as the 'ICT Turtle Soup' setup (Michael J. Huddleston / Inner Circle Trader concepts), traded on 5-minute charts during the NY AM session -- summarized at innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-turtle-soup-pattern and corroborated across multiple independent practitioner writeups (verified via web search 2026-08-31). Ticker verified: QQQ is the Invesco QQQ Trust, launched March 10, 1999, tracks the Nasdaq-100, ~408 billion USD AUM and among the most actively-traded US ETFs today (verified via etfdb.com and invesco.com, web search 2026-08-31).
distinctness_note: Distinct from daily-bar turtle_soup_failed_breakout: that family confirms the sweep-and-reclaim using DAILY closes over 1-2 sessions, which daily OHLC alone can already reveal. This version additionally requires the entire sweep-and-reclaim sequence to occur AND be confirmed within a specific intraday time window (sweep before 11:00 ET, reclaim confirmed by 12:00 ET) on 5-minute bars -- a within-session timing constraint that cannot be read off daily OHLC (which shows only the day's low/close, not when within the session each touch occurred), so minute-bar precision is genuinely load-bearing, not cosmetic. It is not an opening-range-breakout and so is not a re-proposal of qqq_tqqq_orb: the trigger is a failed break of a prior multi-session swing low followed by a reclaim, not a breakout of the day's opening range. Entry is same-session but the position is held up to 20 trading days, so this is swing-shaped, not a day trade. NOTE: near-duplicate Turtle-Soup-lineage variants (a 60-minute-window variant with no volume confirmation; an open-ended-session variant with no volume confirmation) are not catalogued as separate family_ids, under the pipeline's rule against multiplying near-identical trials.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general (a liquidity-sweep-and-reclaim rule applies to any liquid ticker with a defined swing-low history), intended for pooling across a wide liquid-ETF/large-cap universe in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism); QQQ is the single best-liquid proxy for the first test.

name: Intraday Capitulation Reversal-Bar Entry
mechanism: For a liquid large-cap stock, track the intraday percentage decline from the prior session's close using 5-minute bars. When that decline first reaches at least 5% by 14:00 ET (a capitulation threshold measured intraday, not from the daily close) and the very next 5-minute bar closes in the top third of its own range on volume at least 2x the trailing 20-bar average (a reversal signature), enter long at that reversal bar's close, same day. Hold for up to 20 trading days, targeting continuation of the documented short-term reversal that follows large one-day declines.
source: Cox, D.R. & Peterson, D.R. (1994), 'Stock Returns Following Large One-Day Declines: Evidence on Short-Term Reversals and Longer-Term Performance', The Journal of Finance, 49(1), 255-267, DOI 10.1111/j.1540-6261.1994.tb04428.x (verified via web search 2026-08-31, Wiley Online Library). Ticker verified: AAPL (Apple Inc.) is a real, actively-traded NASDAQ-listed company, currently trading with a multi-trillion-dollar market cap (verified via Yahoo Finance/GuruFocus, web search 2026-08-31).
distinctness_note: Distinct from daily-bar large_decline_rebound: that family can only confirm a 'large decline' after the full session closes, and must enter the following session. This version identifies the decline AND its reversal WHILE they are happening intraday -- the decline is measured against a specific ET cutoff time (not the day's final close) and the reversal is confirmed by a specific 5-minute bar pattern, then entered at that bar's intraday close -- information and an execution price only obtainable from minute bars, not daily OHLC. Not ORB-shaped (no opening-range measurement at all), so it is not a re-proposal of qqq_tqqq_orb. Entry triggers intraday but the position is held up to 20 trading days, so this is swing-shaped, not a day trade.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general (an intraday %-decline-plus-reversal-bar rule applies to any liquid stock), intended for pooling across a wide large-cap universe in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism); AAPL is the single best-liquid proxy for the first test.

name: Post-Earnings Reaction-Settle Drift Entry
mechanism: On the session when a company's earnings reaction first trades (the announcement day itself for pre-market/during-hours releases, or the next open for after-hours releases), track the realized range of 5-minute bars starting at 09:30 ET. Once that range first compresses to within 1.3x its own trailing 20-bar rolling average (signaling the initial earnings-driven price-discovery jump has settled -- typically within the first 30-60 minutes), enter in the direction of the initial reaction (long on a positive surprise reaction, short on a negative one) at that settling bar's close. Hold for up to 20 trading days to capture the standard post-earnings-announcement drift.
source: DellaVigna, S. & Pollet, J.M. (2009), 'Investor Inattention and Friday Earnings Announcements', The Journal of Finance, 64(2), 709-749 (verified via web search 2026-08-31) -- documents that the timing of an earnings announcement (day of week, before/after market hours) materially changes how fast and how fully the market reacts, motivating why WHEN within the reaction window an entry is timed matters for capturing the drift. Christensen, K., Timmermann, A. & Veliyev, B. (2025), 'Warp Speed Price Moves: Jumps After Earnings Announcements', Journal of Financial Economics, 167, arXiv:2601.08962 (verified via web search 2026-08-31) documents that earnings announcements induce sharp, minute-scale price jumps requiring high-frequency data to characterize -- direct evidence the initial reaction settles on a minute, not daily, timescale. Note as an honest caveat: that same paper finds a naive post-jump momentum chase is roughly consistent with efficient pricing after 2016, so this candidate should be tested rather than assumed to have edge. Ticker verified: AAPL, see candidate above.
distinctness_note: Distinct from daily-bar pead_earnings_surprise_drift: that family enters using a daily SUE (standardized unexpected earnings) signal at a subsequent day's open or close. This version specifically times entry to the intraday moment the initial post-announcement volatility burst measurably settles (via 5-minute realized-range compression against its own rolling average), which cannot be determined from daily OHLC and requires genuine minute-bar monitoring through the reaction session. Honest caveat carried from the source: a 2025 JFE paper finds naive post-jump momentum chasing is roughly consistent with efficient pricing after 2016 -- this candidate is proposed to be TESTED against that finding, not assumed to beat it.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general (applies to any liquid ticker with a real earnings calendar), intended for pooling across a wide universe in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism, matching how pead_earnings_surprise_drift is already pooled); AAPL is the single best-liquid proxy for the first test.

name: Session-VWAP Reclaim Reversal
mechanism: During the first 60 minutes of the regular session (09:30-10:30 ET), flag when a stock/ETF trades at least 1.5x its 20-day average true range below the running session VWAP. If price then closes back above session VWAP on a 5-minute bar, with volume at least 1.5x the trailing 20-bar average (a 'VWAP reclaim'), enter long at that bar's close. Hold for up to 20 trading days, treating the reclaim as a shift from net institutional selling to net buying flow relative to VWAP, the standard institutional execution benchmark.
source: Berkowitz, S.A., Logue, D.E. & Noser, E.A. (1988), 'The Total Cost of Transactions on the NYSE', The Journal of Finance, 43(1), 97-112 -- establishes VWAP as the standard institutional benchmark for whether a session's dominant flow was net buying or net selling. Shannon, B., CMT (2023), 'Maximum Trading Gains With Anchored VWAP: The Perfect Combination of Price, Time & Volume' -- a well-documented practitioner book (verified via Amazon, Apple Books, and a CMT Association-hosted excerpt PDF, web search 2026-08-31) that specifically describes a VWAP-reclaim-after-selloff pattern used as a multi-day swing entry, not just an intraday scalp. Ticker verified: SPY is the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust, launched January 22, 1993 by State Street, the original and most widely traded US ETF, ~798 billion USD AUM as of Sept 2025, currently trading on NYSE Arca (verified via ssga.com and etfdb.com, web search 2026-08-31).
distinctness_note: Not a re-parameterization of any excluded family: VWAP is an intraday volume-weighted price series that literally does not exist in daily OHLC data, so both the extension measurement and the reclaim confirmation are impossible without minute bars -- unlike a daily close-based mean-reversion signal (e.g. RSI2/IBS). It is explicitly not a re-proposal of qqq_tqqq_orb, whose ruled_out_reason is about data/feed portability of an opening-range-breakout entry: this mechanism uses a SESSION VWAP (resets daily) rather than an anchored/persistent VWAP used by the catalog's AVWAP candidates, triggered by a prior intraday extension below it (not a breakout of a fixed opening-range high/low band), and it holds for a multi-day swing rather than exiting intraday.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general (a VWAP extension-and-reclaim rule applies to any liquid ticker), intended for pooling across a wide liquid-ETF/large-cap universe in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism); SPY is the single best-liquid proxy for the first test.

name: 5-Minute ORB ATR-Stop Day Scalp
mechanism: Uses the first 5-minute bar of the session (09:30-09:35 ET) as the opening range: if that bar closes above its own open, enter long at 09:35 ET; if it closes below, enter short; skip the day if open and close are about equal. Stop-loss is set at 5% of the 14-day ATR from the entry price, profit target at 10x that risk (a 10R take-profit); if neither the stop nor the target is hit, the position is force-flat by 15:55 ET -- every trade closes by the same session's 16:00 ET close, no overnight exposure ever.
source: Zarattini, C. and Aziz, A. (2023), "Can Day Trading Really Be Profitable? Evidence of Sustainable Long-term Profits from Opening Range Breakout (ORB) Day Trading Strategy vs. Benchmark in the US Stock Market", SSRN Working Paper 4416622. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4416622 (verified via web search 2026-08-31: confirmed real backtest of the 5-minute ORB on QQQ, 2016-2023, with a 5%-of-14-day-ATR stop, 10R profit target, and end-of-day liquidation, producing a reported 33% annualized alpha net of commissions vs. buy-and-hold; also confirmed QQQ is a real, currently-trading, highly liquid large-cap ETF with a multi-decade price history and is the paper's own primary test instrument).
distinctness_note: Distinct from the ORB families already in the catalog: nr7_orb_trend_continuation and first_hour_range_breakout_swing (both swing-track, multi-day holds) -- this candidate uses a 5-minute range with an ATR-scaled stop and 10R target and is force-flat every single session by 15:55 ET, never carrying a position overnight. Near-identical 5-minute-ORB day-scalp variants are not catalogued separately; this entry is the most fully specified one (explicit ATR-based stop and 10R target), under the pipeline's rule against multiplying near-identical trials.
pooling_note: Single-ticker-specific for its first test -- the cited paper's core backtest and headline returns are computed specifically on QQQ (and its 3x-leveraged sibling TQQQ), so QQQ is the correct first representative rather than a placeholder standing in for a wider pool.

name: Volume-Filtered ORB (Stocks in Play, Pooled)
mechanism: Each morning, ranks a liquid stock universe by relative volume (today's early volume vs. that stock's own recent average) and restricts trading to the top-ranked 'stocks in play'; within that filtered set, applies the same 5-minute opening-range breakout entered at 09:35 ET as orb_5min_atr_stop_scalp, with every position force-flat by 15:55 ET the same session it opened. The relative-volume filter is the load-bearing, non-cosmetic addition over a plain ORB.
source: Zarattini, C., Barbon, A. and Aziz, A. (2024), "A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market", SSRN Working Paper 4729284. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4729284 (verified via web search 2026-08-31: confirmed real published study applying the 5-minute ORB cross-sectionally to 7,000+ US stocks from 2016-2023, filtered to relative-volume 'Stocks in Play', as a follow-up to the single-ticker ORB paper. Also confirmed AAPL and NVDA are real, currently-trading, highly liquid large-cap stocks.)
distinctness_note: Distinct from orb_5min_atr_stop_scalp, which trades one fixed instrument (QQQ) every day regardless of relative volume; this candidate is a cross-sectional selection strategy that trades a DIFFERENT, volume-filtered set of names each morning, pooled into one family under the pipeline's rule of one pooled trial per mechanism.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general by construction -- the relative-volume 'in play' filter is inherently cross-sectional; intended to be tested as ONE pooled family across a real universe (e.g. an S&P 500 + NASDAQ 100 universe) rather than one instance per ticker; AAPL is the single best liquid representative to seed the first test before that pooled run.

name: VWAP Trend Intraday Scalp
mechanism: Tracks price relative to the cumulative session VWAP computed from 09:30 ET onward on 1-minute bars: goes long whenever price crosses above and holds above VWAP for a minimum confirmation window, goes short whenever price crosses below and holds below VWAP, flipping or flattening on each confirmed crossover through the day. Every open position is force-flat by 15:55 ET at the latest, with no position ever carried past that same session's 16:00 ET close.
source: Zarattini, C. and Aziz, A. (2023), "Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP): The Holy Grail for Day Trading Systems", SSRN Working Paper 4631351. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4631351 (verified via web search 2026-08-31: confirmed real published VWAP trend day-trading system -- long above session VWAP, short below -- tested on QQQ/TQQQ from Jan 2, 2018 to Sep 28, 2023, reporting a USD 25,000 account growing to USD 192,656 net of commissions, a 2.1 Sharpe ratio, and a 9.4% max drawdown.)
distinctness_note: vwap_reclaim_reversal (swing-track) uses a VWAP RECLAIM as a discrete entry trigger held up to 20 days; this candidate instead maintains a continuous long-above/short-below trend position relative to VWAP for one session only, force-flat every day by 15:55 ET. A near-identical QQQ/TQQQ variant from the same source paper is not catalogued separately.
pooling_note: Single-ticker-specific for its first test -- the cited paper's real backtest and dollar returns are computed specifically on QQQ (and TQQQ), so QQQ is the correct first representative rather than a stand-in for a broader pool.

name: Intraday RSI(2) Reversion Day Trade
mechanism: On 5-minute bars, with RSI(2) reset fresh at 09:30 ET every session (never carried from a prior day), enter long when the intraday RSI(2) drops below 10 (deeply oversold) after 10:00 ET, or enter short when it rises above 90. Exit on a move back through the same day's 5-bar intraday SMA, or at a hard 15:55 ET force-flat, whichever comes first -- every position closed the same session, never held past 16:00 ET.
source: Connors, L. & Alvarez, C., "Short Term Trading Strategies That Work" (Connors Research, 2009) originated the 2-period RSI mean-reversion method; MQL5 Articles, "Day Trading Larry Connors RSI2 Mean-Reversion Strategies" (2026) documents the specific intraday adaptation this candidate follows. https://www.mql5.com/en/articles/17636 (verified via web search 2026-08-31). SPY confirmed actively trading.
distinctness_note: Distinct from any daily-bar RSI(2)/oscillator mean-reversion factor already in the daily track (long_mean_reversion_ibs_rsi2, ruled_out): the RSI(2) here is computed exclusively from intraday 5-minute bars that reset every session, and the exit is a same-day 5-bar-SMA cross or a hard 15:55 ET force-flat. Weakly evidenced (practitioner adaptation rather than a dedicated peer-reviewed study) -- a thin intraday edge is easily consumed by trading costs, so the cost model matters here; kept anyway per this pipeline's convention of honest sourcing over silent exclusion.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general (RSI(2) intraday reversion applies to any liquid, range-prone index or large-cap ETF), intended for pooling across a wide universe in a later test, starting with SPY as the most liquid, most-published representative.

name: Overnight Gap Mean-Reversion Fade
mechanism: Measures the overnight gap (today's open vs. the prior session's close) scaled by the ticker's recent realized volatility; when the gap magnitude exceeds roughly 1 standard deviation of its own recent overnight-gap distribution, enters a position AGAINST the gap direction (fading it) at 09:35 ET, sized off an ATR-based stop. Targets reversion toward the prior close/session VWAP, strongest in the first ~120 minutes after the open, and is force-flat by 15:55 ET regardless of whether that target was reached.
source: Stubinger, J. and Schneider, L. (2019), "Statistical Arbitrage with Mean-Reverting Overnight Price Gaps on High-Frequency Data of the S&P 500", Journal of Risk and Financial Management (JRFM), MDPI, 12(2):51. https://www.mdpi.com/1911-8074/12/2/51 (verified via web search 2026-08-31: peer-reviewed paper using a jump-diffusion model on S&P 500 constituent high-frequency data 1998-2015, finding overnight-gap mean reversion strongest in the first ~120 minutes post-open with a reported 51.47%/yr return and 2.38 Sharpe net of costs.)
distinctness_note: Opposite in direction from the gap-continuation families already in the catalog (buyable_gap_up_continuation, gap_and_go_momentum_continuation both trade WITH the gap and hold multi-day); this candidate trades AGAINST the gap as a same-session mean-reversion fade, force-flat by 15:55 ET. This peer-reviewed version is used in preference to blog/practitioner-sourced framings of the same fade.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general, intended for pooling across a wide universe of liquid large-caps in a later test (one pooled trial per mechanism) -- the cited paper itself tests the effect across the full S&P 500 constituent universe; SPY is the single best liquid first representative.

name: Overnight-Intraday Tug-of-War Fade
mechanism: At the 09:30 ET open, compute each stock's overnight return (today's open vs. the prior session's 16:00 ET close). Enter a position that FADES the overnight move -- short if the stock gapped up, long if it gapped down -- sized in proportion to the gap's magnitude, entered at the open. Force-flat the position at 15:58 ET the same session: captures only the documented 'intraday' leg of the overnight/intraday reversal, never the overnight leg itself.
source: Lou, D., Polk, C., & Skouras, S. (2019), "A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns," Journal of Financial Economics, 134(1), 192-213: documents a strong, persistent, offsetting reversal between a stock's overnight (close-to-open) return and its subsequent intraday (open-to-close) return -- overnight-return-sorted hedge portfolios earn intraday excess returns of the opposite sign, e.g. -3.24%/month intraday against the overnight-winner leg. Verified via web search 2026-08-31.
distinctness_note: Opposite mechanism from every gap-continuation family already in the catalog on both axes: fades AGAINST the overnight gap (reversal, not continuation) and is fully flat by the same session's close. A practitioner-facing framing of the same phenomenon (Aboody et al. 2018, JFQA) is economically redundant with this JFE paper's own cross-sectional finding and is not catalogued separately.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general and inherently cross-sectional -- the source paper's own tests are decile-sorted portfolios across thousands of US stocks -- intended for pooling across a wide liquid-equity universe in a later test; a single-ticker MSFT/AAPL run is a feasibility check only, not a fair test of the real effect.

name: First-Half-Hour to Last-Half-Hour Intraday Momentum
mechanism: Measure the ETF's return from the prior session's 16:00 ET close to 10:00 ET (the first half-hour signal window). If that return is positive, buy at 15:30 ET and exit at the 16:00 ET close; if negative, short at 15:30 ET and cover at the close. The position is opened only in the session's final 30 minutes and force-flattened at 15:59 ET as an execution backstop -- there is never any overnight exposure by construction.
source: Gao, L., Han, Y., Li, S.Z., and Zhou, G. (2018), "Market Intraday Momentum", Journal of Financial Economics, 129(2), 394-414 (also circulated as SSRN Working Paper 2440866, "Intraday Momentum: The First Half-Hour Return Predicts the Last Half-Hour Return"). Using high-frequency S&P 500 ETF (SPY) data from 1993-2013, documents that the first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour return, an effect stronger on high-volume/volatile/recession/macro-news days, extending to QQQ and ten other actively-traded ETFs. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2440866 (verified via web search 2026-08-31).
distinctness_note: No excluded daily-track or swing-track family trades a same-day time-of-day return-predictability signal -- pure intraday (30-minute signal window, 30-minute holding period) momentum, zero overnight exposure by construction. Near-identical framings of this exact mechanism from the same Gao/Han/Li/Zhou paper are not catalogued separately, under the pipeline's rule against multiplying near-identical trials.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general -- the cited paper documents the same predictability across SPY and ten other major domestic and international ETFs -- intended for pooling across a small liquid-ETF universe (SPY, QQQ, DIA, IWM) in a later test.

name: FOMC Post-Statement Reversion Fade
mechanism: On scheduled FOMC statement days, record SPY's 14:00 ET price (the moment of release) as a reference. Let the documented initial volatility spike play out for 15 minutes; at 14:15 ET, if price has moved away from the 14:00 reference by more than a threshold (0.15%), enter a position betting on reversion back toward that 14:00 reference level (long if price fell, short if price rose). The position is closed by a hard 15:55 ET force-flat the same session -- entry occurs entirely after the announcement, so there is no overnight exposure at any point.
source: Lucca, D. and Moench, E. (2015), "The Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift", Journal of Finance 70(1), 329-371 (also FRBNY Staff Report No. 512). Documents that after the 2:00pm ET FOMC statement, SPX/SPY on average dips for roughly 15 minutes then reverses, typically ending the session near the pre-announcement 2:00pm level. https://conference.nber.org/confer/2013/MEs13/Lucca_Moench.pdf (verified via web search 2026-08-31).
distinctness_note: Not a re-parameterization of any daily-track macro/calendar family or of any swing-track family -- trades the specific documented post-2:00pm-ET dip-then-recover microstructure pattern, entering only AFTER the statement (unlike a pre-FOMC drift trade, which requires holding overnight into the announcement) and force-flattening by 15:55 ET the same session.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general across broad-market index ETFs; intended for pooling across SPY/QQQ/DIA in a later test, SPY as tickers[0] the primary liquid proxy.

name: Scheduled Macro-Release Jump Continuation
mechanism: On days carrying a scheduled 8:30 AM ET macro release (CPI or the monthly jobs report), measure SPY's return over the 8:29-8:35 ET window bracketing the release. If the absolute move exceeds a threshold (0.20%), enter at 8:35 ET in the direction of that initial jump. The position is force-flattened by 15:55 ET the same session -- tests whether the initial jump reaction continues through the rest of the day.
source: Andersen, T.G., Bollerslev, T., Diebold, F.X., and Vega, C. (2007), "Real-Time Price Discovery in Global Stock, Bond and Foreign Exchange Markets", Journal of International Economics 73(2), 251-277 (NBER WP 11312). Documents that scheduled US macro announcements, including CPI and the employment report, produce statistically significant price jumps in equity markets at the exact release instant. https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w11312/w11312.pdf (verified via web search 2026-08-31). The continuation-through-the-session behavior this family trades is the hypothesis being tested, not itself asserted by the cited paper.
distinctness_note: Distinct from every daily-track macro/calendar family (which trade the day-level announcement premium, not a minute-precision jump trigger) and from fomc_post_statement_reversion_fade above (opposite mechanism -- follows the initial jump rather than fading a dip-then-recover pattern, triggers off 8:30 ET CPI/jobs releases rather than the 2:00pm ET FOMC statement); force-flat by 15:55 ET confirms zero overnight exposure.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general across broad-market index ETFs on any scheduled 8:30 ET release day; intended for pooling across SPY and QQQ (extensible to DIA/IWM) in a later test, SPY as tickers[0].

name: Late-Session Closing-Auction Pressure Scalp
mechanism: In the final minutes of the session, compare price change and volume in the 15:45-15:58 ET window against the preceding 15:30-15:45 ET window and against the stock's own trailing 20-day same-window average volume. If the later window shows an elevated-volume directional move (an OHLCV-observable proxy for the documented surge in closing-auction-routed order flow), enter a position in that direction. Force-flat at 15:59 ET, one minute before the 16:00 ET close.
source: Bogousslavsky, V., & Muravyev, D. (2023), "Who Trades at the Close? Implications for Price Discovery and Liquidity," Journal of Financial Markets (SSRN 3485840): documents closing-auction volume growing to 7.5% of daily US equity volume (from 3.1% in 2010), and that closing prices systematically deviate from the last continuous-market quote midpoint under this pressure. Verified via web search 2026-08-31.
distinctness_note: Complementary but genuinely distinct from swing-track closing_auction_deviation_reversal (up to 5-day hold): that family enters AFTER the close to fade the auction's price deviation once formed, while this family enters intraday BEFORE the close to ride the deviation as it forms, using price/volume as an OHLCV proxy since the raw NYSE/Nasdaq imbalance data feed itself is not available to this pipeline's data client. A version that reads the raw exchange order-imbalance feed is not implementable, because the pipeline's Alpaca minute-bar client does not carry that feed; this OHLCV-proxy version is the implementable form of the same underlying idea.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general (closing-auction volume growth and pre-close price pressure is documented across the broad NYSE/Nasdaq-listed universe, not stock-specific), intended for pooling across a wide liquid large-cap universe in a later test; AAPL is used as the initial single-ticker representative for its exceptionally deep, consistent closing-auction volume.

name: Turtle Soup Failed-Breakout Reversal (Day Trade)
mechanism: When intraday price makes a new N-day (20-day default) low that is a false breakdown -- confirmed when price reclaims back above that prior 20-day low within the same session, on a 5-minute bar close, and the prior 20-day extreme itself occurred at least 4 sessions earlier -- enter long on the reclaim (mirror short logic applies on a failed new-high breakout). The position is force-flattened by 15:55 ET the same session, with no attempt to ride any resulting trend into subsequent days.
source: Linda Bradford Raschke and Laurence A. Connors (1996), "Street Smarts: High Probability Short-Term Trading Strategies", M. Gordon Publishing Group -- the "Turtle Soup" pattern, explicitly designed to fade Donchian-channel breakout entries used by the original Turtle traders. Verified via web search 2026-08-31.
distinctness_note: Same-day-exit sibling of swing family intraday_liquidity_sweep_reversal (which holds up to 20 days) -- this tests the pure intraday scalp version of the identical false-breakout reclaim trigger, closed out the same session via the explicit 15:55 ET force-flat rather than carried for a multi-day continuation; the holding-period change is disclosed here rather than hidden.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general, intended for pooling across a wide universe of liquid ETFs and large-cap stocks in a later test -- SPY is the single best liquid proxy to backtest first.

name: Selling-Climax Capitulation Bounce (Day Trade)
mechanism: A same-session selling climax is flagged when cumulative volume by a given intraday checkpoint reaches at least 3x the trailing 20-day average volume for that same time-of-day, alongside a decline of at least 1.5x the 20-day average daily range achieved intraday; the entry trigger is the next 5-minute bar that closes back above its own midpoint after printing a new session low (a reversal/exhaustion bar). Long entry follows that reversal bar; the position exits at a fixed profit target or trailing stop, or is force-flattened at 15:55 ET, whichever comes first -- never held past the same session's close.
source: Robert D. Edwards and J. Magee, "Technical Analysis of Stock Trends" (multiple editions since 1948; cited edition via W.H.C. Bassetti, 9th ed., Taylor & Francis) -- defines the "selling climax": extraordinary volume at the end of a rapid decline that exhausts sellers' patience/margin and marks an exhaustion-driven reversal point. Verified via web search 2026-08-31.
distinctness_note: Same-day-exit sibling of swing family intraday_capitulation_reversal_bar (which holds up to 20 days) -- this tests the scalp/day-trade version of the identical panic-exhaustion-and-reversal trigger, closed out the same session via the explicit 15:55 ET force-flat instead of a multi-day hold; the holding-period relationship is disclosed here rather than hidden.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general, intended for pooling across a wide universe of liquid ETFs and large-cap/high-beta stocks in a later test -- QQQ is the single best liquid proxy to backtest first given its historically higher intraday volatility relative to SPY.

name: Dollar Index Time-Series Trend
mechanism: Applies time-series (trend) momentum directly to the US Dollar Index ETF (UUP) as the traded position, not as an external filter for another asset. At each month-end, compute UUP's own trailing 12-month total return; if positive, hold UUP long over the next month, if negative, move to cash. Re-check and rebalance every month-end.
source: Moskowitz, T., Ooi, Y.H., and Pedersen, L.H. (2012), "Time Series Momentum," Journal of Financial Economics, 104(2), 228-250. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304405X11002613 (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: UUP, Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund, inception Feb 20 2007, ~436 million USD AUM, ~1.4-3.5M shares/day.

name: Euro Short-Horizon Currency Momentum
mechanism: Applies the FX-specific momentum effect, strongest at short (1-3 month) horizons, to the Euro currency ETF (FXE). At each month-end, compute FXE's trailing 1-month total return; if positive, hold FXE long over the coming month, if negative or flat, move to cash.
source: Menkhoff, L., Sarno, L., Schmeling, M., and Schrimpf, A. (2012), "Currency Momentum Strategies," Journal of Financial Economics, 106(3), 660-684. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X12001353 (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: FXE, Invesco CurrencyShares Euro Trust, inception Dec 2005, ~345-469 million USD AUM, ~149K shares/day.

name: Currency Carry via Realized Distribution Yield
mechanism: Trades the Australian Dollar Trust (FXA) based on its own realized carry income. FXA passes through accrued short-term AUD interest as periodic distributions, so its own trailing 12-month distribution yield is a direct read on AUD's interest-rate carry vs USD. At each month-end, compute trailing-12-month distributions divided by price; go long FXA when that yield is above its own trailing 36-month median, move to cash otherwise.
source: Lustig, H., Roussanov, N., and Verdelhan, A. (2011), "Common Risk Factors in Currency Markets," Review of Financial Studies, 24(11), 3731-3777. https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/24/11/3731/1589752 (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: FXA, Invesco CurrencyShares Australian Dollar Trust, inception June 2006, ~102 million USD AUM, ~36.5K shares/day (liquidity caveat noted; FXY is a fallback if FXA's live quote proves too wide).

name: Yen Value Mean-Reversion
mechanism: Applies a currency value mean-reversion rule to the Japanese Yen Trust (FXY). Each week, compute FXY's price relative to its own trailing 6-month (126-day) moving average as a z-score using the trailing 6-month standard deviation. When FXY trades more than 1.0 std dev below its own 6-month average, go long expecting reversion; exit to cash once the z-score rises back to 0.
source: Asness, C.S., Moskowitz, T.J., and Pedersen, L.H. (2013), "Value and Momentum Everywhere," Journal of Finance, 68(3), 929-985. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/jofi.12021 (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: FXY, Invesco CurrencyShares Japanese Yen Trust, inception Feb 2007, ~440-466 million USD AUM, ~145-193K shares/day.

name: REIT vs Broad Market Relative Strength Rotation
mechanism: Each month, compute the trailing 6-month total return of VNQ (REIT sector) vs SPY (broad market). When VNQ's trailing return exceeds SPY's, hold VNQ; when SPY's trailing return is higher, exit VNQ and hold cash (BIL). Re-evaluated monthly.
source: Faber, M. (2010), "Relative Strength Strategies for Investing," Cambria Investment Management working paper, SSRN 1585517. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1585517 (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: VNQ, Vanguard Real Estate ETF, inception Sept 2004, ~39.3 billion USD AUM, ~308 million USD avg daily dollar volume -- largest/most liquid US REIT ETF.

name: Mortgage REIT vs Equity REIT Relative Strength Rotation
mechanism: Each month, compute REM's (mortgage REITs) trailing 3-month total return relative to VNQ's (equity REITs). When REM is outperforming VNQ, hold REM; when REM is lagging, exit to cash (BIL). Rotates entirely within the REIT sector's own price behavior.
source: Allen, M.T., Madura, J., Springer, T.M. (2000), "REIT Characteristics and the Sensitivity of REIT Returns," Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics, 21(2), 141-152. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=237836 (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: REM, iShares Mortgage Real Estate ETF, inception May 2007, ~545-656 million USD AUM, ~20.3 million USD avg daily dollar volume.

name: REIT Sector Absolute Momentum Trend
mechanism: Each month, compute VNQ's own trailing 6-month total return. If positive, hold VNQ; if negative, move to cash (BIL) until the trailing return turns positive again -- a single-sector absolute-momentum/trend filter on the REIT sector's own price history.
source: Hung, K., Glascock, J.L. (2008), "Momentum Profitability and Market Trend: Evidence from REITs," Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics, 37(1), 51-69. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1026386 (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: VNQ, Vanguard, inception Sept 2004, ~39.3 billion USD AUM.

name: Domestic vs International REIT Relative Strength Rotation
mechanism: Each month, compute the trailing 6-month total return of VNQ (US REITs) relative to VNQI (ex-US REITs). When VNQ's trailing return exceeds VNQI's, hold VNQ; when VNQI's is higher, exit VNQ and hold cash (BIL).
source: Zhang, W., Li, B., Roca, E. (2023), "Moments and momentum in the returns of securitized real estate," Heliyon, 9(8), e18476. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2405844023056840 (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: VNQI, Vanguard Global ex-US Real Estate ETF, inception Nov 2010, ~3.5-3.6 billion USD AUM.

name: Preferred Stock Yield-Spread Valuation Reversion
mechanism: Track PFF's trailing 12-month distribution yield and compute a z-score vs its own trailing 3-year rolling mean/std, recomputed monthly. Go long PFF when its yield z-score rises to 0.75+ above its own average (price depressed relative to its own recent yield regime); exit to cash when the z-score falls back to zero or below.
source: Cohen & Steers (2026), "Yields, regulations reinforce a positive preferred securities outlook," Cohen & Steers Insights. https://www.cohenandsteers.com/insights/yields-regulations-reinforce-a-positive-preferred-securities-outlook/ (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: PFF, iShares Preferred and Income Securities ETF, inception 2007, ~13.0-13.8 billion USD AUM.

name: Convertible Bond ETF Moneyness / Delta Regime
mechanism: Proxies CWB's aggregate equity-vs-bond delta regime using CWB's own trailing 63-day rolling beta to SPY, recomputed daily. Hold CWB when rolling beta is at/above its own trailing 2-year median AND trailing 63-day return is positive (equity-like regime); move to cash when beta is below median with negative trailing return (busted/bond-like regime).
source: RBC Global Asset Management, "Convertible Bonds" investor primer; Advent Capital Management, "Optimizing an Asset Allocation with Convertible Securities" (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: CWB, SPDR Bloomberg Convertible Securities ETF, inception April 2009, ~5.0-5.6 billion USD AUM, ~47 million USD avg daily dollar volume; SPY used only as a beta-calculation reference, never traded.

name: Preferred Stock ETF Volatility-Managed Exposure
mechanism: Compute PFF's own trailing 20-day annualized realized volatility and compare to its own trailing 2-year rolling distribution, weekly. Hold full PFF position when realized vol is below its own 70th percentile (calm regime); cut to cash when vol rises to/above the 70th percentile, re-enter once it falls back below.
source: Moreira, A., Muir, T. (2017), "Volatility-Managed Portfolios," The Journal of Finance, 72(4), 1611-1644. https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.12513 (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: PFF, iShares, inception 2007, ~13.0-13.8 billion USD AUM.

name: Equal-Weight vs Cap-Weight Breadth Ratio (RSP/SPY)
mechanism: Compute the daily ratio of RSP (equal-weight S&P 500) to SPY (cap-weight S&P 500), a real-time proxy for market breadth. Take a 20-day and 100-day moving average of this ratio; go long SPY when the fast MA is above the slow MA (breadth broadening beyond mega-caps), move SPY to cash when the fast MA crosses below the slow MA. Only SPY is ever held; RSP is a signal input only.
source: CXO Advisory Group, "RSP/SPY as a Stock Market Breadth Indicator," https://www.cxoadvisory.com/technical-trading/rspspy-as-a-stock-market-breadth-indicator/ (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Tickers verified: RSP, Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF, inception 2003, tens of billions AUM; SPY, State Street, 1993 inception, largest ETF in the world.

name: Composite Relative-Strength Sector Rotation
mechanism: Each month, compute a composite relative-strength score for Technology (XLK) as the average of its trailing 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month total returns. Compute the same composite for the equal-weighted S&P 500 (RSP) as a broad-market proxy. Hold XLK only when its composite score is positive AND exceeds RSP's; otherwise rotate to cash (BIL).
source: Faber, M. (2010), "Relative Strength Strategies for Investing," SSRN 1585517. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1585517 (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Tickers verified: XLK, Technology Select Sector SPDR, inception Dec 1998, ~117-123 billion USD AUM; RSP, Invesco, ~100 billion USD AUM; BIL, SPDR 1-3 Month T-Bill ETF.

name: Dual-Momentum Cyclical vs Defensive Sector Rotation
mechanism: At each month-end, compare the trailing 12-month total return of Consumer Discretionary (XLY) to Consumer Staples (XLP). Hold XLY only when its own trailing 12-month return is positive AND exceeds XLP's; otherwise rotate fully into cash (BIL).
source: Antonacci, G. (2014), Dual Momentum Investing, McGraw-Hill; Lequeux, N., "Simulation of Gary Antonacci's Dual Momentum Sector Rotation Strategy," Medium (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Tickers verified: XLY, inception Dec 1998, ~22.9 billion USD AUM; XLP, ~14.6 billion USD AUM (both State Street Select Sector SPDRs).

name: Relative Rotation Graph (RRG) Sector Trend Rotation
mechanism: Compute the relative-strength ratio line for Industrials (XLI) as its price divided by SPY's price. Take a fast (~50-day) and slow (~200-day) moving average of this ratio. Hold XLI only while the fast MA of the ratio is above the slow MA AND rising day-over-day; exit to cash (BIL) when the fast MA falls below the slow MA or turns down. Re-evaluated weekly.
source: de Kempenaer, J., Relative Rotation Graphs methodology, StockCharts ChartSchool. https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/chart-analysis/chart-types/relative-rotation-graphs-rrg-charts (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Tickers verified: XLI, inception Dec 1998, ~32.8 billion USD AUM; SPY, State Street, largest ETF in the world.

name: Industry Momentum Formation-Period Rotation
mechanism: At each month-end, compute the trailing 6-month total return of Health Care (XLV) and Energy (XLE). Hold XLV over the following month only if its 6-month return exceeds XLE's; otherwise hold cash (BIL) that month. Re-formed every month-end (Moskowitz-Grinblatt 6-month-formation/1-month-holding structure).
source: Moskowitz, T.J. and Grinblatt, M. (1999), "Do Industries Explain Momentum?", The Journal of Finance, 54(4), 1249-1290. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/0022-1082.00146 (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Tickers verified: XLV, inception Dec 1998, ~44.3 billion USD AUM; XLE, ~43.8 billion USD AUM.

name: Gold Autumn Seasonal (GLD)
mechanism: Academic analysis of gold returns 1980-2010 found September and November are the only calendar months with statistically significant positive average returns (Indian wedding-season/Diwali demand, equity-market Halloween-effect hedging). Holds GLD long from September 1 through November 30 each year, flat/cash the rest of the year.
source: Baur, D.G. (2013), "The autumn effect of gold", Research in International Business and Finance. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0275531912000323 (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: GLD, SPDR Gold Shares, inception Nov 2004, ~130-153 billion USD net assets -- largest gold ETF.

name: Natural Gas Withdrawal-Season Seasonal (UNG)
mechanism: Henry Hub natural gas follows the physical storage cycle: April-October injection season sees price weakness, November-March withdrawal season sees heating-driven demand draw storage down, historically pushing a seasonal premium. Holds UNG long Nov 1 - Mar 31 each winter, flat/cash the rest of the year.
source: Mu, X. (2007), "Weather, storage, and natural gas price dynamics," Energy Economics; CME Group, "Introduction to Natural Gas Seasonality" (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: UNG, United States Natural Gas Fund, inception April 2007, ~504 million USD AUM. K-1-issuing commodity pool, taxable-only scope.

name: Gasoline Driving-Season Seasonal (UGA)
mechanism: US gasoline prices typically bottom in Jan-Feb and rise into a late-spring/early-summer peak, driven by spring refinery-maintenance turnarounds, the mandated summer-blend fuel switch around March 1, and rising driving demand into summer. Holds UGA long from March 1 through Memorial Day each year, flat/cash the rest of the year.
source: US EIA, "Gasoline price fluctuations"; US BLS, "Gasoline prices: cyclical trends and market developments" (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: UGA, United States Gasoline Fund, inception Feb 2008, ~144.6 million USD AUM, ~113K shares/day. K-1-issuing commodity pool, taxable-only scope.

name: Crude Oil Term-Structure Roll Carry (USO/USL)
mechanism: When WTI crude futures are in backwardation, long positions earn a positive roll yield as price converges up to spot; contango produces roll-yield drag. Backwardation strength is approximated via the ratio of USO (near-month WTI) to USL (12-month futures strip) -- a rising ratio signals strengthening backwardation. Rebalances monthly: long USO when the trailing 3-month change in the USO/USL ratio is positive, cash when negative. USL is a signal input only, never traded.
source: Litzenberger, R.H. and Rabinowitz, N. (1995), "Backwardation in Oil Futures Markets," The Journal of Finance, 50(5), 1517-1545; Gorton, G.B., Hayashi, F. and Rouwenhorst, K.G. (2012), "The Fundamentals of Commodity Futures Returns," Review of Finance (verified via web search 2026-09-01). Ticker verified: USO, United States Oil Fund, inception April 2006, ~2.72 billion USD AUM, ~1.73 billion USD/day dollar volume -- the only traded leg. USL is a signal-only reference, materially thinner. K-1-issuing commodity pool, taxable-only scope.

name: Volatility-Managed Small-Cap Leverage Switch (TNA/IWM)
mechanism: Two-state discretization of Moreira & Muir's volatility-managed portfolio applied to US small caps with a real leveraged product: hold the 3x Russell 2000 fund (TNA) in months that follow a LOW realized-variance month for IWM, and step back to the 1x fund (IWM) in months that follow a HIGH realized-variance month. Realized variance is persistent while expected return does not rise in proportion, so exposure concentrated in calm months earns more per unit of risk; for equities the leverage effect makes vol-targeting an implicit momentum overlay (Harvey et al. 2018). The 3x product's variance drag is largest exactly in the high-variance months the rule avoids, which is the executable expression of 'lever up when variance is low'.
source: Moreira, A. and Muir, T. name: Volatility-Managed Credit Exposure, Pooled (HYG + EMB)
mechanism: Volatility targeting applied to spread credit, the second asset class (with equities) where Harvey et al. (2018) find volatility targeting raises the Sharpe ratio -- while for government bonds, currencies and commodities the effect is negligible, which is why Treasuries (#60) and gold are not proposed. Executed with the Moreira-Muir monthly construction as a two-state in/out switch on each credit fund's own trailing realized variance: long high-yield corporates (HYG) and USD emerging-market sovereign bonds (EMB) after a LOW-variance month, flat after a HIGH-variance month, trades pooled. Credit has the same leverage-effect signature as equities (spreads gap wider as prices fall), so vol-targeting again acts as an implicit momentum overlay.

Moreira & Muir (2017), JF 72(4), 1611-1644 (verified). name: Pooled time-series momentum on single-country equity ETFs (long/flat, 12-month)
mechanism: Apply Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen time-series (absolute) momentum independently to 15 single-country iShares equity ETFs: at each month-end, hold a country fund for the following month only if its own trailing 12-month total return is positive, otherwise stay flat in that fund. Every fund's trades are concatenated into ONE pooled sample (one trial, one family). The equity-index test unit in the source literature is the individual country index, not a regional aggregate, and country funds have far more dispersed paths than a DM/EM pair, so pooling them buys real, not duplicated, trades.

Georgopoulou & Wang (2017), "The Trend Is Your Friend: Time-Series Momentum Strategies across Equity and Commodity Markets", Review of Finance 21(4), 1557-1592, https://academic.oup.com/rof/article-abstract/21/4/1557/2338176 (verified; TSMOM across developed AND emerging country indices 1969-2015, edge mainly on the long side). Counter-evidence: Huang, Li, Wang & Zhou (2020), "Time series momentum: Is it there?", JFE 135(3), 774-794 (verified). Tickers (yfinance fund info 2026-09-04): all 15 iShares MSCI single-country ETFs; inception 1996-03-12 for EWJ EWG EWU EWC EWA EWH EWW EWS EWL, 2000 for EWY EWT EWZ, 2003-02-03 EZA, 2004-10-05 FXI, 2012-02-02 INDA; 14 of 15 multi-billion AUM, EZA multi-hundred-million.
distinctness_note: Not a re-parameterization of any catalog family: #53 em_dm_relative_strength_rotation is RELATIVE strength between two regional funds (EEM vs EFA), always invested; this is ABSOLUTE momentum, long/flat, at the single-country level, pooled. #17 covers TLT/GLD/DBC only; #2 dual_momentum_taa_trend (excluded) rotated a multi-asset universe including US index funds. No excluded family trades any single-country fund. Note: overlaps vol_managed_intl_country_etf_pooled in instruments but not mechanism (return sign vs realized variance).
directional_rationale: The rule is flat during a country's own 12-month downtrend, so it should beat buy-and-hold of the same fund on drawdown-adjusted terms if country-level trends persist as the two sources report. Because most of these funds' return is beta to their own index, the batch5 panel's alpha-vs-own-instrument and time-matched excess tests are the adjudicators; Huang et al. 2020's finding that TSMOM is hard to distinguish from a historical-mean rule is the null.
rule_pseudocode:
POOL = [EWJ,EWG,EWU,EWC,EWA,EWH,EWW,EWS,EWY,EWT,EWZ,FXI,EZA,INDA,EWL]
for each T in POOL independently:
  C = auto-adjusted daily close of T (total return)
  M[k] = last available close of T in calendar month k
  at the close of the last trading day of each calendar month m (needs 12 prior month-end closes, else no decision):
    ret12 = M[m] / M[m-12] - 1
    target = LONG if ret12 > 0 else FLAT   (ret12 == 0 -> FLAT)
  if target == LONG and position == FLAT: BUY T at the OPEN of the next trading session
  if target == FLAT and position == LONG: SELL T at the CLOSE of the next trading session
  otherwise hold; no stops, no time exits; one trade = one contiguous holding period
trades of all pool members concatenated into one sample (mining.pooling.pool_trades), scored as ONE trial; in-sample = everything before the sealed 6-month holdout
pooling_note: resolved_pool: ["EWJ","EWG","EWU","EWC","EWA","EWH","EWW","EWS","EWY","EWT","EWZ","FXI","EZA","INDA","EWL"]

name: Small-cap time-series momentum, long IWM or long RWM (inverse) rotation
mechanism: A two-sided trend strategy on US small caps, expressed with a real inverse product: at each month-end compute IWM's own 1-, 3- and 12-month trailing total returns (the Hurst-Ooi-Pedersen composite), take the majority sign, and hold IWM for the next month when the composite is positive or the ProShares Short Russell2000 ETF (RWM) when it is negative. Never in cash: every month is either long small caps or long the inverse fund, so the short side of time-series momentum is tested directly rather than as a flat period.

parameters.combination: majority_sign_of_three_lookbacks (at least 2 of 3 positive -> IWM, else RWM)

source: Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen (2017), "A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing", JPM 44(1), 15-29, https://jpm.pm-research.com/content/44/1/15.abstract (verified via web search 2026-09-04; headline strategy is an equal-weighted combination of 1-, 3- and 12-month time-series momentum, long OR short every market, 67 markets 1880-2016). Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), JFE 104(2), 228-250 (verified; short side weaker for equity indices). Counter-evidence: Goyal & Jegadeesh (2018), RFS 31(5), 1784-1824, https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/31/5/1784/4636242 (verified; TSMOM's edge is largely its time-varying net-long exposure). Tickers: IWM inception 2000-05-22, multi-billion AUM, ~22 million shares/day (yfinance 2026-09-04); RWM ProShares Short Russell2000, inception 2007-01-23 (proshares.com fact sheet and stockanalysis.com, verified 2026-09-04), daily -1x objective, AUM in the low-hundred-million range, ~18 million shares/day.
distinctness_note: First catalog family to hold an inverse product and the first two-sided trend family. Asset class is US small caps, explicitly outside the SPY/QQQ/TQQQ/SPXL/UPRO/SSO/QLD family and its inverses. Existing IWM families use different mechanisms (#25 buy-and-hold, #29 calendar, #49/#50/#51/#52 reversal). A 200-day-MA sell-state variant (long RWM when IWM trends down) would be a second, correlated small-cap trend-short trial and is not catalogued separately; this composite version follows the cited source's construction and is two-sided. In-sample starts at RWM's first month-end (2007-01-31).
directional_rationale: Two sources of possible alpha over buy-and-hold IWM: avoiding the long side during small-cap downtrends (2007-09, 2011, 2015-16, 2018, 2020, 2022) and earning the inverse fund's return during those windows, where Hurst et al. locate trend's crisis alpha. The drag against it is holding a daily-reset inverse fund across multi-month windows (volatility decay plus the small-cap risk premium), so the panel's own-instrument alpha, time-matched IWM excess and SPY excess are the decisive tests, not raw Sharpe.
rule_pseudocode:
ASSETS = {IWM, RWM}; shared calendar from RWM's first session (2007-01-23)
C = auto-adjusted daily close of IWM; M[k] = last IWM close in calendar month k
at the close of the last trading day of each calendar month m (needs 12 prior IWM month-end closes):
  s1  = +1 if M[m]/M[m-1]  - 1 > 0 else -1
  s3  = +1 if M[m]/M[m-3]  - 1 > 0 else -1
  s12 = +1 if M[m]/M[m-12] - 1 > 0 else -1
  composite = (s1 + s3 + s12) / 3
  target = IWM if composite > 0 else RWM      (composite can never be 0 with three +/-1 votes)
if target != current holding: the rotation engine closes the current holding and opens the target at the next session (engine convention; the overlap is one session)
if target == current holding: hold; no stops, no cash state; one segment = one contiguous holding of one asset
in-sample = everything before the sealed 6-month holdout; count every segment (IWM or RWM) as one trade
pooling_note: resolved_pool: ["IWM","RWM"]

Counter-evidence: Goyal & Jegadeesh (2018), RFS 31(5), 1784-1824 (verified) and Huang, Li, Wang & Zhou (2020), JFE 135(3), 774-794 (verified). Pre-registration disclosure: the expected trade count was estimated from the rule's firing rate on a small mega-cap sample before scoring; no pool member's performance was examined.
distinctness_note: Mechanism is time-series (own-history sign) momentum, distinct from every existing single-stock family: #14 fifty_two_week_high_momentum (cross-sectional nearness-to-high), #13 pead (earnings event), value/quality/buyback/accrual factors (fundamental ranks), and the index-level reversal families. No catalog family applies a trend rule to individual equities. Flags: (1) survivorship -- a pool drawn from today's constituents over-represents past winners, inflating buy-and-hold more than the timed version but biasing both; (2) per Goyal-Jegadeesh this rule is in effect a per-stock market-timing bet, so the SPY-excess and own-stock alpha tests are the substantive evidence, not the pooled Sharpe.
directional_rationale: A stock-by-stock trend filter is flat through each name's own multi-year drawdowns that a cap-weighted index hides, so if Lim-Wang-Yao's individual-stock persistence holds out of sample it should beat own-stock buy-and-hold on drawdown-adjusted terms and add to SPY-excess in bear markets. The null to beat, from Huang et al. and Goyal-Jegadeesh, is that the edge is nothing more than being net long when the market is rising; the batch5 panel is built to answer exactly that.
rule_pseudocode:
POOL = expanded_universe_2026-08-29 (the fixed 518-ticker list in data/mining/universe_snapshot_2026-08-29.json; record the list and its as-of date in the run artifacts)
for each T in POOL independently:
  C = auto-adjusted daily close of T (total return)
  M[k] = last available close of T in calendar month k
  at the close of the last trading day of each calendar month m (needs 12 prior month-end closes, else no decision):
    ret12 = M[m] / M[m-12] - 1
    target = LONG if ret12 > 0 else FLAT   (ret12 == 0 -> FLAT)
  if target == LONG and position == FLAT: BUY T at the OPEN of the next trading session
  if target == FLAT and position == LONG: SELL T at the CLOSE of the next trading session
  otherwise hold; no stops, no time exits; one trade = one contiguous holding period
trades of all pool members concatenated into one sample (mining.pooling.pool_trades), scored as ONE trial; in-sample = everything before the sealed 6-month holdout

name: Sector Zweig Breadth Thrust (10-day EMA of advancing share, 0.40 to 0.615 within 10 sessions)
mechanism: Zweig's breadth thrust computed on the sector panel: the 10-day exponential average of the share of seasoned members that advanced on the day. A thrust fires when that average moves from below 0.40 to above 0.615 within 10 sessions -- a rapid swing from washed-out to broad participation, historically the signature of a major low. On a thrust, buy SPY at the next open and hold 63 sessions; no re-entry while a hold is active. Expressed on the pipeline's net_advance_ratio snapshot as (1 + NAR)/2. Sector-basis note: the NYSE version fired 8 times in 40 years (Hill 2019); eleven funds swing between 0.40 and 0.615 far more easily, so the sector version can fire much more often at the SAME thresholds -- deliberately not re-calibrated, so what is tested is the mechanism at coarser resolution; an 11-fund advancing share also overlaps heavily with SPY's own up-day fraction, so only part of its variance is cross-sectional information.

parameters.ema_form: recursive, alpha = 2/(span+1), adjust=False, seeded at the first defined session

source: Zweig, M. (1986), "Winning on Wall Street", Warner Books (origin of the indicator; attribution confirmed across practitioner references via web search 2026-09-04, book text not accessed); Hill, A. (2019), "Perspective - 40 years of the Zweig Breadth Thrust", StockCharts, https://articles.stockcharts.com/article/articles-arthurhill-2019-01-perspective---40-years-of-the-zweig-breadth-thrust---weight-of-the-evidence (fetched 2026-09-04: 10-day EMA of NYSE Advances/(Advances+Declines), bullish when it moves from below 0.40 to above 0.615 in 10 days or less; 8 NYSE signals over 40 years). The 63-session hold is NOT from these sources (neither states an exit) -- pre-registered a priori as one calendar quarter before any return was computed. Panel membership: data/mining/panel/sector_spdr_11_membership.json; the net_advance_ratio series is computed from that panel by mining.panel.breadth_net_advance_ratio.
distinctness_note: An event-triggered mechanism (extreme transition in a 10-day breadth average, fixed hold) rather than a level/regime filter; no existing family uses a breadth thrust. Distinct from #38 vix_spike_reversal_equity_buy (implied-vol spike) and from #49/#50 (index own-return magnitude with day-scale holds): this requires participation to have already recovered above 0.615 and holds a quarter. Caution, disclosed: on an 11-member panel the statistic is coarse and overlaps heavily with SPY's own up-day fraction, so this is partly a two-week-reversal-then-recovery pattern on the index itself; it is accepted because the trigger is the source's, the hold is pre-registered, and the alpha-vs-buy-and-hold panel will expose an index-only explanation.
directional_rationale: The strategy is in SPY only during the 63-session holds after each thrust, so it beats buy-and-hold only if post-thrust quarters carry higher returns than an average quarter -- the documented claim that washout-to-participation reversals mark the start of intermediate uptrends. Time-matched SPY excess is zero by construction inside a hold, so the evidence must come from alpha vs SPY buy-and-hold over the full window, i.e. selection of above-average quarters.
rule_pseudocode:
nar_t = net_advance_ratio snapshot value = (advancers - decliners) / seasoned resolved members at t (>= 2 own bars; UNKNOWN if < 9 resolved members).
share_t = (1 + nar_t) / 2
z_t = a*share_t + (1-a)*z_{t-1}, a = 2/11, seeded z = share at the first defined session; the EMA is computed over the contiguous defined span only (an interior unknown session is refused, as panel_signals does for path-dependent reducers).
in_position = False
for each session t with >= 11 prior defined sessions:
    if not in_position and z_t > 0.615 and min(z_{t-10} .. z_{t-1}) < 0.40:
        buy SPY at open(t+1); in_position = True; exit_session = t+1 + 62   # 63 sessions in position
    elif in_position and t == exit_session: exit SPY at close(t); in_position = False
no stops, no early exits, no re-entry during a hold; a new thrust during a hold is ignored.
pooling_note: resolved_pool: ["SPY"]

name: Sector A/D-Line Bearish Divergence De-risk (SPY six-month high unconfirmed by the sector A/D line)
mechanism: Build the cumulative sector advance-decline line as the running sum of the pipeline's net advance ratio (advancers minus decliners over resolved members, so the line does not drift when XLRE/XLC join). A bearish divergence is flagged on any session where SPY closes at or above its trailing 126-session closing high while the A/D line is below its own trailing 126-session high -- the index makes a six-month high that breadth fails to confirm (the ChartSchool definition; NYSE June-Nov 2007 is the canonical example). Default state is long SPY; after a flag the strategy is flat for 21 sessions (each new flag restarts the clock), then re-enters. Every flag occurs at a six-month index high, so the strategy sits out parts of bull markets and its claim -- that unconfirmed highs are followed by below-average 21-session returns -- is directly falsifiable.

parameters.ad_line: cumulative sum of net_advance_ratio over the contiguous defined span from the snapshot's first defined session (interior gap refused)
parameters.adl_confirmation_test: ad_line >= its trailing 126-session max including today

source: StockCharts ChartSchool, "Advance-Decline Line", https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/market-indicators/advance-decline-line (fetched 2026-09-04: AD Line = prior value + net advances; bearish divergence = the index makes new highs while the AD Line fails to exceed its prior high; cites the NYSE June-November 2007 divergence); Colby, R.W. (2003), "The Encyclopedia of Technical Market Indicators", 2nd ed., McGraw-Hill (existence verified; chapter text not accessed). The 126-session high window and 21-session flat window are NOT quantified by these sources -- both pre-registered a priori before any return was computed. Panel data as for sector_breadth_thrust_zweig.
distinctness_note: A divergence mechanism (disagreement between price and breadth) rather than a breadth level or breadth momentum; no existing family compares a breadth line to the index's own highs. Distinct from #119 rsp_spy_breadth_ratio (price-ratio MA cross) and #51 turtle_soup_failed_breakout (fades the index's own failed 20-day breakout, no breadth input). Not a duplicate of the core index-ETF exposure: SPY's price enters only as a six-month-high test, never as a trend filter, and the flat windows occur INSIDE uptrends, the opposite of MA timing. The pipeline's cumulative_ad_trend snapshot (line minus its 63-day mean) is a different, level-type statistic and is deliberately not used.
directional_rationale: Holds SPY except in the 21-session windows after an index six-month high without breadth confirmation, so it can beat buy-and-hold only if those windows return less than SPY's unconditional 21-session average -- the narrow-leadership hypothesis. Because every flat window begins at an index high inside an uptrend, time-matched SPY excess during flat windows is the sharp test: if unconfirmed highs are ordinary bull-market days, the rule loses to buy-and-hold and fails the gate.
rule_pseudocode:
nar_t = net_advance_ratio snapshot value at t (>= 9 resolved seasoned members else UNKNOWN).
adl_t = cumulative sum of nar over the contiguous defined span starting at the snapshot's first defined session (refuse any interior unknown session).
spy_hi(t) = close_SPY(t) >= max(close_SPY(t-125..t))   # 126 sessions incl. today; False before 126 sessions exist
adl_hi(t) = adl_t >= max(adl(t-125..t))
flag(t) = spy_hi(t) AND NOT adl_hi(t)
off(t) = any flag(s) for s in t-20..t   # 21-session window including today
position rule evaluated at close(t): long SPY when off(t) is False; flat when True.
transitions: flat->long: buy SPY at open(t+1); long->flat: exit SPY at the close of the session on which off(t) first becomes True (engine convention).
no stops, no other exits; cash earns nothing while flat; SPY closes are used only for the six-month-high test, never as a trend filter.

name: Lagged Monthly Oil Price Change Timing Broad Equities (USO signal -> SPY)
mechanism: Cross-asset lead-lag with an under-reaction mechanism: Driesprong, Jacobsen and Maat (2008) find that the prior month's change in the oil price negatively predicts the next month's stock market return in developed and emerging markets, that the predicted excess return after oil rises is negative (not a risk-premium story), that the effect is absent in oil stocks and present in non-oil stocks, and that it strengthens with a few days' lag -- investors underreact to oil-price information. Hong, Torous and Valkanov (2007) independently find the petroleum industry's return forecasts the aggregate market one to two months ahead. Rule: at each month-end, if USO's return over the just-ended month is zero or negative, hold SPY through the next month; if oil rose, stay flat. The traded instrument is the broad market, NOT the energy sector, because the source shows the effect is absent in oil stocks.

parameters.decision_frequency: monthly (last trading day of each calendar month)
parameters.holding_period: one calendar month, consecutive holds merge into one trade

source: Driesprong, G., Jacobsen, B. and Maat, B. (2008), "Striking oil: Another puzzle?", Journal of Financial Economics 89(2), 307-327, https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:eee:jfinec:v:89:y:2008:i:2:p:307-327 (verified abstract via WebFetch 2026-09-04). Corroboration: Hong, H., Torous, W. and Valkanov, R. (2007), "Do industries lead stock markets?", JFE 83(2), 367-396, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X06001383 (authors' PDF read 2026-09-04). Counter-evidence: Tse, Y. (2015), "Do industries lead stock markets? A reexamination", Journal of Empirical Finance 34, 195-203. Tickers (yfinance 2026-09-04): USO = United States Oil Fund LP (USCF), inception April 2006, multi-billion AUM, signal only; the sign of USO's monthly return agrees with the sign of front-month WTI futures (CL=F) in 95.1% of 246 overlapping months, so roll drag does not materially distort the monthly-sign signal. SPY: State Street, inception January 1993.
distinctness_note: No catalog family uses a commodity price as a predictor of broad equities: existing oil families trade the commodity funds themselves (#127 USO/USL carry; #125/#126 seasonals) and the excluded SPY regime families key on credit spreads, curve slope, USD, real rates, VIX-family ratios or SKEW -- none on oil. SPY's own price history never enters the signal. Distinct from #56 commodity_currency_leadlag (DBC trend -> FXA), which trades a currency.
directional_rationale: Holds SPY only in months that follow a zero or negative oil-price month, so it cannot win by being long the market; it beats time-matched benchmark excess only if months following an oil-price rise carry lower (per the source, negative) expected excess returns than months following a decline. Costs are small (SPY's spread is under 1 bp and the position changes at most once a month).

# Monthly. On the last trading day t_m of each calendar month m (SPY and USO aligned on their common calendar; in-sample from June 2006, the first month after USO's April 2006 inception with a full prior month):
#   r_oil = close_USO[t_m] / close_USO[t_(m-1)] - 1        # t_(m-1) = last trading day of month m-1
#   signal_m = (r_oil <= 0)
# Engine mapping (single_long SPY, SignalResult per bar):

#               if not signal_m and a position is open -> exit=True (fills at t_m's close)
#   every other bar: entry=False, exit=False (consecutive True months merge into one trade; no stop, no time stop).

name: Customer-Momentum Lead-Lag: Nasdaq-100 Customers Timing Semiconductor Suppliers (QQQ signal -> SMH)
mechanism: Economic-link cross-predictability (Cohen and Frazzini 2008; Menzly and Ozbas 2010): because investors have limited attention and are specialized, news that moves a firm's principal customers is only gradually incorporated into the supplier's price, so the customer's lagged return positively predicts the supplier's next-month return even after controlling for the supplier's own momentum. Semiconductor companies are the archetypal suppliers whose revenue depends on the large-cap technology, hardware, cloud and consumer-electronics customers concentrated in the Nasdaq-100. Rule: at each month-end compute the prior-month return of the customer proxy (QQQ) minus the prior-month return of the supplier ETF (SMH); if customers outperformed suppliers, hold SMH for the next month; otherwise stay flat. The relative form isolates the customer component not already reflected in the supplier's own return, mirroring the paper's own-momentum control.

parameters.signal: prior-month QQQ return minus prior-month SMH return > 0
parameters.decision_frequency: monthly (last trading day of each calendar month)
parameters.holding_rule: consecutive True months merge into one trade
parameters.history_caveat: SMH's yfinance series before 2011-12-21 is the Semiconductor HOLDRS fixed-basket trust (real traded prices, not an index fund); any result must disclose this

source: Cohen, L. and Frazzini, A. (2008), "Economic Links and Predictable Returns", Journal of Finance 63(4), 1977-2011, https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1540-6261.2008.01379.x (read authors' PDF 2026-09-04: monthly calendar-time portfolios sorting suppliers on their customers' previous-month return; top-minus-bottom quintile 1.55% per month abnormal return 1980-2004; robust to own-firm momentum, industry momentum and within-industry lead-lag). Menzly, L. and Ozbas, O. (2010), "Market Segmentation and Cross-predictability of Returns", Journal of Finance 65(4), 1555-1580 (abstract verified 2026-09-04). Tickers (yfinance 2026-09-04): SMH = VanEck Semiconductor ETF, tens-of-billions AUM, roughly six million shares/day, continuous daily history from June 2000 (as the former Semiconductor HOLDRS, converted December 2011); QQQ = Invesco QQQ Trust, signal only.
distinctness_note: The catalog contains no customer-supplier / economic-link mechanism. It is the opposite of the catalog's relative-strength rotations (#112, #120, #122, #123), which hold the OUTPERFORMER: this holds the LAGGARD (the supplier) after its customers outperformed, on a limited-attention theory rather than trend persistence. Not a duplicate of the core index-ETF exposure: the traded instrument is a semiconductor fund and QQQ's own trend never determines the position. The practitioner 'semis lead the Nasdaq' direction (SMH -> QQQ) is deliberately NOT proposed, because it would trade the broad index. Formation and holding periods are the paper's one-month convention, not a lookback choice.
directional_rationale: In SMH only in months that follow customer outperformance, so it cannot ride the semiconductor bull market passively; to beat SMH buy-and-hold on time-matched excess, months following customer outperformance must carry a higher SMH return than months following customer underperformance. If the effect is dead at the ETF level (Menzly-Ozbas show it shrinks with investor sophistication), the panel will show a long-only strategy with partial exposure and no alpha -- a clean falsification.

# Monthly. On the last trading day t_m of each calendar month m (QQQ and SMH aligned on their common calendar; in-sample from August 2000):

#   signal_m = (r_cust - r_supp) > 0
# Engine mapping (single_long SMH, SignalResult per bar):

#               if not signal_m and a position is open -> exit=True (fills at t_m's close)
#   every other bar: entry=False, exit=False (consecutive True months merge; no stop, no time stop).

name: US-Leads-the-World Lead-Lag: Lagged SPY Return Timing Developed ex-US Equities (SPY signal -> EFA)
mechanism: International cross-market lead-lag: Rapach, Strauss and Zhou (2013) show that lagged monthly US stock returns significantly predict next-month excess returns in ten industrialized countries, in and out of sample, while lagged foreign returns have little power over US returns; a news-diffusion model attributes it to US return shocks being fully reflected in foreign prices only with a lag. Rule: at each month-end, if SPY's return over the just-ended month is positive, hold EFA (MSCI EAFE) for the next month; otherwise stay flat. The signal is the US market; the traded asset is a different asset class (international developed equities).

parameters.decision_frequency: monthly (last trading day of each calendar month)
parameters.holding_rule: consecutive True months merge into one trade

source: Rapach, D.E., Strauss, J.K. and Zhou, G. (2013), "International Stock Return Predictability: What Is the Role of the United States?", Journal of Finance 68(4), 1633-1662, https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/jofi.12041 (citation verified via EconPapers 2026-09-04; content verified via the KOF Swiss Economic Institute bulletin summary: monthly returns January 1985 - December 2010, ten industrialized countries, lagged US returns show superior out-of-sample predictive ability for foreign excess returns). Counter-evidence from the same bulletin: Siliverstovs (2016) finds the predictability concentrated in US recessions. Tickers (yfinance 2026-09-04): EFA = iShares MSCI EAFE ETF, inception August 2001, tens-of-billions AUM, roughly eight million shares/day, history 2001-08-27 onward; SPY signal only.
distinctness_note: Not in the catalog and not a ticker swap: #53 em_dm_relative_strength_rotation ranks EEM vs EFA on their OWN trailing returns; #62 applies own-asset trend to BWX; here EFA's own history never enters the signal -- the US market's lagged return does, on a gradual-information-diffusion mechanism. It does not time the US index family (SPY is only the signal). No family uses a foreign-market predictor.
directional_rationale: In EFA only in months that follow a US gain, so a meaningful share of EFA's beta is forgone; it beats time-matched EFA excess only if months following a US gain carry higher EFA expected returns than months following a US loss. EFA buy-and-hold has been a weak benchmark for two decades, so alpha vs EFA is a fair, not flattering, test; the SPY-benchmark comparison shows separately whether the timed foreign exposure is worth holding at all.
