name: Pre-holiday effect in small caps (IWM, open-to-close of the session before each scheduled NYSE holiday)
mechanism: Hold the small-cap index ETF IWM only during the trading session immediately preceding each scheduled NYSE full-day holiday closure (about nine or ten sessions per year), entering at that session's open and exiting at its close; flat on every other session. Ariel (1990) documents pre-holiday mean returns nine to fourteen times an ordinary day's, accruing throughout the day, independent of the weekend and January effects; Lakonishok & Smidt (1988) find the pattern persistent over ninety years of DJIA data; Ko & Yang (2024) show that out of sample (1983-2019) the premium became insignificant for large firms after 1990 but persists among small firms, which is why the traded instrument is the small-cap fund rather than SPY/QQQ/DIA.

parameters.holiday_set: scheduled NYSE full-day closures only: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day (NYSE since 1998), Presidents' Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth (since 2022), Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day, with NYSE observance rules
parameters.calendar_source: exchange_calendars XNYS, restricted to IWM's own bar index
parameters.entry: open of the pre-holiday session (entry signal fires at the close of the session before it)

source: Ariel, R.A. (1990), "High Stock Returns before Holidays: Existence and Evidence on Possible Causes", Journal of Finance 45(5), 1611-1626, https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1540-6261.1990.tb03731.x (verified via web search 2026-09-04). Lakonishok, J. & Smidt, S. (1988), "Are Seasonal Anomalies Real? A Ninety-Year Perspective", RFS 1(4), 403-425 (verified). Ko, K. & Yang, N. (2024), "The Pre-Holiday Premium of Ariel (1990) Has Largely Become a Small-Firm Effect Out of Sample", Critical Finance Review 13(3-4), 531-538 (fetched 2026-09-04). Quantpedia, Pre-Holiday Effect, https://quantpedia.com/strategies/pre-holiday-effect (fetched). IWM: iShares Russell 2000 ETF, inception 2000-05-22; yfinance history from 2000-05-26. Trade-count basis: IWM's bar index shows 239 sessions before a weekday closure through 2026-03-04 (about six ad hoc closures excluded by rule).
distinctness_note: No catalog family is holiday-anchored. #4 turn_of_month (excluded), #30 santa_claus_rally_yearend, #31 weekend_monday_effect, #32 triple_witching and #71 monthly_opex are month-, year-end-, weekday- or expiry-anchored; Ariel (1990) explicitly shows the pre-holiday premium is not generated by the weekend or January effects. Calendar-date overlap is limited to two holidays and is a shared date, not a shared mechanism. #29 january_small_cap_seasonal is a full-month hold, not a holiday-eve effect. Note: the engine's next-open entry captures only the open-to-close part of the pre-holiday return (Ariel's hourly evidence says the gain accrues through the day), so this is a partial but faithful test.
directional_rationale: In the market only about ten sessions a year (roughly 4% of sessions), so buy-and-hold beta can explain only a tiny slice of any return; the documented premium is a per-session mean many times an ordinary day's, so if it persists in small caps the time-matched excess over SPY on those same sessions should be positive. IWM's pre-holiday excess over SPY on the same sessions isolates the small-firm component the literature says persisted.
rule_pseudocode:
CAL = XNYS sessions from exchange_calendars, intersected with IWM's bar index; AD_HOC = {2001-09-11..2001-09-14, 2004-06-11, 2007-01-02, 2012-10-29, 2012-10-30, 2018-12-05, 2025-01-09}
is_pre_holiday(s): let n = next session after s in CAL; closed = weekdays strictly between s and n; return len(closed) >= 1 and not any(d in AD_HOC for d in closed)
signal_fn(frame, i): today = frame.index[-1]
  entry = is_pre_holiday(next_session(today))   # fires the session BEFORE the pre-holiday session; engine buys at the pre-holiday session's open
  exit  = is_pre_holiday(today)                 # engine sells at the pre-holiday session's close
  return SignalResult(entry=entry, exit=exit)
run_backtest(IWM, signal_fn, direction='long', time_stop=1, cost_bps=measured IWM round-trip)
One trade per scheduled holiday; no other parameters.
pooling_note: resolved_pool: ["IWM"]

name: Same-calendar-month return seasonality across the 11 Select Sector SPDRs (Heston-Sadka / Keloharju-Linnainmaa-Nyberg)
mechanism: At the end of each month, rank the sector SPDRs by their average total return in the SAME calendar month over the prior years (annual lags of 12, 24, ... up to 240 months; at least five complete same-month observations required) and hold the three top-ranked sectors for the coming month; the rest of the panel is not held. Heston & Sadka (2008) show that a security's return in a given calendar month positively predicts its return in that month in later years at every annual lag out to 20 years, and Keloharju, Linnainmaa & Nyberg (2016) show the same seasonality in industry portfolios (long-short same-calendar-month industry strategy 0.70% per month, t = 3.79). The signal is the sector's own history at annual lags -- not trailing momentum, not a fixed month-of-year rule.

parameters.seasonal_signal: mean of the ETF's own total return in calendar month m over years y-1 ... y-20, using only complete months (both bounding month-end closes exist and the ETF's first bar precedes the start of that month)
parameters.tie_break: longer history first, then ticker alphabetical
parameters.decision: last XNYS session of the prior month
parameters.entry: open of the first session of the month
parameters.exit: close of the last session of the month
parameters.execution_note: the cross-sectional rank is precomputed once from the 11 adjusted-close series into a point-in-time selection schedule (month -> set of 3 tickers, using only closes on or before each decision session); each ETF's per-ticker signal_fn then only looks up that schedule, so the pooled_single_asset runner needs no cross-ticker access at run time -- the same pattern as the calendar-driven candidates

source: Heston, S.L. & Sadka, R. (2008), "Seasonality in the cross-section of stock returns", JFE 87(2), 418-445, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X0700195X (verified 2026-09-04; same-calendar-month return responses positive at annual lags 12 through 240 months). Keloharju, M., Linnainmaa, J.T. & Nyberg, P. (2016), "Return Seasonalities", Journal of Finance 71(4), 1557-1590, DOI 10.1111/jofi.12398 (verified; working-paper text read at aqr.com: signal = average same-calendar-month return over the prior 20 years; industry long-short 0.70% per month, t = 3.79; anomaly meta-strategy uses a top-three/bottom-three rule, the precedent for holding the top three). Tickers: the nine original Select Sector SPDRs launched 1998-12-16 (yfinance from 1998-12-22); XLRE 2015-10-07 (from 2015-10-08); XLC 2018-06-18 (from 2018-06-19) -- matching data/mining/panel/sector_spdr_11_membership.json.
distinctness_note: Every existing sector family ranks on TRAILING returns (#120-#123); the signal here is returns at ANNUAL LAGS in the same calendar month, which Heston & Sadka show is a separate effect superimposed on momentum/reversal. It is not the Halloween/Sell-in-May split (#18) nor a fixed single-asset month rule (#124-#126): the month-to-sector mapping is learned from each sector's own history and re-ranked cross-sectionally every month. XLRE and XLC become eligible only once they have five complete same-month observations (2021 and 2024). Different mechanism from vol_managed_sector_spdr_pooled and us_industry_etf_pooled_tsmom on overlapping panels.
directional_rationale: Always invested in three of eleven sectors, so its beta is roughly the index's and any edge must be RELATIVE: top-seasonal sectors beating the sector cross-section in that month (Keloharju et al.'s industry long-short 0.70% per month is the documented spread). Evaluated on time-matched excess over SPY month by month, a passing result would show that sector selection by same-month history adds return over holding the index, which buy-and-hold beta cannot produce.
rule_pseudocode:
POOL = [XLB, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLU, XLV, XLY, XLRE, XLC]; adjusted closes; XNYS calendar for month ends
month_return(e, m, y) = Close_e(last session of month m in year y) / Close_e(last session of month m-1 in year y) - 1, defined only if both closes exist and e's first bar < first calendar day of month m in year y
SCHEDULE (precomputed once, strictly point-in-time):
  for each target month t, decided at the close of the last session of month t-1:
    for e in POOL: obs = [month_return(e, month(t), year(t)-k) for k in 1..20 if defined]; S[e] = mean(obs) if len(obs) >= 5 else None
    eligible = [e for e in POOL if S[e] is not None]
    SCHEDULE[t] = {} if len(eligible) < 9 else top 3 of eligible by S[e] (ties: longer history first, then alphabetical)
signal_fn_e(frame, i): today = frame.index[-1]; last_of_month = today is the last XNYS session of its month
  entry = last_of_month and (e in SCHEDULE[month(today)+1]); exit = last_of_month
run_backtest per ETF with direction='long', time_stop=None, cost_bps = that ETF's measured round-trip; pool all 11 trade lists into one sample (mining.pooling.pool_trades), one trial. First tradable month is the first with >= 9 eligible members (about 2004 for the nine founders); expected count ~3 x 12 x ~22 years.

name: Month-end 60/40 calendar-rebalancing flow (Harvey-Mazzoleni-Melone), SPY vs SH rotation over the last five sessions
mechanism: Institutions that rebalance a 60/40 stock-bond mix on a calendar schedule must sell equities into month-end when stocks have outperformed bonds month-to-date (equities overweight) and buy equities when stocks have underperformed. Harvey, Mazzoleni & Melone measure this with a 'Calendar signal' -- the deviation of a simulated 60/40 S&P 500 / 10-year Treasury portfolio's equity weight from 60%, reset on the last business day of each month -- and find a one-standard-deviation increase lowers next-day equity returns by about 17 bps, with the predictability concentrated in the last week of the month (peaking in the last four sessions, funds avoiding the very last day). Pipeline version: at the close of the sixth-to-last session of the month compute the month-to-date equity-weight deviation from SPY and IEF total returns; if equities are overweight hold the inverse ETF SH, if underweight hold SPY, for the following five sessions (enter at the fifth-to-last session's open, exit at the last session's open); flat the rest of the month.

parameters.bond_proxy: IEF, iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF -- the ETF nearest the paper's 10-year Treasury note futures; signal only
parameters.signal: w_dev = 0.6*(1+R_e) / (0.6*(1+R_e) + 0.4*(1+R_b)) - 0.6, where R_e and R_b are SPY and IEF adjusted-close cumulative returns from the previous month's last session close to the close of session T-6 (T = the month's last XNYS session)
parameters.hold_window: sessions T-5 through T-1: enter at T-5 open, exit at T open (target set at T-6, cleared at T-1)
parameters.quarter_end_scaling: none -- one uniform rule every month

source: Harvey, C.R., Mazzoleni, M.G. & Melone, A. (2025, revised January 2026), "The Unintended Consequences of Rebalancing", NBER Working Paper 33554 (also SSRN 5122748), https://www.nber.org/papers/w33554 (read the PDF 2026-09-04: simulated 60/40 S&P 500 / 10-year note portfolio 1997-09-10 to 2023-03-17; Calendar signal = equity-weight deviation from 60% for a portfolio rebalanced on the last business day of each month; one-standard-deviation increase lowers next-day equity returns by about 17 bps; predictability strong at month-end and absent otherwise, peaks in the last four sessions; the authors state the effect is distinct from the turn-of-the-month anomaly). Etula, Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen (2020), "Dash for Cash", RFS 33(1), 75-111 (verified). Tickers: SPY (yfinance from 1993-01-29); SH = ProShares Short S&P500, inception 2006-06-19, expense ratio 0.89% (stockanalysis.com; yfinance from 2006-06-21); IEF = iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF, inception 2002-07-22 (yfinance from 2002-07-30).
distinctness_note: #4 turn_of_month (excluded) is an unconditional LONG over the last session and first sessions of the month; this family trades the five sessions BEFORE that window, with a sign chosen by month-to-date stock-minus-bond performance, and is short the market (via SH) in months when equities are overweight -- Harvey et al. explicitly separate their effect from the turn-of-the-month anomaly. The bond series is a signal, not a multi-month regime filter, so it is unrelated to #33/#34/#60. Not MA, momentum or regime timing of the index. First catalog family to express short-side exposure through a real inverse product on a sub-month horizon. SH's daily-reset compounding is immaterial over a five-session hold.
directional_rationale: The position flips sign with the signal -- short the index when rebalancers must sell and long when they must buy -- and is held only five of roughly twenty-one sessions a month, so a positive result cannot be a disguised long-market beta; the source shows the pressure is a temporary price impact that reverts within two weeks and survives momentum, reversal and macro controls. Time-matched excess over SPY on the same five sessions is the natural read: SH months should show negative SPY returns and SPY months positive ones.
rule_pseudocode:
CAL = XNYS sessions (calendar-known, so T is known in advance); for each month let T = its last session and T-k the k-th session before T
prev_T(month) = last session of the previous month
target_fn(frames):   # called on every decision bar d; the engine executes the returned target at d+1 open; frames hold SPY, SH (traded) and IEF (signal) truncated through d
  d = frames['SPY'].index[-1]
  if d == T-6 of its month:
     R_e = Close_SPY[d] / Close_SPY[prev_T] - 1; R_b = Close_IEF[d] / Close_IEF[prev_T] - 1   # adjusted closes; return None if either close is missing
     w_dev = 0.6*(1+R_e) / (0.6*(1+R_e) + 0.4*(1+R_b)) - 0.6
     state = 'SH' if w_dev > 0 else ('SPY' if w_dev < 0 else None); return state
  if d in {T-5, T-4, T-3, T-2}: return state   # hold
  return None                                  # at d = T-1 the None target closes the position at T's open; flat until next month's T-6
run_two_asset_rotation({'SPY': spy, 'SH': sh}, target_fn, signal_frames={'IEF': ief}, cost_bps_by_asset = measured round-trips)
One five-session segment per month; no other parameters. In-sample runs from SH's first full month (July 2006), so roughly one segment per month.
pooling_note: resolved_pool: ["SPY","SH"]

name: Dividend month premium: long each pool payer during its predicted ex-dividend month, exit at the ex-day close (pooled)
mechanism: Hartzmark & Solomon (2013) document that a stock earns positive abnormal returns in the months its own past dividend calendar predicts it will go ex-dividend, versus other stocks and versus itself in non-dividend months; the returns build between the dividend announcement and the ex-date and partly reverse afterward, consistent with price pressure from dividend-seeking investors (a demand effect, not information). The rule holds each pool stock from the first session of a predicted dividend month until the close of the ex-dividend day inside that month, stepping aside from the post-ex reversal.

parameters.event_source: yfinance Ticker.dividends per traded name; index = ex-dividend date (yfinance dates are ex-dates: one business day before the record date under T+2 settlement, the record date itself under T+1)
parameters.predicted_month_rule: calendar month m is a predicted dividend month for ticker t if t had an ex-dividend date in month m-3, m-6, m-9 or m-12 (Hartzmark-Solomon quarterly-payer rule; also predicts semi-annual/annual payers via the 6/12 terms)
parameters.entry: open of the first trading day of month m (entry signal fires on the last trading day of month m-1)
parameters.exit: close of the first ex-dividend day inside month m; if no ex-dividend day occurs, close of the last trading day of month m
parameters.pool: the pipeline's cached expanded universe: current S&P 500 + NASDAQ 100 constituents after dedup, with cached OHLC and dated bid/ask quotes from the pipeline's universe cache. Keep ONE share class per issuer (drop GOOG, keep GOOGL; likewise FOX/NWS-type duplicates) so a single corporate event is not counted twice. Survivorship caveat: current constituents only, the same convention as every other pooled family drawn from this universe; any result must disclose it.
parameters.in_sample_start: 2001-01 (first month with a 12-month dividend lookback available from 2000 data)

source: Hartzmark, S.M. and Solomon, D.H. (2013), "The dividend month premium", JFE 109(3), 640-660, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X13000585 and https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jfinec/v109y2013i3p640-660.html (verified 2026-09-04: CRSP 1927-2011; premium ~41 bps/month abnormal; returns concentrate between announcement and ex-date, reverse after; predicted months defined from dividends 3/6/9/12 months earlier). Out-of-sample replication: Kreidl, F. and Scholz, H. (2021), "Exploiting the dividend month premium: evidence from Germany", Journal of Asset Management 22(4), 253-266 (verified). Data facts (yfinance 1.4.1, 2026-09-04): 91 of the 100 S&P 100 names paid at least one dividend 2000-01 to 2026-03-04; 7569 ex-dividend events.
distinctness_note: No catalog family trades a firm's own dividend calendar: #27/#28 and the preferred_stock_* families are continuous factor holds; #4/#18/#30 are market-wide calendar seasonals; the only dividend-adjacent event family (#63 stock splits) is a different corporate action. Disclosed overlap: ex_dividend_day_capture_pooled owns the last two sessions of this window for the same events; the mechanisms differ (multi-week demand run-up vs the ex-day drop ratio) and the run's correlation-based effective-N handles the shared sessions.
directional_rationale: Each stock is held only about 10-15 of every ~63 sessions and only in months its own calendar predicts a dividend, so time-matched SPY excess isolates the documented pre-ex run-up from market beta; the ex-day-close exit steps aside from the post-ex reversal the source documents, which buy-and-hold absorbs. With many thousand pooled trades the alpha t-statistic will be decisive in either direction.
rule_pseudocode:
PRE: for ticker t load OHLC (cached auto-adjusted universe frame) and EX[t] = set of ex-dividend dates from yfinance Ticker.dividends (dates only; amounts unused).
PREDICTED(t, m): True if EX[t] contains any date whose (year, month) equals m-3, m-6, m-9 or m-12 months (calendar arithmetic).
SIGNAL at bar i (date d, all data <= d):
  if flat:
    next_month = calendar month of (d + 1 calendar month, day 1); entry = (d is the last trading day of its calendar month) and PREDICTED(t, next_month)
    [engine executes entry at the next bar's open = first session of next_month]
  if in position (entered on the first session of month m):
    exit = (d in EX[t]) or (d is the last trading day of month m)
time_stop = 23 bars (safety cap only). One position per ticker at a time. direction = long.
POOL: run independently for every ticker in expanded_universe_2026-08-29 (one share class per issuer), concatenate trades (pooling.pool_trades), score the pooled sample as ONE trial.
Point-in-time: entry uses only the ticker's own past ex-dates (3-12 months old); the exit uses the realized ex-date, which is public at least ten calendar days before the record date (NYSE 204.12; Nasdaq 5250(e)(6)) and therefore before any ex-date under T+3/T+2/T+1.
Expected count: ~7,000 on the 100-name subset; roughly 3-4x that on the 518-name pool.

name: Ex-dividend day capture: buy the cum-day open, sell the ex-day close, events with dividend yield at or above 0.5 percent, pooled large caps
mechanism: On the ex-dividend day the stock's price drops on average by less than the dividend (Elton-Gruber tax-clientele and Lakonishok-Vermaelen short-term-trader explanations), so a total-return position that owns the stock at the cum-day close and sells on the ex-day earns the dividend minus a smaller price drop plus the cum-day buying pressure of dividend-capture traders. Graham, Michaely and Roberts (2003) show the abnormal ex-day return persisted after decimalization; Henry and Koski (2017) show institutions still earn it. The premium scales with the dividend, so a pre-registered per-event yield floor keeps only events whose premium can clear round-trip costs.

parameters.event_source: yfinance Ticker.dividends per traded name; index = ex-dividend date E
parameters.yield_floor: dividend amount / unadjusted close two sessions before E (the signal bar) >= 0.005; events below the floor are skipped (unadjusted closes come from a yfinance auto_adjust=False pull, since the cached universe frames are adjusted)
parameters.entry: open of session E-1 (the cum day); entry signal fires at the close of E-2
parameters.exit: close of session E (held = 1 bar); no other exit
parameters.price_series: yfinance auto-adjusted OHLC for the trade, so the dividend is embedded in the trade return (the ex-day adjusted return equals dividend received minus the price drop)
parameters.pool: the pipeline's cached expanded universe: current S&P 500 + NASDAQ 100 constituents after dedup, with cached OHLC and dated bid/ask quotes from the pipeline's universe cache. Keep ONE share class per issuer (drop GOOG, keep GOOGL; likewise FOX/NWS-type duplicates) so a single corporate event is not counted twice. Survivorship caveat: current constituents only, the same convention as every other pooled family drawn from this universe; any result must disclose it.

source: Lakonishok, J. and Vermaelen, T. (1986), "Tax-induced trading around ex-dividend days", JFE 16(3), 287-319 (verified 2026-09-04). Eades, Hess and Kim (1984), JFE 13(1), 3-34 (verified). Elton, Gruber and Blake (2005), Review of Economics and Statistics 87(3), 579-586 (verified). Graham, Michaely and Roberts (2003), Journal of Finance 58(6), 2611-2636, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=318483 (verified). Henry, T.R. and Koski, J.L. (2017), "Ex-dividend profitability and institutional trading skill", Journal of Finance 72(1), 461-494, https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jofi.12472 (verified). Exchange notice rules verified 2026-09-04: NYSE Listed Company Manual 204.12 and Nasdaq Rule 5250(e)(6) require notice at least ten calendar days before the record date, so the ex-date is public by the E-2 signal bar under T+3, T+2 and T+1. Data facts (2026-09-04): 7569 ex-dividend events 2000-01 to 2026-03-04 across the 100-name S&P 100 subset; 4411 have a per-event yield of at least 0.5 percent.
distinctness_note: No ex-dividend family exists in the catalog (the dividend factor holds are continuous portfolios). This is the classic two-session dividend-capture trade, nested inside the last two sessions of dividend_month_premium_predicted_ex_month's window for the same events -- disclosed; the mechanisms differ (ex-day drop ratio and cum-day capture-buying vs the multi-week demand run-up) and the run's correlation-based effective-N accounts for the shared sessions. The 0.5 percent yield floor is fixed before testing on economics, not tuned: round-trip spreads are about 1-3 bps and the premium is a fraction of the dividend, so a 0.1 percent quarterly dividend cannot clear cost under any documented drop ratio. Taxable note: a dividend held fewer than 61 days is non-qualified; the pipeline's STCG haircut already covers this.
directional_rationale: Two sessions of exposure per event contribute only a few bps of expected beta return per trade, while the documented ex-day premium is a fraction of a dividend of at least 0.5 percent plus cum-day buying pressure; time-matched SPY excess over many thousand pooled trades is a sharp test of whether the ex-day anomaly survives in liquid large caps after 2003.
rule_pseudocode:
PRE: for ticker t load unadjusted closes (yield test) and auto-adjusted OHLC (backtest); DIV[t] = {ex_date E: dividend amount} from Ticker.dividends.
SIGNAL at bar i (date d, all data <= d):
  if flat:

name: Utilities beta rotation (Gayed-Bilello BRS): 4-week XLU/SPY relative strength, weekly
mechanism: Always fully invested in equities, but rotates between the low-beta Utilities sector (XLU) and the broad market (SPY) on a 4-week relative-strength signal. At the last session of each week, compare the XLU/SPY total-return price ratio to its value 4 weekly decisions earlier; if utilities have outperformed over the prior 4 weeks, hold XLU for the coming week, otherwise hold SPY. Gayed & Bilello show utilities leadership is a leading indicator of near-term market volatility and fat-tail weeks, so the rotation lowers beta exactly when the market is about to be weak and restores it when the market is leading -- an intermarket lead-lag effect, not a trend filter on the index and not a static low-beta tilt.
source: Gayed, M.A. & Bilello, C.V. (2014), "An Intermarket Approach to Beta Rotation: The Strategy, Signal, and Power of Utilities", 2014 Charles H. Dow Award, SSRN abstract_id=2417974, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2417974 (verified via web search 2026-09-04; rule text extracted verbatim from the PDF mirror at operators.macro-ops.com: 'When a price ratio (or the relative strength) of the Utilities sector to the broad market is positive over the prior 4-week period, position into Utilities for the following week ... negative over the prior 4-week period, position into the broad market for the following week'; the paper's own ETF implementation uses XLU vs VTI from July 2001; 1926-2013 result 13.9% annualized vs 9.8% for the market; the paper states the outperformance disappears when commission plus slippage exceeds 0.37% per trade). The same rule was independently verified from the authors' gurufocus summary and the CFA Institute Enterprising Investor summary (2014-07-03). Tickers: XLU = State Street Utilities Select Sector SPDR, inception 1998-12-16, multi-tens-of-billions AUM; SPY inception 1993-01-22. yfinance: XLU from 1998-12-22, SPY from 1993-01-29.
distinctness_note: Not in the catalog. Differs from #41 defensive_sector_recession_signal_rotation (same XLU/SPY pair but driven by a yield-curve spread, not the pair's own relative strength), #122 sector_rrg_relative_strength_trend (XLI/SPY ratio 50/200-day MA cross holding Industrials or cash), #119 rsp_spy_breadth_ratio and #15 betting_against_beta_low_vol (static SPLV hold). Not index trend timing: 100% in equities every week, so it cannot reproduce a leveraged-ETF rotation's regime-model exposure. Only one expression of the Gayed signal is catalogued: this one is the paper's native, verbatim-verified rule (an inverse-product expression, long SH in utilities-leading weeks, would be a second correlated trial). Correlated with low_vol_high_beta_factor_momentum_rotation (both roughly one-month-scale beta rotations); the pairwise-correlation trial correction handles that.
directional_rationale: The edge claimed is timing, not beta: the rotation's average beta sits between XLU's and SPY's, yet the paper reports about 4 percentage points per year over the market since 1926 because utilities leadership precedes high-volatility and fat-tail weeks. If that lead-lag holds, the strategy earns positive alpha vs SPY with lower drawdowns; if it is only index drift, time-matched SPY excess will be near zero and the beta-in-disguise flag will fire.
rule_pseudocode:
DATA: daily auto-adjusted OHLC for XLU and SPY from yfinance, restricted to their common calendar (starts 1998-12-22). No other series.
DECISION BARS: the last trading session of each ISO week (normally Friday; the preceding session if Friday is a holiday). On every other session, the target is the most recent decision's target.
FOR each decision bar t (using only closes <= t):
  ratio_t   = Close_XLU[t] / Close_SPY[t]
  ratio_ref = ratio on the 4th prior weekly decision bar
  IF ratio_ref is unavailable (fewer than 4 prior decision bars): target = None (warm-up only)
  ELSE IF ratio_t > ratio_ref: target = 'XLU'      # utilities outperformed over the prior 4 weeks
  ELSE:                        target = 'SPY'      # ties and negatives -> broad market, per the paper
EXECUTION (rotation_engine.run_two_asset_rotation convention): the target decided on bar t executes at bar t+1's open. An unchanged target does not trade; a changed target closes the old leg and opens the new leg at that open; each completed segment is charged its own round-trip cost once. After warm-up the strategy is never flat.
PARAMETERS ARE FIXED: 4-week lookback, weekly decision, no threshold band, no cash state, no MA or absolute-momentum filter.
pooling_note: resolved_pool: ["XLU","SPY"]

name: Low-volatility vs high-beta factor-momentum rotation (SPLV vs SPHB, 1-month, monthly)
mechanism: Time-series factor momentum applied to the low-beta factor, expressed long-only as a two-leg rotation: SPLV (the 100 lowest-volatility S&P 500 stocks) vs SPHB (the 100 highest-beta S&P 500 stocks). Each month, hold whichever leg had the higher trailing 1-month total return, i.e. go with the sign of the long-low-beta/short-high-beta factor's own most recent return. Gupta & Kelly (2019) document that individual factors can be timed on their own recent performance (positive time-series momentum in 59 of 65 factors, strongest at the 1-month formation window); Ehsani & Linnainmaa (2022) show the average factor earns 51 bps/month after a positive year vs 6 bps after a negative year, concentrated in high-eigenvalue factors of which low-beta is one. The bet is on the persistence of the factor spread, not on the level of the unconditional low-vol premium.
source: Gupta, T. & Kelly, B.T. (2019), "Factor Momentum Everywhere", JPM 45(3), 13-36, https://jpm.pm-research.com/content/45/3/13 and SSRN abstract_id=3300728 (verified via web search 2026-09-04: 65 characteristic factors, individual-factor time-series momentum positive in 59 of 65, the 1-month formation/1-month holding configuration the strongest). Ehsani, S. & Linnainmaa, J.T. (2022), "Factor Momentum and the Momentum Factor", Journal of Finance 77, 1877-1919, doi:10.1111/jofi.13131 (verified). Tickers (web search 2026-09-04): SPLV = Invesco S&P 500 Low Volatility ETF, inception 2011-05-05, multi-billion AUM; SPHB = Invesco S&P 500 High Beta ETF, inception 2011-05-05, high-hundreds-of-millions AUM. yfinance: both from 2011-05-05.
distinctness_note: Differs in mechanism from #15 betting_against_beta_low_vol, which tests the UNCONDITIONAL low-beta premium as SPLV/USMV buy-and-hold; this family bets on the autocorrelation of the same factor's return (factor momentum), and its payoff does not depend on the static premium being positive. Differs from #14 (stock-level cross-sectional momentum), #49/#50 (index reversal) and the sector-pair momentum rotations #120-#123 (6-12 month sector relative strength with cash fallback). Both legs are S&P 500 subsets, so the strategy is never out of the market and never resembles a leveraged-ETF rotation's index timing. Lookback disclosure: 1 month is Gupta & Kelly's baseline and strongest configuration, chosen on source precedent and the trade-count power floor, not on any return measurement. Correlated with utilities_beta_rotation_relative_strength.
directional_rationale: SPLV and SPHB bracket the S&P 500's beta from both sides, so a rotation between them averages roughly market beta; any excess over SPY must come from picking the leg currently in favor. If factor momentum holds one month ahead, the rotation should beat both legs' buy-and-hold and show positive time-matched excess over SPY; if not, it collapses to a noisy 50/50 blend whose alpha vs SPY is zero.

DATA: daily auto-adjusted OHLC for SPLV and SPHB from yfinance, common calendar from 2011-05-05. No other series.
DECISION BAR: the first trading session of each calendar month (mining.signals._monthly_decision_frame convention), using data through that session's close; the target holds until the next month's decision.
FOR each decision bar t with decision_date d:

  base_X = Close_X on the last session on or before anchor, for X in {SPHB, SPLV}   # _calendar_anchor_close(lookback_months=1)

name: Gold vs long-Treasury relative momentum (Antonacci economic-stress pair, GLD vs TLT, 12-month, monthly)
mechanism: The relative-momentum half of Antonacci's 'economic stress' dual-momentum module, always invested: each month hold whichever of GLD (physical gold) or TLT (20+ year Treasuries) had the higher trailing 12-month total return. Both are safe-haven assets that respond to economic stress but separate for momentum purposes -- gold responds to inflationary expectations and Treasuries to deflationary pressure -- and Antonacci reports that leadership between them persists at the 12-month horizon (about 1.6 switches per year in 1974-2011 data). This family tests only the selection between the two havens; it deliberately omits the T-bill absolute-momentum filter, which the catalog already covers on both legs (#17).
source: Antonacci, G. (2012), "Risk Premia Harvesting Through Dual Momentum", Portfolio Management Consultants working paper, first place 2012 NAAIM Founders Award, SSRN abstract_id=2042750, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2042750 (verified via web search 2026-09-04; rule text extracted from the PDF mirror at trendfollowing.com: twelve-month formation period, positions adjusted monthly without skipping a month, the economic-stress module uses the Barclays U.S. Treasury 20+ year index and gold, 1.6 switches per year). Secondary confirmation: Allocate Smartly's Composite Dual Momentum write-up (fetched 2026-09-04) implements the module as GLD vs TLT on 12-month returns. Tickers: GLD = SPDR Gold Shares, inception 2004-11-18, AUM above one hundred billion; TLT = iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF, inception 2002-07-22, multi-tens-of-billions AUM. yfinance: GLD from 2004-11-18, TLT from 2002-07-30.
distinctness_note: Differs from #17 cross_asset_time_series_momentum, which applies the ABSOLUTE (own-return-sign, long/flat) 12-month rule to TLT and GLD separately -- exactly the T-bill/absolute half of Antonacci's module -- so this family isolates the relative half and is always invested. Differs from #36 real_rate_gold_equity_rotation (TIP trend rotating SPY/GLD), #44 gold_miners_real_rate_rotation, #34/#60 (TLT vs SHY by slope/volatility) and #124 gold_autumn_effect_seasonal. The T-bill fallback is left out on purpose: adding it would re-parameterize #17. The fairest passive comparator is a 50/50 GLD/TLT blend, not expressible as a single ticker; GLD is set as benchmark_ticker and the driver's own-instrument and SPY panels cover the rest. Note: the expected trade count is only modestly above the 30 floor; treat a weak result as underpowered rather than disproven.
directional_rationale: Near-zero equity beta (both legs are havens), so any alpha versus SPY cannot be market beta in disguise; the real test is versus holding the havens passively. Antonacci's evidence is that 12-month leadership between gold and long Treasuries persists because inflationary and deflationary stress regimes last for years, so the rotation should capture most of the leading haven's run while avoiding most of the lagging one's drawdown -- beating both GLD and TLT buy-and-hold risk-adjusted, which a static blend cannot do.

name: 3x Long Treasury (TMF) held only in the 3-session FOMC window
mechanism: Hillenbrand (RFS 2025) documents that a 3-day window around FOMC meetings -- the session before the statement, the statement session, and the session after (about 10 percent of trading days) -- captures the entire secular decline in the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield since 1989, while yield changes on all other days are transitory and net to zero; he attributes it to Fed announcements guiding the long-run path of rates. Savor and Wilson (JFQA 2013) independently show Treasury excess returns are concentrated on scheduled macro-announcement days and rise with maturity. The rule buys the 3x 20+ year Treasury product for exactly those three sessions and is flat otherwise, so the traded exposure is roughly 3x duration for ~10 percent of the time; over a 3-session hold the leveraged product's path-dependence term (Avellaneda-Zhang 2010) is negligible.

parameters.statement_session_rule: second day of a two-day meeting; the meeting day for a one-day meeting (statement-day convention since 1994 per Hillenbrand)
parameters.event_source: federalreserve.gov FOMC calendars: fomc_historical_year.htm (by year, through 2020) and fomccalendars.htm (2021-2027); the statement-date list must cover 2009-04 (TMF inception) onward and be filtered to scheduled meetings -- a free, public, point-in-time source

source: Hillenbrand, S. (2025), "The Fed and the Secular Decline in Interest Rates", Review of Financial Studies 38(4), 981-1013, https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/38/4/981/7979199 (verified via web search 2026-09-04; window definition verified from the author's Banca d'Italia seminar PDF https://www.bancaditalia.it/pubblicazioni/altri-atti-seminari/2023/Hillenbrand_paper.pdf). Savor, P. and Wilson, M. (2013), "How Much Do Investors Care About Macroeconomic Risk? Evidence from Scheduled Economic Announcements", JFQA 48(2), 343-375 (verified). Avellaneda, M. and Zhang, S. (2010), "Path-Dependence of Leveraged ETF Returns", SIAM Journal on Financial Mathematics 1(1), 586-603, https://math.nyu.edu/inmemoriam/avellaneda/SIAMLETFS.pdf (verified). TMF = Direxion Daily 20+ Year Treasury Bull 3X, inception 2009-04-16 (stockanalysis.com and yfinance first bar 2009-04-16, 4375 daily bars through 2026-09-04).
distinctness_note: Versus #5 pre_fomc_drift (SPY, ruled_out): different asset class (Treasuries, not the broad index family), a different window (three sessions centred on the statement, not the 24 hours before), and a bond-specific published source. Versus #103 fomc_post_statement_reversion_fade (intraday SPY fade). Versus #60/#34/#17 (TLT price-based regimes): this uses no price signal at all -- a pre-published calendar event. The leveraged product is the traded instrument, not a decay-avoidance rule. Honest adverse sub-period inside the sample: the 2022-2023 hiking cycle. A broader Savor-Wilson variant (CPI and jobs days) is not catalogued: data/mining/macro_release_dates.json covers only 2019 onward.
directional_rationale: TMF buy-and-hold since 2009 is deeply negative (volatility decay plus the 2020-2023 bond bear), and this rule is in the market only about 10 percent of sessions, so its beta to TMF buy-and-hold is near 0.1; any edge must show up as positive time-matched excess over TMF on the held windows and a positive HAC alpha, which is exactly what Hillenbrand's finding and Savor-Wilson's maturity-increasing announcement premium predict.
rule_pseudocode:
E = sorted list of SCHEDULED FOMC statement sessions (two-day meeting -> second day; one-day meeting -> that day), taken from federalreserve.gov calendars as published before each year; unscheduled/emergency meetings excluded (not knowable at decision time).
For each NYSE session t in TMF's history (index s(t)):
  signal(t) = 1 if there exists e in E with s(t) in {s(e)-2, s(e)-1, s(e)}  else 0
Engine semantics: signal(t)=1 at the close of t -> long TMF from the open of t+1; position held while signal stays 1; exit at the close of the first session whose signal is 0 -> the position is held from the open of session e-1 through the close of session e+1 (exactly 3 sessions), one trade per scheduled meeting. Scheduled meetings are at least 5 weeks apart so windows never overlap. No price-based inputs; decision uses only the calendar known at t. About 8 meetings/year x 17 years = ~130 trades.

name: 30-year bond auction cycle: -3x Treasury (TMV) for 5 sessions into the auction, 3x (TMF) for 5 sessions after, T-bills otherwise
mechanism: Lou, Yan and Zhang (RFS 2013) show secondary-market Treasury prices fall over the roughly 5 sessions before each scheduled auction and recover over the roughly 5 sessions after (2-, 5- and 10-year notes, 1980-2008), attributing it to dealers' limited risk-bearing capacity and slow-moving end-investor capital. Herb (JBF 2025) extends the post-auction premium to the 30-year bond itself, and Fleming, Liu and Nguyen (FRBNY Staff Report 1188, 2026) confirm with 33 years of intraday data that auction-day price pressure persists. The 30-year bond has been auctioned monthly since March 2009, matching TMF/TMV's April 2009 inception. Two-sided directional expression through real leveraged products: long the -3x fund in the pre-auction leg, long the 3x fund in the post-auction leg, cash (BIL) otherwise; each leg is only 5 sessions so inverse/leveraged decay is negligible.

parameters.event: 30-year Treasury bond auction date (new issues and reopenings)
parameters.event_source: TreasuryDirect auction query (treasurydirect.gov/auctions/auction-query/), CSV/JSON export, security type Bond, security term 30-Year; non-TIPS history available from 1998-07-27 per the page; dates are known in advance via the tentative auction schedule (free, public, point-in-time)
parameters.pre_leg_window: sessions a-4 through a inclusive (auction day included; auctions close 13:00 ET)
parameters.overlap_rule: post-leg of the earlier auction takes precedence
parameters.pre_registered_fallback: if run_two_asset_rotation cannot take a daily calendar target with three assets, run the post-leg alone as single_long TMF (the leg with the larger documented effect) with the same 5-session window

source: Lou, D., Yan, H. and Zhang, J. (2013), "Anticipated and Repeated Shocks in Liquid Markets", Review of Financial Studies 26(8), 1891-1912, https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/26/8/1891/1589893 (verified via web search 2026-09-04; the 5-session windows, magnitudes and t-statistics verified from the LSE working-paper PDF https://personal.lse.ac.uk/loud/Shocks.pdf: 10-year 5-day pre/post return differential 23.84 bps, t = 1.78; 5-year 22.54 bps, t = 3.67). Herb, P. (2025), "The treasury auction risk premium", Journal of Banking and Finance 170, 107316 (verified via search-result abstract only; full text not fetched -- the 30-year post-auction figures are therefore second-hand). Fleming, M.J., Liu, W. and Nguyen, G. (2026), "Intraday Price Pressure and Order Flow Around U.S. Treasury Auctions", FRBNY Staff Report 1188, https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/staff_reports/sr1188.html (verified). Auction cadence verified via treasurydirect.gov general-auction-timing and Treasury refunding statements. Tickers: TMF and TMV (Direxion Daily 20+ Year Treasury Bull/Bear 3X, both inception 2009-04-16); BIL = SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Month T-Bill, the pipeline's standard cash proxy.
distinctness_note: No catalog family uses Treasury auction dates or any supply-calendar event; the mechanism (dealer-inventory price pressure around anticipated supply) is unrelated to the catalog's price-based Treasury regimes (#60, #34, #17, #61) and to long_treasury_3x_fomc_window_drift's FOMC calendar (overlap of a session or two per year). It expresses a SHORT side through a real inverse product; TBF (-1x) is not used for the pre-leg because of its size. HONEST WEAKNESSES: (a) the 2013 multi-day evidence is on 2/5/10-year notes and the 10-year effect was marginal (t = 1.78); (b) the long-end support (Herb 2025) measures auction-to-secondary underpricing, part of which accrues before an ETF buyer's next-open entry; (c) the effect is a few basis points of yield per leg, so TMF/TMV spreads matter; (d) TMV's net assets (around two hundred million) sit at the bottom of the liquidity bar. Catalogued despite a low prior because it is a genuinely new mechanism with a two-sided expression, a free point-in-time date source, and ~500 expected trades; the DSR bar prices the multiple-testing cost.
directional_rationale: TMF buy-and-hold since 2009 is deeply negative and this rule is long duration for about 5 of every 21 sessions and short duration for about 5, so its beta to TMF buy-and-hold is near zero and its return cannot come from the level or trend of rates; the time-matched excess over TMF on the post-legs and over cash on the pre-legs directly tests the documented pre-auction concession and post-auction recovery.
rule_pseudocode:
A = sorted list of 30-year bond auction dates (TreasuryDirect export; new issues and reopenings), each known several sessions ahead via the tentative schedule. s(.) = NYSE session index.
On each decision session t (rotation engine: target chosen on t executes at the open of t+1), evaluate the EXECUTION session x = t+1:
  if there is an auction a with s(a)-4 <= s(x) <= s(a):        target = "TMV"   # pre-leg, 5 sessions a-4..a
  elif there is an auction a with s(a)+1 <= s(x) <= s(a)+5:    target = "TMF"   # post-leg, 5 sessions a+1..a+5
  else:                                                        target = "BIL"
  if both conditions hold for two different auctions (only possible if auctions fall fewer than 10 sessions apart, which the regular monthly schedule never does), the post-leg of the earlier auction wins.
Every target change is one trade (BIL -> TMV at session a-4, TMV -> TMF after the auction, TMF -> BIL after session a+5); typical sequence per auction: 3 trades. Decision uses only the published calendar as of t; no price inputs. ~12 auctions/year x 17 years x 3 = ~600 target changes; ~500 counted as TMV/TMF segments.

name: Post-split drift, pooled real split events across the expanded large-cap universe, 12-month hold from the first session after the split's effective date
mechanism: Managers self-select into forward splits when they expect strong performance, and the market underreacts: Ikenberry, Rankine and Stice (1996) find +7.9 percent year-one excess returns after 2-for-1 splits following a +3.4 percent announcement reaction; Ikenberry and Ramnath (2002) find ~9 percent one-year drift after splits of 5-for-4 or larger. This pooled real-event reformulation enters at the first session after the effective (ex) date -- the date yfinance provides -- and holds for the source's 12-month horizon.

parameters.event_source: yfinance Ticker.splits per traded name; index = first split-adjusted trading day
parameters.ratio_rule: ratio >= 1.25 and abs(12*ratio - round(12*ratio)) <= 0.005 (a true forward split ratio such as 5:4, 4:3, 3:2, 2:1, 3:1, 4:1, 5:1, 7:1, 10:1, 20:1); excludes spin-off / reorganization adjustment factors yfinance stores in the same series (factors that are not a whole-twelfth ratio, e.g. 1.281)
parameters.entry: open of the first trading day after the split-date bar
parameters.exit: time stop only: close of the 252nd bar after entry
parameters.pool: the pipeline's cached expanded universe: current S&P 500 + NASDAQ 100 constituents after dedup, with cached OHLC and dated bid/ask quotes from the pipeline's universe cache. Keep ONE share class per issuer (drop GOOG, keep GOOGL; likewise FOX/NWS-type duplicates) so a single corporate event is not counted twice. Survivorship caveat: current constituents only, the same convention as every other pooled family drawn from this universe; any result must disclose it.
parameters.retest: a separate family_id, charged as its own trial; it is NOT in any --retest list and has no pinned holdout to preserve. Catalog entry 63 is a distinct family and is unaffected by this one.

source: Ikenberry, D.L., Rankine, G. and Stice, E.K. (1996), "What do stock splits really signal?", JFQA 31(3), 357-375, https://www.jstor.org/stable/2331396 (verified 2026-09-04). Ikenberry, D.L. and Ramnath, S. (2002), "Underreaction to self-selected news events: the case of stock splits", RFS 15(2), 489-526 (verified). Counter-evidence, disclosed: Byun, J. and Rozeff, M.S. (2003), Journal of Finance 58(3), 1063-1085 (verified: 12-month buy-and-hold abnormal returns after splits not significantly different from zero over 1927-1996). Boehme, R.D. and Danielsen, B.R. (2007), Financial Review 42(4), 485-506 (verified: post-announcement returns do not persist after the actual split date, 1950-2000). Data facts (yfinance 1.4.1, 2026-09-04): 92 clean forward splits meeting the ratio rule 2000-01 to 2026-03-04 across the 100-name S&P 100 subset (31 since 2010; 20 in calendar 2000).
distinctness_note: NEW family_id: the catalog's stock_split_signaling_drift is the TOFR-ETF-proxy definition, kept unchanged, so the pooled real-split event study is a distinct family by the pipeline's mechanism x asset-class convention (single-stock corporate events vs a thematic ETF proxy). Honest read: both positive sources measure drift from the ANNOUNCEMENT date, and two later papers find it gone by the effective date; entering after the effective date tests the residual, disputed portion. Nothing is tuned: the 5-for-4 floor is Ikenberry-Ramnath's sample rule, the 12-month horizon is both sources' reporting horizon. Survivorship is a larger caveat here than for the dividend candidates (companies that split into a bubble and later left the index are missing); the directional panel is the corrective, and a beta_in_disguise flag is exactly the answer this test exists to give.
directional_rationale: A 12-month hold carries full market beta, so buy-and-hold comparison is essential: the documented drift (7-9 percent in year one from announcement, of which the post-effective-date share is disputed) must appear as positive alpha versus SPY and positive time-matched SPY excess; if the panel flags beta_in_disguise the family is rejected without a new trial being charged.

PRE: for ticker t load auto-adjusted OHLC and SPLITS[t] = {date S: ratio} from Ticker.splits; keep only ratio >= 1.25 with abs(12*ratio - round(12*ratio)) <= 0.005.
SIGNAL at bar i (date d, all data <= d):
  if flat: entry = (d in SPLITS[t])   [engine executes entry at the next bar's open = first session after the split-date bar]
  if in position: exit = False (time stop governs)
time_stop = 252 bars -> the engine closes the trade at the close of the 252nd bar after entry (reason time_stop). One position per ticker; a split occurring while a position is open is skipped. direction = long.
POOL: run independently for every ticker in expanded_universe_2026-08-29 (one share class per issuer), concatenate trades, score the pooled sample as ONE trial under this family's own family_id (a separate family charged as its own trial, per parameters.retest).
Point-in-time: the split-date bar is the first split-adjusted session, weeks after the public announcement; the signal reads only that the event has occurred.
Expected count: 92 on the 100-name subset; plausibly 200-300 on the 518-name pool.

name: Overnight-Minus-Intraday Return Continuation (Cross-Sectional, Pooled Large-Cap)
mechanism: Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019, JFE 134(1):192-213) show a strong monthly continuation effect when stocks are sorted on their trailing ONE-MONTH overnight return (their 'ret_night', Table 1, t=16.57 on the hedge portfolio) or trailing one-month intraday return ('ret_day') -- the paper's single strongest, most-cited, standalone per-stock decile-sort result. This family combines both named variables into one cross-sectional spread (ret_night_21d minus ret_day_21d, each a 21-trading-day compounded return) and ranks the existing 518-name large-cap universe monthly, going long the top decile (equal-weighted, continuous hold while in the top decile, matching the pooled long-only convention of large_cap_single_stock_pooled_tsmom.py). Two OTHER constructions in the same paper are not used: decomposing standard 12-1 momentum into its overnight-only leg (Sharpe 0.77 vs 0.31) needs an overnight-only execution capability this engine does not have; a 60-month half-life EWMA version of the same spread (the paper's own TugOfWar regime-timing variable) is not itself a standalone per-stock strategy in the source paper and its window is impractical against this repo's per-trade holdout.

parameters.pool: the pipeline's cached expanded universe: current S&P 500 + NASDAQ 100 constituents after dedup, with cached OHLC and dated bid/ask quotes from the pipeline's universe cache. Same resolved pool as large_cap_single_stock_pooled_tsmom. Survivorship caveat: current constituents only, same convention as every other pooled family drawn from this universe.
parameters.tie_break: longer history first, then ticker alphabetical

source: Lou, D., Polk, C. & Skouras, S. (2019), "A tug of war: Overnight versus intraday expected returns", Journal of Financial Economics 134(1), 192-213. Verified 2026-09-09 against the full paper (personal.lse.ac.uk/polk/research/TugOfWar.pdf): the ret_night/ret_day definitions are one-month (Table 1, Table 4). A 2026 NY Fed follow-up (Boyarchenko, Larsen & Whelan, 'The Disappearing Overnight Drift', Liberty Street Economics 2026) finds the closest-studied version of this class of edge decayed to roughly zero in 2021-2025, so this family may be decayed too.
distinctness_note: Mechanism is a cross-sectional rank on a trailing overnight-vs-intraday return SPREAD, distinct from every existing single-stock family: large_cap_single_stock_pooled_tsmom (own-history 12-month sign), fifty_two_week_high_momentum (nearness-to-high), pead_earnings_surprise_drift (earnings event), value/quality/buyback/accrual factors (fundamental ranks). No catalog family ranks names on the split between their own overnight and intraday return components.
directional_rationale: If overnight-vs-intraday return continuation genuinely persists at the individual-stock level (not just decayed to zero the way the whole-index-timing version has), a top-decile long-only tilt on it should show measurable excess over SPY out of sample; the null this family is built to test against is that the effect has already decayed to noise in the 2021-2025 window this holdout overlaps.
rule_pseudocode:
POOL = expanded_universe_2026-08-29 (same 518-ticker list as large_cap_single_stock_pooled_tsmom, copied verbatim)
for each T in POOL, at every bar t of its own history:
  overnight_t = Open_t / Close_{t-1} - 1
  intraday_t  = Close_t / Open_t - 1
  ret_night_21d(t) = prod_{i=t-20..t} (1+overnight_i) - 1
  ret_day_21d(t)   = prod_{i=t-20..t} (1+intraday_i) - 1   (undefined -- T excluded from that month's ranking -- if fewer than 21 valid trailing bars)
  signal(t) = ret_night_21d(t) - ret_day_21d(t)
at the close of the last trading day of each calendar month m (per ticker's own bar dates): rank all ELIGIBLE tickers by signal(m) descending, tie-break longer own history first then ticker alphabetical; if fewer than 100 tickers are eligible that month, nobody is selected that month
top_decile = round(10% of eligible count) highest-ranked tickers
if T in top_decile this month and position==FLAT: BUY T at the OPEN of the next trading session
if T not in top_decile this month and position==LONG: SELL T at the CLOSE of the next trading session
otherwise hold; no stops, no time exits; one trade = one contiguous holding period while T stays in the top decile across consecutive months
trades of all pool members concatenated into one sample (mining.pooling.pool_trades), scored as ONE trial

name: Cboe S&P 500 PutWrite Index Volatility-Regime Rotation (vs SPY)
mechanism: Rotates between SPY and the Cboe S&P 500 PutWrite Index (^PUT, a systematic short-put-writing benchmark collateralized by T-bills) on a realized-volatility regime signal computed from SPY's own trailing 21-trading-day squared log returns vs. an expanding all-history median -- structurally identical to vol_managed_smallcap_leverage_switch (TNA/IWM). Economic rationale (Cboe's own live PUT dashboard text, fetched 2026-09-09): PUT-write strategies tend to outperform in range-bound/bearish regimes and underperform in bull regimes, so the family holds the overlay when realized vol is elevated (above the expanding median) and SPY when vol is calm.
source: Cboe S&P 500 PutWrite Index (^PUT); data verified live 2026-09-09 via yfinance (7,566 daily bars, 1996-08-02 -> 2026-09-09, dense/gap-free except the real 2001 9/11 NYSE closure).
distinctness_note: Only family in the catalog trading a Cboe systematic options-overlay benchmark index rather than an equity/ETF/futures-proxy instrument; mechanism (SPY-vol-regime rotation into a short-put-writing benchmark) is distinct from every other rotation_two_asset family, all of which rotate between two directly-tradable instruments.
directional_rationale: If PUT-write's documented regime-dependent relative performance (outperforms range-bound/bearish, underperforms strong bull markets) genuinely persists and is capturable via a mechanical realized-vol regime switch, the rotation should show measurable excess over a static SPY holding out of sample; the null is that the regime-dependent relationship is too noisy or too slow-moving to capture at a monthly rebalance cadence, or that costs (here an assumed, deliberately conservative constant, not a measured quote) eat the edge.
rule_pseudocode:
SIGNAL_SOURCE = SPY
RV_t = sum over trailing 21 trading days ending at t (inclusive) of ln(Close_s/Close_{s-1})**2
MED_t = expanding median of {RV_u : u <= t}, undefined until 252 RV observations exist
at the close of the last trading day of each calendar month t:
  if RV_t <= MED_t (inclusive tie -> low variance): TARGET = SPY
  else: TARGET = PUT
TARGET executes at the t+1 open and is held unchanged (no intra-month re-evaluation) until the next month's decision
both legs' round-trip cost charged once per held segment: SPY from a captured quote, PUT from the module's disclosed ASSUMED_COST_BPS=25.0 (no quote exists for a non-tradable calculated index) -- the assumed cost is an open assumption
one trial (this family only; a BXM-based sibling is not catalogued because its yfinance feed carried a ~54-day data gap as of 2026-09-09)
pooling_note: resolved_pool: ["SPY","PUT"]

name: Synthetic 2x Leveraged Dip-Buy, Pooled Large-Cap (Margin-Financed)
mechanism: Buy a SYNTHETIC 2x margin-financed position (constructed from the underlying's own decades-long price history via data_pipeline.build_synthetic_leveraged, not a real too-young 2x single-stock ETF) whenever an individual large-cap stock closes at or below 80% of its own trailing 252-session high (of daily High). Exit at the first of: the synthetic position up 50% from its own entry price, or 252 sessions elapsed. Pooled across the existing 518-name S&P 500 + NASDAQ 100 universe.

parameters.pool: the pipeline's cached expanded universe: current S&P 500 + NASDAQ 100 constituents after dedup, with cached OHLC and dated bid/ask quotes from the pipeline's universe cache. Same resolved pool as large_cap_single_stock_pooled_tsmom. Survivorship caveat: current constituents only, same convention as every other pooled family drawn from this universe.

Mechanism (a percentage-drawdown entry with a percentage-gain profit target AND a time stop) is distinct from every other single-stock family: large_cap_single_stock_pooled_tsmom (12-month sign), fifty_two_week_high_momentum (nearness-to-high, not distance-below), overnight_intraday_tilt_pooled_largecap (overnight/intraday spread rank).     high_lookback = 252           # trading days ("52-week high")

    time_stop_sessions = 252      # or after 1 year, whichever first

               undefined until 252 sessions of history exist
      dip_flag_t = Close_t <= 0.80 * high_t
      while FLAT: on the first bar t where dip_flag_t is True, BUY the
        SYNTHETIC 2x position at the OPEN of bar t+1 (entry_price =
        synthetic Open_{t+1})
      while LONG: SELL at the first bar u (u > entry_fill_bar) where EITHER
        synthetic Close_u >= 1.50 * entry_price, OR
        (u - entry_fill_bar) >= 252
        whichever comes first, at synthetic Close_u
      if the dip condition is still True on the bar the position closed on
        (the exit bar itself), a NEW entry is decided there immediately --
        intended ("still oversold, buy again"), not prevented.
      one trade = one contiguous holding period; trades of all pool members
        concatenated into one sample, scored as ONE trial.

name: Capex Cycle Blue Chip Dip Pooled
mechanism: Buy a blue-chip S&P 500 stock (from a 25-name mechanical capex-growth watchlist) whenever it is BOTH (a) growing capex spend fast -- point-in-time YoY capex growth (SEC EDGAR XBRL, filed-date gated, never fiscal-period-end) >= 30% -- AND (b) concurrently underperforming SPY by >= 15 percentage points over the trailing 504 sessions (~2 years). Exit at the first of: either condition no longer holding, or 252 sessions held (a capex cycle playing out implies a bounded horizon, not an open-ended hold). Re-evaluated only at month-end bars, pooled across the 25-name watchlist, scored as one trial. Thesis: today's accelerating capex on AI/infrastructure pays off later, and the market hasn't yet priced that in for names concurrently lagging SPY -- distinguished from the well-documented OPPOSITE-signed unconditional capex/asset-growth anomaly (Titman/Wei/Xie 2004; Cooper/Gulen/Schill 2008, now the CMA factor) by requiring the SECOND, independent underperformance condition those papers never test. Mandatory falsification check: blue_chip_reversal_no_capex_control (identical rule minus the capex condition) -- if the capex-conditioned arm does not beat the control, capex added nothing.

parameters.watchlist_source: PENDING_CONFIRMATION -- objective mechanical rule: among S&P 500 names in the top 100 by CURRENT absolute capex, the 25 with the largest capex GROWTH multiple (recent disclosure / 2019-12-31 disclosure). N, base date, and level-floor rank are disclosed defaults, not yet confirmed; built by scripts/build_capex_watchlist.py

source: Design choices: the rule above; watchlist methodology in src/mining/capex_watchlist.py, built by scripts/build_capex_watchlist.py.

name: Blue Chip Reversal No Capex Control
mechanism: MANDATORY control arm for capex_cycle_blue_chip_dip_pooled, not a separate hypothesis -- IDENTICAL 25-name watchlist, IDENTICAL underperformance condition (>= 15pp trailing-504-session underperformance vs SPY)/window, IDENTICAL exit rule (signal-off or 252-session time stop), with the capex-growth condition REMOVED entirely ("buy blue-chip losers vs SPY, no capex filter"). Falsifies the main family's own honest residual risk: any edge found in the capex-conditioned arm could simply be ordinary price-reversal (De Bondt-Thaler and descendants) with the capex filter contributing nothing, or actively hurting (Titman/Wei/Xie 2004 and Cooper/Gulen/Schill 2008 both find high-capex firms earn WORSE forward returns unconditionally). It has its own catalog entry so it can be scored either as its own trial or as an unscored falsification check.

name: Sector Breadth Collapse Leverage Flip (SPXL/SPXS, % sectors above 50-day MA, 70/30 hysteresis)
mechanism: Using the sector SPDR panel's percent-above-moving-average breadth statistic (fraction of the 11 Select Sector SPDR funds trading above their own trailing 50-session mean), hold the leveraged bull fund SPXL (Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3X) by default. When that fraction falls to or below 0.30 (the source's own 'oversold' level -- sector participation has COLLAPSED to a minority), flip into the leveraged bear fund SPXS (Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bear 3X) at the next session's open. When it recovers to or above 0.70 (the source's 'overbought' level), flip back into SPXL. Never in cash: every session holds one 3x leg, so the flip between bull and bear leverage -- not a move to cash -- is what is tested, following the same real-leveraged-product execution convention as vol_managed_smallcap_leverage_switch and small_cap_tsmom_long_inverse_rotation.
source: StockCharts ChartSchool, "Percent Above Moving Average", https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/market-indicators/percent-above-moving-average (fetched 2026-09-17: defines the indicator as stocks-above-a-specified-length-MA divided by total stocks in the index; common lengths 50-day short-to-medium-term, 150/200-day medium-to-long-term; 50% marks bull/bear bias, readings above 70% are 'deemed overbought' and below 30% 'deemed oversold'; explicitly discusses a falling indicator against a rising market as 'underlying weakness'). Applied to the sector-fund panel (11 members) rather than full-index constituents, exactly as sector_breadth_thrust_zweig and sector_ad_line_divergence_derisk already do, with the same disclosed coarseness caveat. The 3x/-3x LEVERAGED-FLIP EXECUTION (SPXL/SPXS in place of cash) is NOT from this source -- pre-registered a priori, following the same real-leveraged-product convention as vol_managed_smallcap_leverage_switch and small_cap_tsmom_long_inverse_rotation. Tickers verified 2026-09-17: SPXL = Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3X Shares, inception 2008-11-05; SPXS = Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bear 3X Shares, inception 2008-11-05 (Direxion fund fact sheets; both actively trading). Breadth indicator: computed on the pipeline's point-in-time sector_spdr_11 membership basis via mining.panel.breadth_participation (participation_above_ma, window=50, min_members=9); mining.panel_signals names percent-of-members-above-their-own moving average as one of its three panel breadth statistics, and this is the first catalog family to use it.
distinctness_note: First catalog family to use the participation_above_ma (percent of sectors above their own trailing moving average) breadth statistic -- distinct from sector_breadth_thrust_zweig (a 10-day EMA of the ADVANCING-SHARE net-advance ratio, event-triggered on a rising transition, response = buy-and-hold SPY for a fixed 63 sessions) and sector_ad_line_divergence_derisk (a cumulative advance-decline LINE compared against SPY's own six-month high, response = flat cash for 21 sessions). Also distinct from rsp_spy_breadth_ratio, which is a price-ratio moving-average cross of two ETFs (RSP/SPY, a cap-weight-vs-equal-weight breadth PROXY), never a direct percent-of-members statistic. Not a duplicate of the core index-ETF exposure: the only other family trading SPXL/SPXS is quarterly_index_rebalance_flow_leverage_window (a five-session calendar-rebalancing window, not a breadth regime), and the ruled_out 3x families (qqq_tqqq_orb / nine_sig_tqqq_value_averaging / overnight_drift) involve TQQQ, never an S&P-tracking 3x pair. Same leveraged-flip EXECUTION precedent as vol_managed_smallcap_leverage_switch (TNA/IWM, signal = realized variance) and small_cap_tsmom_long_inverse_rotation (IWM/RWM, signal = trailing-return sign vote) but a different asset class (S&P 500 3x, not small caps) and a different signal family entirely (sector-panel breadth, not a price-only statistic of the traded instrument itself).
directional_rationale: The strategy holds one 3x leg at all times (never cash), so alpha over SPY buy-and-hold must come from correctly TIMING which leg is held, not from average beta. The bear leg's daily reset imposes a real decay cost on every session it is held while SPY does not fall, so the rule earns its keep only if breadth-collapse sessions are followed by SPY returns bad enough, often enough, to outweigh that decay during the whipsaw sessions around a real regime turn. Evaluate on alpha / time-matched SPY excess, not raw Sharpe (same convention as the catalog's other leveraged-flip rotation families), since ~3x average beta magnitude before leverage-adjustment misleads a raw comparison.
rule_pseudocode:
part_t = participation_above_ma snapshot value as of session t (None strictly before the snapshot's first defined session, 1999-03-05; SPXL/SPXS both trade from 2008-11-05 onward so in practice always already defined over the traded history).
standing initialized to None.
for each session t in the shared SPXL/SPXS calendar (in order):
    if part_t is None: standing unchanged
    elif standing is None: standing = SPXL if part_t >= 0.50 else SPXS   # one-time seed on the first-ever defined session, NOT sourced
    elif standing == SPXL and part_t <= 0.30: standing = SPXS
    elif standing == SPXS and part_t >= 0.70: standing = SPXL
    else: standing unchanged                                            # inside the 0.30-0.70 hysteresis band
    decision(t) = standing
if decision(t) != current holding: the rotation engine closes the current holding and opens decision(t) at the next session's open (engine convention); if unchanged: hold, no churn. No stops, no cash state, no other exits.

name: Quarter-end calendar-rebalancing flow (Harvey-Mazzoleni-Melone), leveraged S&P 500 window (SPXL/SPXS)
mechanism: Generalizes the sibling family month_end_rebalancing_flow_rotation's mechanism (Harvey, Mazzoleni & Melone's calendar-rebalancing price pressure: funds with a scheduled calendar reset must sell equities when stocks have outperformed bonds since the last reset and buy when they have underperformed) from a MONTHLY reset to a QUARTERLY reset -- a real, distinct institutional review cadence (many pension and endowment mandates rebalance quarterly rather than monthly), expressed through a leveraged pair instead of a 1x/inverse pair. At the close of the sixth-to-last session of the calendar quarter (Q-6) compute the quarter-to-date equity-weight deviation of a simulated 60/40 SPY/IEF portfolio from 60%; if equities are overweight hold the 3x-short S&P 500 fund (SPXS), if underweight hold the 3x-long S&P 500 fund (SPXL), for the following five sessions (enter at the fifth-to-last session's open, exit at the last session's open); flat the rest of the quarter. The signal itself is computed on the UNLEVERAGED SPY series (a daily-reset 3x product's own multi-session return is not 3x the underlying's due to volatility drag, so using SPXL/SPXS closes for a quarter-long deviation would mix the rebalancing signal with leverage decay) -- only the EXECUTED position is leveraged.

parameters.equity_proxy: SPXL (traded, 3x S&P 500 long -- ProShares/Direxion leveraged expression of the SPY signal)
parameters.bond_proxy: IEF, iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF -- signal only, unleveraged
parameters.signal: w_dev = 0.6*(1+R_e) / (0.6*(1+R_e) + 0.4*(1+R_b)) - 0.6, where R_e and R_b are the UNLEVERAGED S&P 500 (SPY-equivalent, read from SPXL's own 3x daily-reset series is NOT used for the signal -- see signal_price_source) and IEF adjusted-close cumulative returns from the previous quarter's last session close to the close of session Q-6 (Q = the quarter's last XNYS session)
parameters.signal_price_source: SPY (unleveraged) closes are used to compute R_e -- SPXL/SPXS are daily-reset 3x products whose multi-session cumulative return is NOT 3x the underlying's cumulative return (volatility drag), so using SPXL's own closes for a quarter-long deviation would mix the rebalancing signal with leverage decay; the signal is computed on the unleveraged index and only the EXECUTED position is leveraged
parameters.hold_window: sessions Q-5 through Q-1: enter at Q-5 open, exit at Q open (target set at Q-6, cleared at Q-1)
parameters.reset_frequency: calendar quarter (Jan-Mar, Apr-Jun, Jul-Sep, Oct-Dec), not calendar month
parameters.quarter_end_scaling: none -- one uniform rule every quarter

source: Harvey, C.R., Mazzoleni, M.G. & Melone, A. (2025, revised January 2026), "The Unintended Consequences of Rebalancing", NBER Working Paper 33554 (also SSRN 5122748), https://www.nber.org/papers/w33554 (same source as the sibling family month_end_rebalancing_flow_rotation, verified 2026-09-17: simulated 60/40 stock-bond portfolio, calendar-based rebalancers create predictable price pressure concentrated in the sessions before a scheduled reset). REFORMULATION DISCLOSURE: the paper's own empirical measurement (the ~17bps/day next-day-return effect) is at MONTHLY rebalancing frequency; no quarterly-frequency magnitude is measured by this source or claimed here -- this family applies the SAME signal construction to a quarterly reset as a distinct, real institutional calendar-rebalancing cadence, not a re-measurement of the paper's own monthly finding. Quarter-end as a recognized, separate institutional calendar-rebalancing review point (distinct from month-end) is corroborated by https://globalmarketstructure.com/en/capital-flows-and-positioning/passive-etf-and-rebalancing-flows/pension-fund-rebalancing/ (verified via web search 2026-09-17: "Calendar rules are tied to scheduled review points, often around month-end, quarter-end, or other policy dates"), which documents quarter-end as a genuine calendar-rebalancing convention without itself quantifying a price effect -- no magnitude is drawn from that source. Tickers: SPXL = Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3X Shares, inception 2008-11-05, yfinance history from 2008-11-05 (verified live 2026-09-17); SPXS = Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bear 3X Shares, inception 2008-11-05, yfinance history from 2008-11-19 (verified live 2026-09-17); SPY and IEF as already verified by the sibling entry.
distinctness_note: Directly related to, and DISTINCT from, month_end_rebalancing_flow_rotation (this catalog): same root citation and w_dev formula, but (a) a QUARTERLY reset instead of monthly -- a different, real institutional rebalancing clientele, not the same effect resampled -- so segments occur ~4x/year instead of ~12x/year and the quarter-to-date deviation accumulates over roughly 3x as many sessions before the Q-6 decision; (b) a 3x LEVERAGED pair (SPXL/SPXS) instead of a 1x/inverse pair (SPY/SH), amplifying the lower-frequency signal rather than trading it 1x -- the 'leverage window' in the family name. Also distinct from triple_witching_week_effect (this catalog), which shares a similar quarterly calendar cadence (both key off the quarter's final sessions) but an ENTIRELY DIFFERENT economic mechanism: triple_witching is driven by simultaneous derivatives (futures/options) expiration unwind and pinning, not by passive calendar-rebalancer stock-bond flow, trades the week AROUND the third Friday (not a T-6-to-T-1 pre-reset window), and is a fixed long-only index position with no directional sign flip. Also distinct from sp500_index_addition_effect (this catalog), which is a per-stock event study on index ADDITIONS/DELETIONS (a different company on a different date each time, no standing exposure), not a standing calendar-timed index-level rotation. Also distinct from vol_managed_smallcap_leverage_switch (this catalog), which also trades a real leveraged product (TNA) but on US small caps with a realized-variance signal reset monthly, not an S&P 500 stock-bond calendar-rebalancing signal reset quarterly. Not MA, momentum or regime timing of the index; not a disguised long-market beta, since the position sign flips with the signal and is held only 5 of roughly 60 sessions a quarter, same directional-purity argument the sibling family already makes.
directional_rationale: The position flips sign with the signal -- 3x short the index when quarterly rebalancers must sell and 3x long when they must buy -- and is held only five of roughly sixty sessions a quarter, so a positive result cannot be a disguised long-market beta at 3x leverage; a beta-in-disguise check (time spent long vs short, and time-matched excess over SPY conditioned on the held side) is the natural read, same convention the sibling family and the batch5 directional-support panel already apply.
rule_pseudocode:
CAL = XNYS sessions (calendar-known, so Q is known in advance); for each calendar quarter let Q = its last session and Q-k the k-th session before Q
prev_Q(quarter) = last session of the previous quarter
target_fn(frames):   # called on every decision bar d; the engine executes the returned target at d+1 open; frames hold SPXL, SPXS (traded), IEF and SPY (signal) truncated through d
  d = frames['SPY'].index[-1]
  if d == Q-6 of its quarter:
     R_e = Close_SPY[d] / Close_SPY[prev_Q] - 1; R_b = Close_IEF[d] / Close_IEF[prev_Q] - 1   # adjusted closes; return None if either close is missing
     w_dev = 0.6*(1+R_e) / (0.6*(1+R_e) + 0.4*(1+R_b)) - 0.6
     state = 'SPXS' if w_dev > 0 else ('SPXL' if w_dev < 0 else None); return state
  if d in {Q-5, Q-4, Q-3, Q-2}: return state   # hold
  return None                                  # at d = Q-1 the None target closes the position at Q's open; flat until next quarter's Q-6
run_two_asset_rotation({'SPXL': spxl, 'SPXS': spxs}, target_fn, signal_frames={'IEF': ief, 'SPY': spy}, cost_bps_by_asset = measured round-trips)
One five-session segment per quarter; no other parameters.
pooling_note: resolved_pool: ["SPXL","SPXS"]

name: Sector Dispersion Regime Cyclical Stance (XLY)
mechanism: Each trading day, compute the cross-sectional return dispersion (RD) across a panel of the 9 original S&P Select Sector SPDR ETFs (XLB, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLU, XLV, XLY) -- the standard deviation, across the 9 sectors, of that day's own simple return. Smooth RD with a trailing 20-day rolling mean and compare it to its OWN trailing 252-day rolling mean to classify each day as a LOW- or HIGH-dispersion regime. Hold Consumer Discretionary (XLY) -- the classic higher-beta, momentum/procyclical-sensitive sector -- only while the regime reads LOW; exit to cash the moment it flips HIGH. This follows the documented countercyclical-state-variable role of cross-sectional return dispersion: low RD precedes stronger momentum/procyclical conditions, high RD precedes stronger value/countercyclical conditions, so a low-RD regime is the window in which leaning into a cyclical sector is best supported by the literature. Rebalance only on a regime flip, not on every daily dispersion print. Implementation note: signal_fn needs the full 9-ticker panel's daily returns (via data_pipeline.fetch_ohlc per ticker, aligned by date), not just XLY's own frame -- same 'fetch extra tickers inside signal_fn' pattern as the other regime-gated candidates in this catalog.
source: Stivers, C.T. & Sun, L. (2010), "Cross-Sectional Return Dispersion and Time-Variation in Value and Momentum Premiums," Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis, 45(4), 987-1014 -- documents cross-sectional return dispersion (RD) as a leading countercyclical state variable, negatively related to the subsequent momentum/procyclical premium and positively related to the subsequent value/countercyclical premium. Sector-level practitioner framing of the identical statistic (cross-sectional standard deviation of daily sector returns): Morningstar Indexes, "Dispersion as a Gauge of Market Regime" (indexes.morningstar.com/insights/analysis/bltca007ed69ad2ef48/dispersion-as-a-gauge-of-market-regime). Verified via web search 2026-09-17. Ticker verified: XLY = Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF, State Street, inception 1998-12-16, actively trading -- same inception cohort as XLB/XLE/XLF/XLI/XLK/XLP/XLU/XLV (the 9 original Select Sector SPDRs); XLRE (2015) and XLC (2018) are deliberately excluded from the dispersion panel to avoid either truncating the whole series to a post-2018 start or requiring a panel whose membership changes over time. DISTINCTNESS NOTE: gates a single cyclical sector's exposure (XLY vs. cash) on a cross-sectional DISPERSION (second-moment) regime computed across a 9-instrument panel -- distinct from defensive_sector_recession_signal_rotation (rotates between two named tickers on a yield-curve LEVEL signal) and from every price-trend/relative-strength-ranking candidate already in this catalog.
