directional_rationale: Cross-sectional return dispersion is a documented leading countercyclical state variable (Stivers & Sun 2010): a low-dispersion regime has historically preceded stronger momentum/procyclical conditions, so the mechanism holds the higher-beta, momentum-sensitive Consumer Discretionary sector only in that regime and steps to cash the moment dispersion regimes to high (countercyclical conditions favored).
rule_pseudocode: PANEL: daily simple returns across the 9 original Select Sector SPDRs (mining.signals.DISPERSION_PANEL). SIGNAL: dispersion_t = cross-sectional std (ddof=1) of that day's panel returns (mining.signals.sector_dispersion). REGIME: smoothed_t = trailing 20-session mean of dispersion_t; regime_t = 'low' if smoothed_t < its own trailing 252-session mean, else 'high' (a tie or a date before either rolling window fills reads as 'high', i.e. flat) (mining.signals.dispersion_regime). DECISION: hold XLY when regime_t=='low', flat otherwise, rebalancing only on a regime flip (mining.signals.make_sector_dispersion_cyclical_stance_signal_fn).

name: Retail sector inventory/sales breadth short (XRT)
mechanism: Using SEC EDGAR XBRL inventory (InventoryNet and real retail-specific sibling tags) and sales/revenue tags for a liquid retail-sector universe (XRT's own real, current holdings), short XRT for the following quarter when sector-wide breadth of retailers showing inventory growth outpacing sales growth crosses a threshold (0.50 of the coverage-checked universe, re-evaluated -- and rolled forward while still triggered -- every quarter-end). Distinct from the price/momentum sector families and from the capex-based EDGAR families in this catalog: a different fundamental axis (inventory/sales divergence, not capital-spending growth).

parameters.universe_source: CONFIRMED: XRT's own current holdings (a dated snapshot of the fund sponsor's daily holdings file), coverage-checked by mining.retail_inventory_coverage, applied backward over the full backtest window. Disclosed survivorship-bias caveat: retailers delisted for distress (e.g. Sears, Toys R Us, Bed Bath & Beyond, RadioShack) are invisible to this proxy universe -- judged CONSERVATIVE (understates real crisis-period breadth rather than inflating it), same disclosed-caveat convention as money_market_fund_flow_riskoff's burn-in issue.

distinctness_note: No prior catalog family shorts a sector ETF driven by a cross-sectional EDGAR fundamentals breadth measure. The capex-cycle candidates (capex_cycle_blue_chip_dip_pooled, blue_chip_reversal_no_capex_control) use capex growth vs SPY underperformance on individual blue-chip names, a different fundamental (capital spending, not inventory/sales) and a different construction (pooled per-name longs, not a single sector-ETF short driven by cross-sectional breadth).
source: Bernard, V.L. & Thomas, J.K. (1989), "Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Delayed Price Response or Risk Premium?", Journal of Accounting Research 27, 1-36 (the same foundational inventory/margin-compression-adjacent anomaly literature already cited elsewhere in this catalog for PEAD candidates) -- this candidate's own mechanism (sector-wide inventory-vs-sales breadth) is a DISTINCT construction, not a relabeling. Universe: XRT's current holdings from State Street's official daily holdings file. Implementation: src/mining/batch5/retail_inventory_sales_breadth_short.py, the coverage check in src/mining/retail_inventory_coverage.py (scripts/run_retail_inventory_coverage_check.py) and EDGAR instant-concept parsing in src/mining/edgar_data.py (InventoryNet is a balance-sheet 'instant' XBRL concept, not a duration concept like capex/revenue). The coverage check excludes holdings without a usable point-in-time inventory AND revenue series, for example marketplace/platform businesses that carry no traditional inventory. A rough backtest (scripts/run_retail_inventory_breadth_mining.py) runs through the generic backtest engine with direction=short and GROSS returns only when no usable regular-hours XRT spread sample is available (a cost number is never invented). This family is subject to ABI-1 scoring like any other.

name: Margin Debt Deleverage Synthetic Leverage Flip (SPY 2x synthetic / SH)
mechanism: FINRA aggregate NYSE member-firm customer margin-debt month-over-month deceleration/contraction flips equity exposure between a synthetic 2x margin-financed long position in SPY (data_pipeline.build_synthetic_leveraged, the same construction synthetic_leveraged_dip_buy_pooled_largecap.py already uses) and the real inverse ETF SH. Positive MoM growth (leverage/risk appetite still expanding, even if decelerating in rate) -> hold the synthetic 2x SPY position; MoM growth crosses to zero or below (the debt level itself contracted month over month -- forced deleveraging, margin calls, reduced risk appetite) -> hold SH (real short S&P 500 exposure), not cash. Never sits in cash: it flips the full leverage direction, so a false signal costs a real round-trip through both legs.
source: FINRA Margin Statistics, finra.org/rules-guidance/key-topics/margin-accounts/margin-statistics, monthly, from Jan 1997 -- same source series as margin_debt_growth_regime, reused unchanged (mining.signals.finra_margin_debt_growth_available_series with lookback_months=1 instead of that sibling family's 12). signal_lag_trading_days=20 is reused verbatim from margin_debt_growth_regime's pre-registered constant and carries the same disclosed residual risk (FINRA's true publication lag can run past 20 sessions in some months).
distinctness_note: Distinct from margin_debt_growth_regime (implemented under two constructions): that family holds SPY outright and exits to cash on a trailing-12-month (YoY) growth sign flip. This family (a) uses a month-over-month (1-month) lookback -- a genuinely faster, noisier read on credit-cycle deceleration, not a parameter tweak of the 12-month construct -- and (b) never sits in cash: it flips the full leverage direction, 2x-long to -1x, so a false signal costs a real round-trip through both legs' spreads and the daily-reset inverse fund's own volatility decay, which the YoY/cash sibling never pays.
directional_rationale: Aggregate margin debt is a systemwide leverage/risk-appetite proxy; a month-over-month contraction in the debt level itself (not merely decelerating growth) marks a materially sharper deleveraging signal than a trailing-12-month growth-rate sign flip, so the mechanism trades the full long/short leverage swing rather than a long/cash regime hold.
rule_pseudocode: SIGNAL: growth_t = known-as-of-t month-over-month % change in FINRA aggregate margin debt (margin_debt_lookback_months=1), lagged signal_lag_trading_days=20 real trading sessions past each month's own month-end (mining.signals.finra_margin_debt_growth_available_series). THRESHOLD: growth_threshold=0. DECISION: risk_on_known_t = growth_known_t > 0 -> hold SPY_2x_synthetic (leverage=2.0, data_pipeline.build_synthetic_leveraged); else -> hold SH. Re-evaluated daily off the as-of-known value via mining.signals.make_external_regime_target_fn. Common-history note: SH's inception (2006-06-21) is the binding common-inception floor for the in-sample window, not SPY's own 1993 start.
liquidity_basis: The synthetic 2x SPY leg is priced off a captured SPY bid/ask quote (regular session); the SH leg is priced off a captured SH quote. No liquidity claim is made for the FINRA margin-debt series itself, which is never traded.

name: Single-Session Extreme-Decline Reversal (SPY)
mechanism: Compute SPY's daily close-to-close log return r_t = ln(Close_t / Close_{t-1}). Compute a trailing 20-trading-session realized volatility as the sample standard deviation (ddof=1) of the 20 daily log returns strictly PRECEDING session t (never including r_t itself, so the trigger day cannot inflate or deflate its own normalizer). Define z_t = r_t / trailing_vol_t -- a SINGLE SESSION's own close-to-close return expressed in trailing-volatility units, not a multi-day cumulative return and not an intraday reading. When z_t <= -2.5 (an extreme, one-day decline relative to SPY's own recent volatility regime), enter long at the next session's open. Hold for a fixed 3 trading sessions, then exit at that session's close; no other exit condition (no stop-loss, no signal-based early exit, no rebalancing). One position at a time: a fresh trigger while a hold from an earlier trigger is still open is skipped.
source: Cox, D.R. & Peterson, D.R. (1994), "Stock Returns Following Large One-Day Declines: Evidence on Short-Term Reversals and Longer-Term Performance", The Journal of Finance, 49(1), 255-267, DOI 10.1111/j.1540-6261.1994.tb04428.x (the same citation as this catalog's intraday_capitulation_reversal_bar record, verified via web search 2026-08-31). This family applies the same documented phenomenon (large one-day declines followed by short-term reversal) as a literal daily-bar, close-to-close, z-score-normalized signal -- no intraday bar, no 14:00 ET cutoff, no reversal-bar/volume confirmation (those are intraday_capitulation_reversal_bar's own additions on top of the same underlying literature). Ticker verified: SPY, State Street, inception 1993.
rule_pseudocode: SIGNAL: r_t = ln(Close_t/Close_{t-1}); trailing_vol_t = std(ddof=1) of r_{t-20}..r_{t-1}, strictly before t (mining.batch5.single_day_extreme_decline_reversal_long.trigger_zscore). ENTRY: z_t = r_t/trailing_vol_t <= -2.5 on session t (mining.batch5.single_day_extreme_decline_reversal_long.trigger_positions); the engine's own next-bar-open execution (backtest_engine.run_backtest) fills at session t+1's open. EXIT: fixed time stop -- held == 3 sessions from the fill, then exit at that session's close; no other exit condition. Because mining.abi1_driver.build_single_asset_curve calls run_backtest WITHOUT its own time_stop argument, the 3-session hold is expressed by this module's own precomputed exit schedule (mining.batch5.single_day_extreme_decline_reversal_long.entry_exit_positions), not the engine's time_stop parameter. One position at a time: a trigger while an earlier hold is open is skipped.
distinctness_note: Deliberately narrower than three existing catalog families (quoting each one's catalog mechanism): (1) large_decline_rebound triggers on "the trailing 10-trading-day cumulative close-to-close return" dropping below -10%, holds 5 days -- a 10-DAY CUMULATIVE trigger, not this family's single-session return. (2) short_term_reversal_weekly triggers on "the trailing 5-trading-day (1-week) cumulative close-to-close return" z-scored against "its own trailing 1-year distribution of 5-day returns" at a -1.5 threshold, holds 5 days -- a 5-DAY CUMULATIVE return z-scored against a distribution of 5-day returns, not this family's single session's own return z-scored against a trailing 20-session volatility at a stricter -2.5 threshold. (3) intraday_capitulation_reversal_bar triggers when "intraday percentage decline from the prior session's close" using 5-minute bars "first reaches at least 5% by 14:00 ET" plus a reversal-bar/volume confirmation, enters same-day, holds up to 20 days -- an INTRADAY, minute-bar trigger this family never reads (this family's trigger fires only after the full session has printed its own close, and it enters the FOLLOWING session, never same-day). None of the three can fire on one ordinary single-session decline the way this family's trigger does.

name: VWAP-Cross Decaying-Conviction Exit (Day Trade)
mechanism: Enters long, long-only, on the same session-VWAP-cross confirmation as the sibling vwap_trend_intraday_scalp family: vwap_confirmation_bars consecutive 1-minute closes strictly above the running, 09:30 ET-anchored session VWAP. The exit is entirely different: at the fill, a fixed take-profit distance (base_target_pct) and stop-loss distance (base_stop_pct) are recorded as a fraction of entry price, and BOTH distances shrink monotonically toward a floor (floor_fraction of the base distance, never zero) via exponential decay of the excess above that floor, with a half_life_minutes half-life -- modeling declining conviction the longer the move takes to happen: a stalled trade looks for a smaller win and protects a smaller loss instead of holding the original, wider levels indefinitely. Force-flat by 15:55 ET regardless of whether TP/SL has fired, matching the sibling's own force-flat time -- no position is ever carried past the same session's close.
source: Entry mechanism (session-VWAP-cross confirmation) reused, mirrored not modified, from this catalog's own vwap_trend_intraday_scalp family (day_trading_signals.py, make_vwap_trend_intraday_scalp_signal_fn), itself sourced to Zarattini, C. and Aziz, A. (2023), 'Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP): The Holy Grail for Day Trading Systems', SSRN Working Paper 4631351. The decaying-conviction take-profit/stop-loss exit is an original hypothesis constructed for this mining candidate -- disclosed explicitly as NOT drawn from a published source, rather than misattributed to one. Its starting TP/SL magnitudes (1.0% target / 0.5% stop) are benchmarked against this codebase's own selling_climax_capitulation_bounce_daytrade family (day_trading_signals.py, make_selling_climax_capitulation_bounce_daytrade_signal_fn, profit_target_pct=0.01/trailing_stop_pct=0.005) -- the only other pct-of-entry-price (not ATR-multiple) day-track TP/SL pair already in this codebase.
distinctness_note: Sibling of vwap_trend_intraday_scalp (day_trading_signals.py, make_vwap_trend_intraday_scalp_signal_fn): this family reuses that sibling's identical session-VWAP-cross confirmed-entry logic (vwap_confirmation_bars consecutive closes strictly above the running, 09:30 ET-anchored session VWAP), mirrored/cited rather than copied-and-modified in place. The exit mechanism is where the two families genuinely diverge: vwap_trend_intraday_scalp exits on a CONFIRMED REVERSE VWAP CROSS (flip-based, no take-profit/stop-loss at all, gated by min_hold_minutes), while this family instead opens a fixed take-profit/stop-loss pair at entry and lets BOTH distances shrink monotonically toward a floor as the trade ages -- a time-decaying 'conviction' exit modeling the idea that a VWAP-trend thesis which hasn't played out yet deserves a smaller target and a tighter protective stop, not the same wide levels held indefinitely. This family never checks the below-VWAP condition once in a position -- it is a pure price-level exit, not a trend-reversal exit, and the two exit conditions can never fire each other's trigger. This family is also LONG-ONLY, mirroring the sibling's own long-only scope exactly; the mechanism's natural short mirror is not part of this family.
pooling_note: Single-ticker-specific for its first test, mirroring the sibling family's own QQQ representative choice -- the decaying-conviction exit hypothesis is orthogonal to ticker selection, so QQQ (the sibling's own first-test instrument) is the natural first test rather than a placeholder for a wider pool.

name: Presidential Election Cycle -- Year 3 / Pre-Election Year Seasonal (SPY)
mechanism: US presidential elections fall in years divisible by 4 (2024, 2028, ...). Wong & McAleer (2009) analyze weekly S&P 500 index data 1965-2003 and find that US equity prices systematically peak in the third and fourth years of a presidential term and are weakest in the first two, identifying the presidential election cycle as the single most dominant cycle detected in the data -- commonly attributed to incumbent administrations and the Federal Reserve front-loading stimulative fiscal/monetary policy ahead of a re-election year (an incumbent-incentive mechanism, not a claim about either political party). Holds SPY long for the ENTIRE calendar year whenever that year is "Year 3" of the 4-year cycle -- the pre-election year, where year % 4 == 3 (e.g. 1995, 1999, 2003, ..., 2023, 2027) -- flat/cash in every other year (Years 1, 2 and 4). Rebalances (enters or exits) at most twice per 4-year cycle, never mid-year.
source: Wong, W.-K. & McAleer, M. (2009), "Mapping the Presidential Election Cycle in US Stock Markets", Mathematics and Computers in Simulation, 79(11), 3267-3277, DOI 10.1016/j.matcom.2009.05.007 (verified via web search 2026-09-17) -- this family's primary, falsifiable, peer-reviewed citation. Corroborating practitioner source (background only, not itself the falsifiable citation): Yale Hirsch's "Stock Trader's Almanac" four-year cycle tables (popularized since the 1960s) report Year 3 (the pre-election year) as the strongest of the four cycle years by a wide margin; figures vary by compilation source window. Ticker verified: SPY, SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust, State Street, inception 1993-01-29.
rule_pseudocode: IN-SEASON TEST: for a bar dated in calendar year Y, in_season(Y) = ((Y - target_year_offset_from_election) % cycle_length_years == election_year_modulus), i.e. Y % 4 == 3 (mining.batch5.presidential_cycle_year3_seasonal.in_season_mask). ENTRY: entry[t] = in_season(year of bar t+1) -- flagged one bar before every in-season bar so the engine's own next-bar-open fill (backtest_engine.run_backtest) lands on the season's own first open (mining.batch5.presidential_cycle_year3_seasonal.season_decisions). EXIT: exit[t] = in_season(year of bar t) and not in_season(year of bar t+1) -- fires on the season's own last trading day, filled at that bar's close. The bucket's own final bar never signals exit on its own account (deferred to the engine's end_of_data close). One position at a time; the season's whole-calendar-year span means no re-entry risk within a season.
distinctness_note: No other catalog family keys off any multi-year political or election cycle. Verbatim mechanism text of the three nearest existing siblings by theme (broad-market calendar/seasonal equity rules): (1) halloween_indicator_seasonal -- "Hold equity index ETF exposure only November-April (the 'winter' half of the calendar year), flat or in cash May-October." An ANNUAL, EVERY-YEAR six-month split; this family fires in only ONE of every FOUR years and holds the WHOLE calendar year. (2) santa_claus_rally_yearend -- "Go long a broad equity index ETF at the close of the 6th-to-last trading day of the calendar year ... hold through the close of the 2nd trading day of the new January ... a fixed 7-trading-day seasonal window each year end." An EVERY-YEAR, 7-TRADING-DAY window straddling New Year's; this family's window is an entire calendar year, occurs once per 4 years, and never straddles a year boundary. (3) january_small_cap_seasonal -- "Hold small-cap equity exposure only during the calendar month of January ... stay in cash or a risk-free proxy the rest of the year." An EVERY-YEAR, ONE-MONTH, SMALL-CAP-specific window attributed to a post-tax-loss-selling rebound; this family trades broad-market SPY, holds a full calendar year, fires once every 4 years, and its driver (a documented political-economic cycle in aggregate market prices) has nothing to do with tax-loss selling or any single calendar month. None of the three, nor any other catalog entry, expresses a rule whose periodicity is 4 calendar years rather than 1.

name: Bitcoin Extreme-Decline Spillover Risk-Off (QQQ)
mechanism: Fetch BTC-USD daily spot OHLC (Kraken public spot market, mining.crypto_data.fetch_kraken_spot_ohlcv). Compute BTC's own daily log return r_t = ln(Close_t/Close_{t-1}) on BTC's own calendar (crypto trades every day). Compute a trailing 20-day realized volatility as the sample standard deviation (ddof=1) of the 20 daily log returns strictly PRECEDING day t (never including r_t itself). Define z_t = r_t / trailing_vol_t. When z_t <= -2.0 (an extreme single-day BTC decline relative to BTC's own recent volatility regime), reduce QQQ exposure to cash for a 5-calendar-day cooldown window starting that day (a later trigger inside an open cooldown extends it forward, never shortens it). Outside a risk-off window, hold QQQ at full weight. Each BTC-calendar-day reading becomes tradeable on the first QQQ trading session strictly after that day (a 1-session lag, conservatively safe given BTC's own UTC candle-close timing relative to the next NYSE open -- see the module's own 'No look-ahead' note).
source: Two independent, real, verified sources combine into this hypothesis (both verified via WebSearch/WebFetch 2026-09-17): (1) Bitcoin's correlation with the Nasdaq-100 has structurally increased since 2020 and strengthens specifically during risk-off/stress episodes -- CME Group's own 2025 research notes 'Bitcoin behaves much like a leveraged version of major stock market indices' and describes this correlation as 'alive and well (during risk-off)' (cmegroup.com/insights/economic-research/2025/why-is-bitcoin-moving-in-tandem-with-equities.html); BTC-Nasdaq-100 correlation reached roughly 0.87 during 2024's most correlated stretches versus near-zero 2014-2019. (2) Iyer, R. & Popescu, A. (2023), 'New Evidence on Spillovers Between Crypto Assets and Financial Markets', IMF Working Paper WP/2023/213, International Monetary Fund (elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/001/2023/213/article-A001-en.xml) -- finds crypto assets are a predominant NET TRANSMITTER of return/volatility spillovers to conventional financial markets, with spillover magnitude INCREASING during periods of heightened turbulence, and flags increased crypto-equity correlation during risk-off episodes as a genuine financial-stability transmission channel. Ticker verified: QQQ, Invesco, inception 1999. Data source verified real and free: Kraken public spot OHLC API (api.kraken.com/0/public/OHLC), no auth/key required; real fetched daily BTC-USD history measured 2026-09-17 spans 2024-09-28 through the fetch date (see the module's own 'Why spot, not funding rate' note for the real, measured ~720-row/~2-year ceiling on this endpoint, independent of the 'since' parameter beyond that lookback).
rule_pseudocode: SIGNAL: r_t = ln(Close_t/Close_{t-1}) on BTC-USD's own daily calendar; trailing_vol_t = std(ddof=1) of r_{t-20}..r_{t-1}, strictly before t (mining.batch5.bitcoin_extreme_decline_spillover_riskoff.btc_decline_zscore). REGIME: risk_off_t = OR of (z_s <= -2.0) for s in [t-4, t] calendar days (a 5-day causal rolling-max persistence, mining.batch5.bitcoin_extreme_decline_spillover_riskoff.btc_riskoff_regime); risk_on_t = NOT risk_off_t. AVAILABILITY: each BTC-calendar-day reading becomes tradeable on the first QQQ session strictly after that day (mining.signals.lag_boolean_regime_to_availability, lag_trading_days=1). DECISION: entry_t = risk_on known at QQQ session t; exit_t = NOT risk_on (mining.signals.make_external_regime_signal_fn) -- identical generic long/cash combinator every FRED-driven single_long family in this catalog already uses. BENCHMARK: SPY, not QQQ, per abi1_driver.evaluate_family's own documented contract (same convention as fed_net_liquidity_regime_qqq). DATA NOTE: Kraken's daily BTC-USD OHLC covers only 2024-09-28 onward (as of 2026-09-17, last still-forming candle dropped), while QQQ history starts 1999-03-10; the QQQ history before the BTC data begins carries no regime reading, disclosed not hidden.
distinctness_note: No other catalog family references crypto/bitcoin/BTC/Kraken. (1) single_day_extreme_decline_reversal_long triggers on SPY's OWN single-day z-score decline and enters a LONG dip-buy in SPY itself -- same asset triggers and is traded, same direction (buy). This family's trigger asset (BTC) and traded asset (QQQ) are different instruments in different asset classes, and a trigger is a temporary EXIT-TO-CASH, not a buy -- opposite polarity, genuinely cross-asset. (2) usd_strength_risk_regime uses a SLOW 200-day moving-average cross on a currency-strength proxy (UUP) to move SPY into SHY -- this family is an ASYMMETRIC-SPIKE/EVENT trigger (a single extreme day, not a slow MA cross) on a different asset class (crypto, not currency), defensive posture cash (not SHY), traded QQQ (not SPY). (3) fed_net_liquidity_regime / money_market_fund_flow_riskoff / margin_debt_growth_regime are all FRED/FINRA-sourced, slow-moving aggregate-liquidity or leverage TREND regimes (13-week MA of a weekly series; expanding-window z-score of a monthly series; trailing-12-month growth), each with a publication lag measured in weeks -- this family's trigger is a single extreme DAILY event in a real-time, 24/7-traded market with a 1-session lag, an entirely different data source. (4) margin_debt_deleverage_synthetic_leverage_flip flips between a synthetic 2x long and the inverse ETF SH on a monthly FINRA aggregate, never sitting in cash -- this family's defensive posture is cash, never a directional flip to an inverse position, and its trigger is a daily crypto-market price shock, not a monthly FINRA release. (5) vix_spike_reversal_equity_buy / vvix_vix_derisking_regime use an OPTIONS-IMPLIED volatility index (VIX/VVIX) of the SAME asset class being traded (US equities) as the trigger -- this family's trigger is a REALIZED price shock in a genuinely different asset class (crypto spot), testing a real, cited cross-asset spillover channel rather than 'equity options markets are pricing in more near-term risk'. None of the above can fire the way this family does: every equity-price or equity-implied-vol sibling is blind to a crypto-market event with no equity-index move of its own (yet), and every macro/FRED sibling is blind to intra-month, real-time crypto price action entirely.

name: Stock-Bond Rolling Return-Correlation Regime Flip (TLT signal -> SPY)
mechanism: Rolling 60-trading-day Pearson correlation of SPY's and TLT's own daily log returns (contemporaneous -- the reading for day t includes day t's own SPY/TLT returns, the academic literature's own realized-correlation convention). Campbell, J.Y., Pflueger, C. & Viceira, L.M. (2020), "Macroeconomic Drivers of Bond and Equity Risks", Journal of Political Economy 128(8), 3148-3185 (see also Cieslak, A. (2020), "Common Shocks in Stocks and Bonds", NBER Working Paper 28184) show the stock-bond correlation's sign depends on the covariance between inflation shocks and growth shocks: countercyclical inflation news produces the traditional NEGATIVE correlation (bonds hedge stocks, the classic 60/40 logic); procyclical, monetary-shock-driven inflation news produces POSITIVE correlation (bonds and stocks fall together, no hedge benefit) -- this model explains roughly 70% of long-run variation in the US stock-bond correlation. AQR, "A Changing Stock-Bond Correlation", documents the real 2022 episode: the SPX/AGG rolling correlation spiked to roughly +0.50, the highest in the modern sample, driven by the Fed's aggressive tightening cycle, equities and bonds falling together for the first time since 1977. Rule: hold SPY long while the rolling 60-day SPY/TLT return correlation is <= 0.30 (risk-on, the market's more typical negative-to-near-zero-correlation growth-shock regime); go flat to cash when the correlation exceeds 0.30 (risk-off, an unusually positive, monetary/inflation-shock-driven regime historically associated with a worse equity backdrop). Re-evaluated every trading day.
source: AQR, "A Changing Stock-Bond Correlation" (https://www.aqr.com/Insights/Research/Journal-Article/A-Changing-Stock-Bond-Correlation; verified via web search 2026-09-18) -- documents the real 2022 SPX/AGG rolling-correlation spike to roughly +0.50, the highest in the modern sample, driven by the Fed's tightening cycle. Campbell, J.Y., Pflueger, C. & Viceira, L.M. (2020), "Macroeconomic Drivers of Bond and Equity Risks", Journal of Political Economy 128(8), 3148-3185 -- shows the stock-bond correlation's sign depends on the covariance between inflation shocks and growth shocks, explaining roughly 70% of long-run variation in the US stock-bond correlation. Cieslak, A. (2020), "Common Shocks in Stocks and Bonds", NBER Working Paper 28184 -- independent corroboration of the same inflation/growth-shock sign-flip mechanism. Tickers verified: SPY, State Street, inception 1993-01-29; TLT, iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF, BlackRock, real fetched inception 2002-07-30 (data_pipeline.fetch_ohlc, verified 2026-09-18).
rule_pseudocode: DAILY. Common calendar = intersection of SPY's and TLT's own trading calendars (each instrument's own log return computed on its OWN calendar first, then intersected -- mining.batch5.stock_bond_correlation_regime_flip.spy_tlt_rolling_correlation). r_SPY_t = ln(Close_SPY_t/Close_SPY_{t-1}), r_TLT_t = ln(Close_TLT_t/Close_TLT_{t-1}). corr_t = trailing 60-common-calendar-day Pearson correlation of r_SPY and r_TLT, ending at and including t (pandas .rolling(60).corr()). Engine mapping (single_long SPY, SignalResult per bar): entry_t = (corr_t is defined) and (corr_t <= 0.30) -> fills at bar t+1's open; exit_t = (corr_t is defined) and (corr_t > 0.30) -> fills at bar t's own close. An undefined corr_t (fewer than 60 common-calendar return observations yet, or before TLT's own history begins) emits no signal -- the engine holds whatever position it already has. CALIBRATION: C=0.30 was set at the measured 95th percentile of the 60-day rolling SPY/TLT correlation over the available common history (data_pipeline.fetch_ohlc), so the rule is flat only in the most positively correlated regimes.
distinctness_note: No other family in this catalog computes a rolling CORRELATION between SPY's and TLT's own RETURNS. Nearest TLT-touching neighbors, verbatim mechanism text: yield_curve_slope_duration_rotation -- "Compute the daily price ratio TLT/SHY as a proxy for the Treasury yield-curve slope ... Take the ratio's 126-trading-day (6-month) rate of change." A TLT/SHY PRICE RATIO trend on the curve's slope, never a correlation, never touching SPY. credit_spread_hy_ig_risk_regime -- "Compute the daily price ratio HYG/LQD ... Take a 20-day and a 100-day simple moving average of this ratio." An HYG/LQD PRICE RATIO moving-average crossover on the credit spread, never touching TLT or a correlation. treasury_duration_volatility_timing -- "Compute TLT's trailing 20-day realized annualized volatility against its own trailing 252-day median." A SINGLE-INSTRUMENT realized-volatility regime on TLT alone, no SPY involvement. usd_strength_risk_regime -- "Track UUP's closing price against its own 200-day simple moving average." A currency TREND signal, never touching TLT or computing a correlation. cross_asset_time_series_momentum -- "Apply a trailing-return trend-following rule ... to non-equity-index ETFs -- Treasuries (TLT), gold (GLD), broad commodities (DBC)." Trailing-return MOMENTUM applied to TLT on its own (one sleeve leg), never a relationship with SPY. gold_long_treasury_relative_momentum_rotation -- "each month hold whichever of GLD ... or TLT ... had the higher trailing 12-month total return." A RELATIVE-MOMENTUM rotation between GLD and TLT (SPY is not even one of the two legs), comparing trailing return magnitude, not correlation. None of the above measures the actual statistical co-movement (a Pearson correlation coefficient) between equity and Treasury returns the way this family does.

name: Fair-Value-Gap Reversal Cascade Continuation (Day Trade)
mechanism: Each day, first derives today's directional bias from the last two completed daily bars (price_structure.daily_bias) -- only a bullish or bullish-continuation reading is tradeable, long-only scope, anything else skips the day. Once biased bullish, waits for the first fully-completed 60-minute bucket (anchored 09:30 ET) whose structure classification (price_structure.classify_reversal_bar) confirms the same bullish direction versus its own predecessor bucket -- same-direction structure on the hourly chart confirming the daily bias. Once confirmed, watches 5-minute buckets for a bullish fair-value gap (price_structure.fair_value_gaps) that formed at or after the hourly confirmation, dropping any gap a later 5-minute bar's low trades cleanly through without rejecting; entry triggers the instant the latest complete 5-minute bar's own low retests that gap's upper edge AND that same bar closes as a bullish reversal bar. The engine fills at the next bar's open; the stop is the trigger bar's own low and the target is the greater of a fixed R-multiple or the prior completed day's high minus the real fill price, so a fill that has already cleared yesterday's high still gets real room. Force-flattened by 15:55 ET regardless of stop/target status; one trade per day maximum.
source: Synthesized from three 2026 YouTube trading-education transcripts (TTrades Playbook: Fractal Model Fundamentals; 'Advanced MMXM Logic Continuations'; 'The GxT Universal Sequence') that independently teach the same underlying price-action framework under different vocabulary -- verified by direct cross-transcript quotes, not web search.
distinctness_note: Superficially similar to three bare liquidity-sweep/reclaim families: turtle_soup_failed_breakout (SPY, daily), intraday_liquidity_sweep_reversal (QQQ/SPY/IWM, swing), and turtle_soup_failed_breakout_reversal_daytrade (SPY/QQQ/IWM, day). This family adds three real filters those bare-sweep families lack: a two-day-derived directional bias gate (price_structure.daily_bias), a required same-direction hourly structure confirmation (price_structure.classify_reversal_bar) before any entry is even considered, and gating the entry to a specific 3-candle fair-value-gap zone (price_structure.fair_value_gaps) rather than any arbitrary reclaim level. Whether these filters produce a real edge beyond the bare sweeps is exactly what this trial tests -- it pays its own DSR trial rather than inheriting anything from the bare-sweep families.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general (applies to any liquid index ETF); QQQ/SPY/IWM chosen to match this catalog's existing day-trading universe.

name: Cross-Asset Divergence Fair-Value-Gap Continuation (Day Trade)
mechanism: Identical cascade to sibling family fvg_reversal_cascade_continuation_daytrade (daily bias -> hourly confirmation -> 5-minute fair-value-gap retest-and-reject, long-only) -- QQQ is the ONLY traded instrument here. One additional gate is inserted at the hourly-confirmation step: the primary's (QQQ's) own hourly confirmation is only ACCEPTED when SPY (the secondary, correlated instrument -- read-only reference data, never itself traded) FAILS to show the identical bullish structure at the identical hour, i.e. a genuine cross-asset divergence rather than a same-direction move both instruments happen to share; if both confirm together, QQQ's own confirmation is rejected and the cascade keeps waiting. If SPY's matching hourly bucket is not yet covered by its own data, the gate defaults permissive and QQQ's own confirmation is used on its own rather than blocking on missing data. Entry, fill, stop/target, and the 15:55 ET force-flat are otherwise identical to the sibling family.
source: Synthesized from three 2026 YouTube trading-education transcripts (TTrades Playbook: Fractal Model Fundamentals; 'Advanced MMXM Logic Continuations'; 'The GxT Universal Sequence') that independently teach the same underlying price-action framework under different vocabulary -- verified by direct cross-transcript quotes, not web search.
distinctness_note: Distinguished from sibling family fvg_reversal_cascade_continuation_daytrade by the added cross-asset divergence gate at the hourly-confirmation step -- a disclosed ETF proxy for the correlated-futures-pair concept the source transcripts describe, since this pipeline has no futures data plumbing; QQQ/SPY is used as the available correlated large-cap-index pair instead. Also distinguished from the three bare liquidity-sweep/reclaim families turtle_soup_failed_breakout (SPY, daily), intraday_liquidity_sweep_reversal (QQQ/SPY/IWM, swing), and turtle_soup_failed_breakout_reversal_daytrade (SPY/QQQ/IWM, day) -- none of which gate on any cross-asset divergence at all.
pooling_note: Not mechanism-general in the pooling sense -- QQQ/SPY is a specific, disclosed correlated pair; a different primary/secondary pairing would be a distinct hypothesis, not a pool member.

name: Green-Day Morning Pullback Continuation Scalp (Day Trade)
mechanism: Long-only intraday continuation scalp, pooled SPY/QQQ. Each session, tracks the running high since the open; once price has rallied at least min_rally_gain_pct off the session open, watches for a pause of at least min_consolidation_bars one-minute bars with no new high, retracing no more than max_pullback_retrace_pct of the rally leg -- confirmed only if that pause completes within the pullback_window_start_et..pullback_window_end_et morning window. Enters long the instant price closes back above the pre-pullback high (continuation breakout), stop at the pullback's own low, target min_target_r_multiple x initial risk. The setup is abandoned for the day (no trade) if price closes back below the session open at any point before entry, or if the pullback's own low is undercut before a breakout fires -- either invalidates the 'still a green day' premise the pattern depends on. Force-flattened by force_flat_et = 14:30 ET regardless of stop/target status -- a deliberately earlier cutoff than every sibling family in this catalog's day-trading track (which exit 15:55-15:59), chosen to get flat before afternoon profit-taking on strong-open days.
source: A common discretionary intraday pattern (a session that rallies from the open, pauses, then continues, with positions closed before 14:30 ET), formalized here as a mechanical entry/exit rule, plus the standard technical-analysis heuristic that a pullback retracing under half of the prior leg is read as a shallow, continuation-consistent pause rather than a reversal (the same class of generalized price-action convention this catalog's mining.price_structure primitives already document; no single external source is named for that heuristic).
distinctness_note: Distinct from sibling day-trading families fvg_reversal_cascade_continuation_daytrade / cross_asset_divergence_fvg_continuation_daytrade (those gate on a PRIOR day's daily_bias plus an hourly-structure/fair-value-gap retest; this family instead gates on the CURRENT day's own realized morning rally magnitude and a plain running high/low consolidation range -- no daily_bias, classify_reversal_bar, or fair_value_gaps machinery at all). Distinct from orb_5min_atr_stop_scalp (a fixed first-5-minutes opening-range breakout with no rally-magnitude or daily-trend gate). Distinct from intraday_half_hour_momentum_continuation (raw first/last half-hour momentum, no explicit pullback-and-breakout structure). Distinct from vwap_trend_intraday_scalp (trades confirmed VWAP crossovers directly, no rally-then-pause classification or fixed morning window). force_flat_et=14:30 is also a genuine parameter deviation, not a cosmetic one -- every other family in this catalog's day-trading track exits 15:55-15:59; this family exits roughly 90 minutes earlier by design.
pooling_note: Mechanism-general (applies to any liquid index ETF); SPY/QQQ chosen as this catalog's two most liquid, most-traded index ETFs.

name: IPO Long-Run Underperformance Fade (beta-neutral overlay)
mechanism: The BETA-NEUTRAL test of the same thesis as ipo_long_run_underperformance_fade (Ritter 1991: newly public companies underperform the broad market over the following one to three years, largely because issuers and underwriters time offerings to windows of investor over-optimism). Built because the naked-short framing is not a sound test: a never-exited short can lose more than its full notional, and ABI-1's daily excess over SPY, applied to a naked short of a market-correlated instrument, measures the account's negative market beta rather than IPO's relative underperformance. This family holds the benchmark itself (SPY, fully invested) PLUS a market-neutral overlay: short the Renaissance IPO ETF with notional equal to a fixed fraction of account equity, and an additional long SPY position sized to the IPO leg's trailing 252-session OLS beta to SPY (daily simple returns, estimated from data ending the session BEFORE it is applied). The hedge is re-estimated and the overlay re-opened on the first trading session of each calendar month, filled at that session's Open, with share counts held fixed between rebalances. Account excess over SPY is then the overlay alone, roughly x*(beta_hat*r_spy - r_ipo), with a residual SPY beta near zero, so ABI-1 scores IPO's behaviour relative to its own hedge rather than market direction. No overlay is opened until a full 252-session window of prior returns exists (until then the account is plain SPY and its excess is exactly zero).
source: Ritter, J.R. (1991), "The Long-Run Performance of Initial Public Offerings," Journal of Finance, 46(1), 3-27 -- the same primary source and instrument (Renaissance IPO ETF, inception October 14, 2013) as ipo_long_run_underperformance_fade. The beta-neutral benchmark-plus-overlay design is this pipeline's own design choice, not a literature citation; derivation, fixed constants and accounting conventions are in src/mining/beta_neutral_overlay.py. The overlay notional (0.25 of equity) is chosen for Reg-T feasibility up to a hedge ratio of 3; the score is NOT invariant to it (ABI-1 scores the log excess, whose curvature term penalizes a larger overlay, more so on more volatile return series), so a larger notional is the conservative direction. NOT MODELLED, and each of these flatters the strategy: short-borrow fees, margin financing of the net long, wash-sale disallowance (short-rebate interest is income, so omitting it is conservative) -- the pipeline has no margin-rate or borrow-fee source, and its T-bill series is only a lower bound on financing cost that was deliberately not charged by design, so any apparent survivor needs a cost-sensitivity re-check. LIMITATION: the hedge neutralizes SPY beta only -- the IPO ETF's size/growth/momentum tilts versus the S&P 500 stay unhedged, so an apparent edge could be a style premium rather than an IPO-specific effect. Taxable account only: a short position needs a margin account.
distinctness_note: A different strategy DEFINITION from ipo_long_run_underperformance_fade (a naked short of the IPO ETF that ABI-1 cannot score meaningfully), not a re-score of it, so it pays its own trial under its own family_id -- the same convention money_market_fund_flow_riskoff_bounded_burnin and fed_net_liquidity_regime_qqq followed. Reachable only through scripts/run_ipo_fade_beta_neutral_abi1.py: make_signal_fn always raises so the generic dispatch cannot mis-score it.

name: Short-Rate Easing Small-Cap Rotation (IWM / SPY)
mechanism: Hold the broad market (SPY) by default and rotate the whole account into small caps (IWM) while monetary policy is easing, measured by the 3-month Treasury bill rate (^IRX close, in percentage points) sitting at least 0.10 percentage points BELOW its own trailing 252-session mean. Decision at each month-end m (the last trading session of the month, taken from the exchange's schedule fixed in advance -- weekends, Good Friday and Memorial Day stepped over -- never inferred from a later data row): rtb = irx_close[m] - mean(irx_close over the 252 sessions ending at m, m included); easing = (rtb <= -0.10); target = IWM if easing else SPY. The rotation engine executes the target at the NEXT session's open (decision on bar t, fill at the t+1 open), so a switch lands on the first session of the following month. Differences only, never ratios or logs, because the bill rate is not strictly positive (7 sessions closed at or below zero in March 2020) and the signal frame is loaded without the positivity gate meant for traded prices. The account is always invested (never in cash), so it does not carry the cash-drag handicap of a flat/cash rotation; ABI-1 always benchmarks SPY, so, apart from per-switch execution costs and the few sessions before the first reading, the pre-tax scored excess is the IWM-minus-SPY return earned during easing months and zero in every other month (the first listed account type is taxable, so ABI-1 additionally taxes the account's realized gains but never the SPY benchmark). Both constants (252 sessions, -0.10) were fixed before any P&L existed for this family and must not be tuned after any backtest result.
source: Thorbecke, W. (1997), "On Stock Market Returns and Monetary Policy," Journal of Finance, 52(2), 635-654 (bibliographic details and the abstract-level finding that expansionary policy raises ex-post stock returns verified 2026-09-23; the finer claim that SMALL stocks respond more comes from a secondary summary and was NOT confirmed against the paper's own text). Perez-Quiros, G. and Timmermann, A. (2000), "Firm Size and Cyclical Variations in Stock Returns," Journal of Finance, 55(3), 1229-1262 (bibliographic details verified 2026-09-23; abstract-level finding that small firms show the highest asymmetry across recession and expansion states and a higher sensitivity of expected returns to credit-market-condition variables). Ang, A. and Bekaert, G. (2007), "Stock Return Predictability: Is It There?," Review of Financial Studies, 20(3), 651-707 (bibliographic details verified 2026-09-23; abstract-level finding that the short rate is the only robust short-run predictor of equity returns in their sample -- an AGGREGATE-market result, not a size differential). Fixed-window detrending of the short rate (the relative bill rate) follows the Campbell (1991), "A Variance Decomposition for Stock Returns," Economic Journal, 101(405), 157-179 and Hodrick (1992), Review of Financial Studies (volume and pages not re-verified) tradition; that a detrended risk-free rate carries forecasting power for stock returns was confirmed ONLY via a secondary source, and the exact detrending window those papers use was NOT verified against them (UNVERIFIED). HONEST LIMITS: the literature supports a policy-easing to equity-returns link and a small-firm sensitivity, but none of these papers tests THIS rule (a monthly IWM-versus-SPY rotation on a fixed-window detrended bill rate); the 252-session window and the -0.10 threshold are this pipeline's own pre-registered constants, not literature values. Data: ^IRX history from 1960-01-04 (verified by fetch 2026-09-23), fully warmed long before IWM's first vendor-history row of 2000-05-26; SPY is the standing ABI-1 benchmark.
distinctness_note: Selects between small-cap and large-cap US equity from the LEVEL of the short rate relative to its own trailing year (a monetary-easing proxy); defensive_sector_recession_signal_rotation is also ^IRX-based (that is the overlap) but uses the 10y-minus-3m yield-curve SLOPE to choose XLU versus SPY, and small_cap_tsmom_long_inverse_rotation / vol_managed_smallcap_leverage_switch key on price or volatility, not monetary policy. ABI-1 scores each family at the fixed ABI1_N_TRIALS with no pairwise-correlation correction between families (verified in src/mining/constants.py and abi1_driver.evaluate_family), so the ^IRX overlap is disclosed, not corrected; size_premium_smallcap holds small caps against the same SPY benchmark all the time, and this family is that bet switched on only in easing regimes. Disclosed limits: easing regimes are few (a handful of easing cycles since 2000), so statistical power is very low; the bill rate fell through the 2001-2002 and 2008 bear markets, so the rotation holds IWM THROUGH both -- a size-times-policy bet with no crash protection.

name: Treasury and Aggregate-Bond Month-End Index-Demand Overlay (SPY core, long IEF/TLT/AGG over the last 3 scheduled sessions)
mechanism: Fixed-income benchmark indices (the Bloomberg US Aggregate among them) rebalance on the last business day of each month, and life insurers and passive bond funds are large net buyers of Treasuries around those benchmark-rebalance dates: a temporary, predictable demand shock in the last few sessions of the month. Hartley and Schwarz find positive, highly significant excess returns on coupon Treasuries only in the last few days of the month (largest over the last 3 to 5 days, rising with maturity, about 0.25 percent for the 10-year over the last 3 days), roughly zero on all other days, with an annualized Sharpe near 1, positive in every 5-year block from 1990 to 2018 and no structural break, and attribute it to window dressing and index-rebalancing demand rather than crash risk. The New York Fed's September 2024 note finds Treasury volume about 46 percent higher and price impact about 28 percent lower on the last trading day of the month since 2020 and conjectures that passive Treasury-ETF rebalancing drives it. Expression: because ABI-1 scores the account's daily excess over SPY buy-and-hold, a bond fund held IN PLACE of SPY would score about minus SPY on the swap days, so the premium is isolated only by holding SPY as the core at all times and adding, for the last 3 scheduled NYSE sessions of each month only (entry at the close of the session before the window, T-3; exit at the close of the month's last scheduled session, T), a margin-financed LONG-ONLY overlay in IEF, TLT and AGG (equal thirds, total notional 0.5 of account equity, one pooled trial) funded by borrowing at the ^IRX bill rate with no spread charged. The month-end dates come from the exchange's regular-holiday schedule fixed in advance (unscheduled closures are not removed), never from the data. Costs are a full round trip per ETF per month from a real quote sample. No hedge leg and no short leg.

parameters.core: SPY fully invested at all times (the benchmark series itself)
parameters.entry: close of the last scheduled session before the window (T-3)
parameters.exit: close of the last scheduled session of the calendar month (T)
parameters.calendar: exchange_calendars XNYS scheduled sessions: weekdays minus regular holidays; unscheduled closures are not removed
parameters.financing_rate: ^IRX 13-week bill coupon-equivalent yield of the last close strictly before each session, on the borrowed overlay notional, actual calendar days over 365, no spread

source: Hartley, J. and Schwarz, K. (2019), "Predictable End-of-Month Treasury Returns", SSRN 3440417 (working paper dated 22 Nov 2019; journal publication status UNVERIFIED). The paper's own returns are built from an off-the-run zero-coupon curve, not ETF total returns. Supporting: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Liberty Street Economics, "End-of-Month Liquidity in the Treasury Market" (September 2024), fetched. Bloomberg US Aggregate Index factsheet dated 12 Jun 2024 ("Rebalance Date: The last business day of each month"), text extracted. Third-party ETF replication, UNVERIFIED against its source data: Allocate Smartly, "Predictable End-of-Month Treasury ETF Returns", which reports the positive bias migrating earlier from about 2014 (front-running). IEF and TLT (inception July 2002) and AGG (inception September 2003) are ordinary 1099 funds, not K-1 pools. HONEST LIMITS: none of the sources tests THIS rule; the 3-session window, the 0.5 notional (chosen for Reg-T slack; the score is not invariant to it because ABI-1 scores the LOG excess) and the bill-rate financing rule are this pipeline's own pre-registered choices, fixed before this pipeline computed any return of this account and never to be tuned after a score. NOT ALL WERE CHOSEN BLIND: before the constants were fixed, descriptive overlay statistics on these same three ETFs (in-sample data only; the holdout was not looked at) were examined, covering the window length, the close-fill entry against the engine's next-open fill, and the rotation expression against the overlay expression. The 3-session window (the paper's headline example), the T-3 close entry, the overlay expression and the choice of the three ETFs were fixed after those looks; the 0.5 notional, the bare bill-rate financing and the calendar rule were chosen without any look at their effect. Those looks ran outside the trial ledger, so DSR's trial count does not charge them and a DSR pass must be read with them in mind. A real margin rate adds a spread over the bill rate that is NOT modelled and this flatters the strategy; taxable account only because the overlay is borrowed; RISK LAYER (the risk-basis rule): ABI-1's four risk refusals (the 0.35 absolute drawdown cap, drawdown no worse than SPY's, longest losing-week streak no longer than SPY's, worst 8-week stretch no worse than SPY's) are measured on the overlay-only excess account, the account's daily arithmetic excess over SPY in units of whole-account equity, not on the whole SPY-core account, which holds SPY through 2008, where SPY's own drawdown alone is about 55 percent, so the whole account clears the 0.35 cap only if the overlay offsets most of it; the three SPY-relative refusals compare the overlay's own excess with SPY itself and, for a small overlay measured over a window that holds a large SPY drawdown, are expected to be much less binding than on the whole account, so the risk layer here is mainly the absolute cap on the overlay's own drawdown. Data: yfinance daily adjusted OHLC for IEF, TLT, AGG, SPY and ^IRX; ex-ante NYSE schedule from exchange_calendars XNYS (regular holidays only).
distinctness_note: Unconditional long bond ETFs into the benchmark-index rebalance date, held as a financed overlay on an SPY core, scored through its own bespoke driver (scripts/run_treasury_month_end_overlay_abi1.py; make_signal_fn always raises so the generic dispatch cannot mis-score it). Nearest catalog families: month_end_rebalancing_flow_rotation shares the last-sessions-of-the-month zone and a flow story but trades SPY versus SH conditional on a 60/40 equity-side weight-deviation signal (pension rebalancing), not bonds unconditionally, and is a rotation not an overlay; long_treasury_auction_cycle_3x_inverse_rotation is a dealer risk-bearing effect around 30-year auction dates expressed in 3x products and cash, while Hartley and Schwarz show the month-end premium survives controlling for the auction cycle (partial calendar overlap exists because 2-, 5- and 7-year notes settle at month-end); long_treasury_3x_fomc_window_drift is tied to the FOMC calendar (about 8 windows a year) rather than the monthly index-rebalance date (about 12). Not the excluded equity turn_of_month on mechanism: bond-side and driven by index demand. But that family was excluded for economic immateriality (its own catalog reason: a real effect too small to be worth trading, not a mechanism failure), and this overlay faces a related question: if the paper's roughly quarter-percent gross move per window carried over to these ETFs, a half-notional overlay would earn roughly an eighth of a percent of equity per window before financing, costs and tax. It is still worth one permanent trial because ABI-1 scores the risk-adjusted daily excess over SPY, which does not depend on account size, the bond-side index-demand mechanism is a different one, and the record settles whether the effect is statistically detectable at all; any DSR pass would still need its own materiality review before real capital is committed.

name: Bond-Equity Divergence of Fear Gauges: MOVE vs VIX De-Risk Rotation (SPY / SHY)
mechanism: Hold the broad market (SPY) by default and rotate the whole account into short-term Treasuries (SHY) for the following week whenever bond-market implied volatility (^MOVE) is unusually high RELATIVE to equity-market implied volatility (^VIX) -- the divergence of the two fear gauges. Standardize each index with an EXPANDING z-score whose mean and sample standard deviation (ddof 1) are taken over the observations STRICTLY BEFORE the date (at least 756 prior observations, counted over the sessions on which both indices print, so both indices are standardized over the same sample): zMOVE_t = (MOVE_t - mean(MOVE before t)) / std(MOVE before t), likewise zVIX_t. DFG_t = (zMOVE_t - zVIX_t) / sqrt(2), which for two standardized, positively correlated series is exactly their second principal component (the construction Ruan and Wei use; the sign here is chosen so a HIGH value means bond-market fear relative to equity-market fear). Weekly decision at each scheduled decision date F -- the Friday close, or the last scheduled session of the week when Friday is a scheduled exchange holiday. That schedule is the exchange's published holiday rules, fixed in advance and read from no data file, so no later observation, not even the existence of a later session, can decide which day is the decision day. S_F = the mean of the last 10 DFG observations ending at F (F's own print included); derisk = (S_F > 0.5), strict; target = SHY if derisk else SPY. A decision date on which either index has no print (a vendor hole, or a bond-market-only holiday such as Veterans Day) has NO reading: the previous regime carries through that week, and the code never falls back to an earlier day, which would need foreknowledge. The rotation engine executes the target at the NEXT session's open (decision on bar t, fill at the t+1 open), so a reading dated Friday is held from the next session. Before the first defined reading (the first 756 observations after the ^MOVE inception of 2002-11-12 plus the 9 further observations the 10-observation mean needs, i.e. until the first Friday reading on 2005-12-16) the account holds the default, SPY, following the rule's 'otherwise hold SPY', rather than sitting in cash for three years. All three constants (756, 10, 0.5) were fixed a priori -- the 10-observation smoothing and the +0.5 threshold from switch-count and time-in-market feasibility, with no returns examined -- and must not be tuned after any backtest result. The paper's specification is a regression forecast, not a trading rule, and no threshold rule was published, so the weekly holding period, the smoothing and the threshold are this pipeline's own assumptions.
source: Ruan, X. and Wei, X., 'Divergence of Fear Gauges and Stock Returns' (SSRN 5001821, sample 2004-2022); a published version appears as 'When fears diverge: Bond-equity relative uncertainty and stock market returns' (ScienceDirect PII S1057521926002188). Verified ONLY through search-result summaries (the abstract pages returned HTTP 403 when fetched): the divergence is the second principal component of standardized MOVE and VIX, it negatively predicts subsequent stock returns, and the stated channel is a reallocation of flows between bonds and stocks that puts price pressure on stocks now and compresses the subsequent equity risk premium. UNVERIFIED: the author order and journal name of the published version, the predictive horizon, the R-squared, and the paper's exact sign convention. HONEST LIMITS: the paper is a regression forecast, not a trading rule, and is one new paper, not replicated; the weekly holding period, the 10-observation smoothing and the 0.5 threshold are this pipeline's own pre-registered constants, not literature values; the paper's whole 2004-2022 sample lies inside this test window. Data: yfinance ^MOVE (history from 2002-11-12), ^VIX, SPY and SHY (all verified by fetch 2026-09-23); both volatility indices are never-revised index levels, so there is no vintage risk.
distinctness_note: The first family in this catalog to read the Treasury-market implied volatility index ^MOVE, and the only one built on the RELATIVE reading of bond-market versus equity-market implied volatility (a cross-asset relative-uncertainty signal with a reallocation-flow rationale). Nearest neighbours: vvix_vix_derisking_regime compares two EQUITY-option volatility indices; vxn_vix_spread_derisking_regime is an intra-equity spread (Nasdaq-100 versus S&P 500 implied volatility) read through a moving-average cross of a ratio, whereas this family crosses asset classes and uses expanding standardization with no moving-average crossover; skew_index_tail_risk_regime reads S&P put-skew demand and contains no bond-market information; stock_bond_correlation_regime_flip uses REALIZED SPY/TLT return correlation, not implied volatility. Two sibling variants of the same idea (a trailing-252-session standardization, and a leverage-overlay version) are treated as duplicates of this one and are not catalogued; this is the single specification. Disclosed limits: a weekly state on two slow-moving volatility indices changes in clusters, so the number of independent episodes, and with it statistical power, is far lower than the weekly decision count suggests, and the paper's whole 2004-2022 sample lies inside this window; ABI-1 taxes the account's realized gains and never the SPY benchmark; ^MOVE has no print on some scheduled decision dates (bond-market-only holidays among them), each of which carries the previous regime one week, and SPY sessions missing from either signal frame drop out of the account because the driver intersects the signal frames onto the traded calendar; ABI-1 scores every family at the fixed trial count with no pairwise correlation correction, so the overlap with the other implied-volatility de-risk families is disclosed, not corrected. When the vendor has no row for SHY, ^VIX or ^MOVE on a session, the ABI-1 driver's two-traded-leg calendar check refuses this (and any) SPY/SHY rotation until the vendor fills it.
rule_pseudocode: WEEKLY, decided at the decision date's close, filled at the next session's open by mining.rotation_engine. common = the sessions on which BOTH ^MOVE and ^VIX print (the signal's own calendar, intersected with no traded calendar). For each index x on common: for observation t with at least 756 prior observations, z_t = (x_t - mean(x[:t])) / std(x[:t], ddof=1) (statistics over observations strictly before t; NaN when the standard deviation is zero). DFG_t = (z_MOVE_t - z_VIX_t) / sqrt(2). S_t = mean of the last 10 DFG observations ending at t (undefined until 10 are defined). Decision dates = scheduled_decision_dates: one per ISO week, the Friday or, if the exchange schedules Friday closed (Good Friday, and New Year's Day / Independence Day / Christmas / Juneteenth on or observed on a Friday), the last scheduled session before it -- a closed-form function of the calendar, no data file. A decision date has a reading only if it is present in common and S is defined there; derisk = S > 0.5 (strict). State series = the reading at each such decision date, carried forward over every session until the next reading (through weeks with no reading); before the first reading the state is the default, SPY. target = SHY if derisk else SPY, via signals.make_external_regime_target_fn.

name: Cross-Asset Financial Turbulence (Mahalanobis Distance) De-risk Trigger (SPY vs SHY)
mechanism: Hold the broad market (SPY) by default and rotate the whole account into short Treasuries (SHY) for the following week when a multivariate financial-turbulence reading across five liquid asset classes ranks in the top fifth of its own history. Financial turbulence (Kritzman and Li 2010) is the Mahalanobis distance of one day's returns across stocks (SPY), emerging markets (EEM), long Treasuries (TLT), gold (GLD) and investment-grade credit (LQD) from their historical mean and covariance: d_t = (r_t - mean)' inv(cov) (r_t - mean), with r_t the daily log returns and mean and cov the EXPANDING sample statistics (ddof 1) over the sessions strictly BEFORE t (at least 500 earlier sessions; never regularized -- a singular or ill-conditioned covariance raises an error). It flags days when prices move unusually far AND days when assets break their usual correlations (stocks and bonds falling together, gold failing to hedge), which a volatility reading on one asset misses. m_t is the trailing 10-session mean of d_t. At each SCHEDULED last session of the week (Friday, or Thursday when the exchange calendar shuts that Friday; fixed in advance from the calendar, never inferred from a later data row), pct is the share of the strictly earlier m values that are strictly below m_t (at least 250 earlier values are needed); target = SHY if pct is above 0.80, otherwise SPY. The rotation engine executes the target at the NEXT session's open, so a reading dated at a Friday is held from the following Monday. Before the first defined reading (about three years: 500 + 9 + 250 panel sessions after GLD's 2004-11-18 inception) the account holds SPY, the default holding, so the warm-up carries no cash-drag handicap and no signal is being traded there. All constants were fixed a priori (the 10-session window and the 0.80 percentile from switch-count and time-in-market feasibility with no returns examined; the 500 and 250 session minimums as specified) and must not be tuned after any backtest result.
source: Kritzman, M. and Li, Y. (2010), "Skulls, Financial Turbulence, and Risk Management," Financial Analysts Journal, 66(5), 30-41 (verified by search: Taylor & Francis, SSRN and secondary summaries; the paper's use of turbulence as an exposure-scaling filter is confirmed). UNVERIFIED: any specific claim about the size of post-turbulence drawdowns or the paper's own filter threshold. HONEST LIMITS: the paper publishes a filtering concept, not a trading rule; one reading of the PDF is that its only scaling test is on a G10 currency carry strategy, not equities, so the SPY-to-SHY use, the weekly Friday decision, the 10-session smoothing, the 0.80 percentile and the 500/250-session minimums are this pipeline's own pre-registered constants, not literature values. Data: yfinance dividend-adjusted daily closes for SPY, SHY, EEM (from 2003-04), TLT and LQD (from 2002-07) and GLD (from 2004-11-18, which binds the five-asset panel start); first weekly reading 2007-11-30 (real fetch 2026-09-23).
distinctness_note: Distinct statistic, crowded shape class. A covariance-aware Mahalanobis distance over five asset classes (stocks, emerging markets, long Treasuries, gold, investment-grade credit) that responds to both magnitude and correlation-structure violations; no other catalog family uses turbulence / Mahalanobis / Kritzman. Nearest: stock_bond_correlation_regime_flip reads one pairwise rolling SPY/TLT correlation against a fixed threshold; vol_managed_sector_spdr_pooled (and the other vol_managed_* families) switch each instrument on its own trailing realized variance, whereas turbulence is one joint measure so a day of moderate moves in the wrong combination flags even when no single asset's volatility is extreme; sector_dispersion_regime_cyclical_stance measures cross-sectional dispersion across nine equity sectors and sets a cyclical stance, whereas this spans stocks, bonds, credit, gold and emerging markets and de-risks to short Treasuries. It still sits in the realized-risk de-risk neighbourhood that several sibling families already cover, so it is a low-prior probe. Disclosed limits: the account holds SPY (the default holding) until the first reading, 2007-11-30, about three years in.
directional_rationale: Volatility and correlation clustering is one of the most durable regularities in asset returns, and correlation breakdowns are typical of leveraged-position unwinds that last days to weeks; weekly evaluation and expanding percentile bounds keep the cost of being wrong low. RISKS: it is closest in spirit to volatility-regime timing, which several sibling families already cover; the distance reacts after a shock has hit, so it can sit in SHY during V-shaped rebounds; the state changes cluster into a small number of independent stress episodes; expanding-history percentile thresholds make early-sample readings noisy; the five-ETF panel is a judgment call and any change to it is a new trial; Kritzman and Li publish a filtering concept, not a trading rule.
rule_pseudocode: WEEKLY, decided at the scheduled last session of each Monday-to-Friday week (the Friday, stepping back to Thursday over Good Friday or an exchange-observed Friday holiday; never derived from the data; a scheduled week end missing from the data gets no reading). Panel = SPY, EEM, TLT, GLD, LQD daily log returns on sessions where all five have a one-session return (a missing print drops that session and the next; a date missing from every asset is a closure). d_t = (r_t - mean_{t-1})' inv(cov_{t-1}) (r_t - mean_{t-1}) where mean_{t-1} and cov_{t-1} are the expanding sample mean and covariance (ddof 1) of the returns before t, defined once 500 earlier sessions exist; a covariance that is not positive definite or whose eigenvalue ratio exceeds 1e8 (ten to the eighth power, parameter max_covariance_condition_number_exponent = 8) raises ValueError (no ridge, no shrinkage). m_t = mean of d over the last 10 panel sessions. At a week end w: pct = (number of strictly earlier m values strictly below m_w) / (number of strictly earlier finite m values), defined once 250 earlier m values exist; defensive = (pct > 0.80); target = SHY if defensive else SPY. Engine mapping (rotation_two_asset via mining.rotation_engine.run_two_asset_rotation): the target read on decision bar t executes at bar t+1's open. Before the first reading the account holds SPY.

name: Commodity Futures Open-Interest Growth Cycle -> Commodity-versus-Treasury Overlay (SPY core, long DBC when HIGH or long TLT when LOW)
mechanism: Hedgers' response to news about future economic activity shows up as changes in the AMOUNT of futures contracts outstanding before it is fully in prices, because risk-absorbing capital is limited and other investors underreact. Rising commodity open interest signals stronger activity and rising inflation expectations: good for commodity returns, bad for bonds (Hong and Yogo report that a one standard deviation rise cuts expected bond returns by 0.32 percent per month). Expression: SPY is held at all times (the benchmark series itself) PLUS a margin-financed LONG-ONLY overlay of 0.25 of account equity in ONE leg chosen by the state, DBC when the state is HIGH and TLT when it is LOW (one pooled trial, no hedge leg, no short leg). Signal: per contract, the monthly log growth of CFTC Legacy Futures-Only open interest (contract counts) at each scheduled month-end, taken from the last report usable by then (a report as of Tuesday D is usable from D+6 calendar days), averaged within each of four sectors (agriculture, energy, livestock, metals), the sectors equal-weighted, CMI = the mean of the last 12 monthly aggregate values; the state is HIGH when CMI is strictly above the expanding median of CMI (current month included, minimum 36 monthly observations), else LOW. The state is fixed at the close of each scheduled month-end session and the leg held to the next. The scored convention is MONTHLY-RESIZED (one switch): every calendar month is its own window, so each month re-sizes the overlay to 0.25 of equity and pays a full round trip even when the leg continues; merging consecutive same-leg months into one window (one round trip) is a report-only merged sensitivity computed beside the scored result. The month-end dates come from the exchange's regular-holiday schedule fixed in advance, never from the data.

parameters.core: SPY fully invested at all times (the benchmark series itself)
parameters.data: CFTC Legacy Futures-Only open_interest_all (Socrata dataset 6dca-aqww), contract COUNTS not dollar open interest
parameters.publication_blackouts: month-ends inside the 2013, 2018-19 and 2025-26 publication blackouts carry the prior state and are left out of the median; delayed reports count as available only from their conservative public-by date
parameters.monthly_growth: per contract ln(OI_m / OI_(m-1)) of the last available report at each scheduled month-end; contracts without a value are left out
parameters.aggregation: mean within each sector, then the equal-weight mean of the sectors that have a value
parameters.state_rule: HIGH when CMI is strictly above the expanding median of evaluated CMI including the current month, else LOW
parameters.decision: state fixed at the close of each scheduled month-end session T(m), held for the following month
parameters.merge: scored convention: every calendar month is its own window, so each month re-sizes the overlay to 0.25 of equity and pays a full round trip even when the leg continues; merging consecutive same-leg months into one window (one round trip, fixed share count) is a report-only sensitivity
parameters.entry: close of T(m) for every month
parameters.exit: close of T(m+1), the next scheduled month-end session
parameters.calendar: exchange_calendars XNYS scheduled sessions: weekdays minus regular holidays; unscheduled closures are not removed
parameters.financing_rate: ^IRX 13-week bill coupon-equivalent yield of the last close strictly before each session, on the borrowed overlay notional, actual calendar days over 365, no margin spread
parameters.control_arm: report-only always-TLT 0.25x overlay, same costs and financing, merged and monthly-resized variants

source: Hong, H. and Yogo, M. (2012), "What does futures market interest tell us about the macroeconomy and asset prices?", Journal of Financial Economics 105(3):473-490 (1965-2008 sample, monthly; NBER working paper 16712; the paper reports that commodity market interest predicts commodity returns and that a one standard deviation rise cuts expected bond returns by 0.32 percent per month, with no out-of-sample test). Context on why the post-2008 sample is a genuine out-of-sample and a possible regime break: Tang, K. and Xiong, W. (2012), Financial Analysts Journal 68(6):54-74 (not independently checked). FIVE DEVIATIONS FROM THE PAPER, all pre-declared, so the citation supports the idea and the two signs but NOT this exact rule: contract counts, not dollar open interest (dollar open interest is spot price times quantity and would mostly re-encode commodity price momentum, which other catalog families already cover); contract-level growth averaged within each sector, then the sectors equal-weighted and averaged arithmetically over 12 months, not the paper's aggregate-then-growth with a geometric average; 18 contracts in four sectors, not about 30 commodities; a median split, not a regression on the continuous variable; TLT (a 20-plus-year fund), not the 10-year note. This is one pooled trial and no parameter may be tuned after seeing a result. POINT-IN-TIME STATUS: the CFTC series is NOT verified never-revised; documented corrections exist (the reports as of 2017-03-28, 2018-09-18 and 2019-10-15) and the Socrata dataset serves the corrected values, not as first published; it is never labelled never-revised. The fixed D+6 availability lag is false in the three CFTC publication blackouts (the 2013, 2018-19 and 2025-26 federal shutdowns); at each publication blackout month-end (2013-10-31, 2018-12-31, 2019-01-31, 2019-02-28, 2025-10-31, 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-31 in the history) the family refuses to update its state and carries the prior state, leaves that month out of the median and reads the last report that was really public; the 2025-26 blackout falls inside the ABI-1 holdout. The 2018-19 blackout starts with the Christmas-shifted report as of Monday 2018-12-24 (CFTC press release 7864-19), so 2019-02-28 is a blackout month-end too; the 2025-26 table keeps the CFTC's first plan's outer bound although its accelerated plan cleared the backlog on 2025-12-29, so 2025-12-31 is carried though its report was already public (conservative). A CMI whose 12-month base month is a blackout month-end measures a window longer than 12 months (2014-10-31, 2019-12-31, 2020-01-31 and 2020-02-28); disclosed, not repaired. TIE MONTH: at 2019-11-29 CMI equals its expanding median exactly and the pre-registered strict rule resolves that EXACT TIE to LOW. The D+6 lag has three days of margin in a normal week and none in a holiday-shifted week. Five scored month-end decisions (2009-11-30, 2011-02-28, 2015-11-30, 2020-11-30 and 2022-02-28) read a report from a US-federal-holiday week whose plain D+6 date falls on the decision day itself; the CFTC usually moves such a release to the Monday afternoon, about 30 minutes before the close on the decision day (not verified against a CFTC notice). COMPOSITION DRIFT of the expanding-median baseline: grains start 1998, lean hogs 1996, natural gas 1990, copper 1989 and RBOB 2006, so the early CMI is built from fewer contracts. On the CFTC counts: 241 of the 476 CMI values (50.6 percent) have a 12-month window in which fewer than 18 contracts carry a growth value (all 18 carry one from 2006-03-31 and 12 of the 247 evaluation months since 2006-02 are still partial), and palladium has real reporting gaps of 84, 168 and 259 days in 2000-2002 (a stale value is carried for up to 247 days). When the state is mostly LOW for long stretches the account is close to a static long-TLT overlay, so the effective sample is small. SIXTH DISCLOSED LIMITATION (a limitation, not a deviation from the paper, so the deviations stay FIVE): the 18-contract universe is a present-day survivor set, the contracts that exist and report cleanly today, with no membership rule applied at each historical date, so a contract that stopped trading before 2026 cannot be in it. HONEST LIMITS (each of the first two flatters the strategy): no margin spread over the bill rate is modelled (financing is the bare ^IRX bill rate; a real margin rate adds a spread); DBC is energy-heavy while the signal is equal-weight across four sectors; Reg-T margin calls and borrow availability are not modelled; the merge convention (a report-only merged sensitivity, NOT the scored one) keeps a fixed share count inside a merged window, so its notional drifts from 0.25 of equity, and it also flatters the strategy through the tax walk: this pipeline's realization tax walk charges the short-term rate on a round trip held 365 days or less and a zero long-term rate on one held longer, so a merged window held beyond a year realizes its gain untaxed; the scored convention is therefore MONTHLY-RESIZED (one switch: every calendar month is its own window with a full round trip and a re-size to 0.25 of equity, short-term taxed, conservative on cost; no window held beyond a year) and the merged sensitivity is computed beside it; taxable account only because the overlay is borrowed. CONTROL ARM (report-only, no ledger row): an always-TLT 0.25x overlay with the same costs and financing is computed beside the result, merged and re-sized monthly, and a pass is only meaningful if the strategy beats it. RISK LAYER (the risk-basis rule): ABI-1's four risk refusals (the 0.35 absolute drawdown cap, drawdown no worse than SPY's, longest losing-week streak no longer than SPY's, worst 8-week stretch no worse than SPY's) are measured on the overlay-only excess account, the account's daily arithmetic excess over SPY in units of whole-account equity, not on the whole SPY-core account. Data: yfinance daily adjusted OHLC for DBC, TLT, SPY and ^IRX (DBC lists 2006-02-06); CFTC Legacy Futures-Only open_interest_all from the CFTC public reporting Socrata dataset 6dca-aqww; ex-ante NYSE schedule from exchange_calendars XNYS (regular holidays only).
distinctness_note: No other catalog family uses futures positioning or open-interest data at all (no other catalog row or source module refers to open interest, CFTC, hedging pressure or Commitments of Traders). The trend-following neighbours use price momentum of DBC, TLT and GLD (cross_asset_time_series_momentum); this signal uses the QUANTITY of contracts outstanding, deliberately not dollar-weighted so it does not re-encode price trend, and it drives a two-leg commodity-versus-duration overlay on an SPY core rather than a single-asset trend switch. commodity_currency_leadlag trades an AUD fund from DBC's return; crude_oil_term_structure_roll_carry uses the curve slope of one commodity; commodity_backwardation_momentum_selection uses a term-structure ranking.
